#!/bin/bash
# Tests for worktree-guard.sh. Run: bash .claude/hooks/worktree-guard.test.sh
here=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
H="$here/worktree-guard.sh"
# Paths are built at run time: a main checkout the guard must derive from git, never a machine path.
TMP=$(cd "$(mktemp -d)" && pwd -P); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
MAIN=$TMP/elsewhere/paddock-main
git init -q "$MAIN" || exit 1
WT=$TMP/dev-targets/wt/some-agent
export CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR=$MAIN
unset WORKTREE_GUARD_MAIN
fail=0
# who: agent|coord
run() { # who cwd command
  if [ "$1" = agent ]; then extra='{"agent_id":"a1","agent_type":"implementer"}'; else extra='{}'; fi
  jq -nc --arg c "$3" --arg d "$2" --argjson x "$extra" '{tool_name:"Bash",cwd:$d,tool_input:{command:$c}} + $x' | "$H" 2>/dev/null
}
expect() { # name want who cwd command
  out=$(run "$3" "$4" "$5")
  case "$out" in *'"deny"'*) got=deny ;; *) got=allow ;; esac
  if [ "$got" != "$2" ]; then echo "FAIL: $1 (want $2, got $got)"; fail=1; else echo "ok: $1"; fi
}
# --- unguarded cd (everyone)
expect "2026-11-12 shape: cd missing; git switch -c" deny agent "$WT" "cd /missing/worktree; git switch -c foo"
expect "2026-11-10 shape: cd train-wt; git merge" deny agent "$WT" "cd $TMP/dev-targets/wt/train-wt; git merge fix/x"
expect "newline after cd is unguarded" deny coord "$MAIN" $'cd /x\ngit status'
expect "subshell ( cd X; ... ) is unguarded" deny agent "$WT" "( cd /x; git status )"
expect "cd X || echo; more is unguarded" deny agent "$WT" "cd /x || echo no; git status"
expect "cd X && ... is allowed" allow agent "$WT" "cd $WT && git status"
expect "cd X || exit 1; ... is allowed" allow agent "$WT" "cd $WT || exit 1; git status"
expect "cd X || return; ... is allowed" allow agent "$WT" "cd $WT || return; git status"
expect "a bare cd is allowed" allow agent "$WT" "cd $WT"
expect "cd X; with nothing after is allowed" allow agent "$WT" "cd $WT;"
expect "( cd X && ... ) is allowed" allow agent "$WT" "( cd $WT && git status )"
expect "a ; inside quotes is not a separator" allow agent "$WT" "cd $WT && echo 'a; b'"
expect "if cd X; then is not a bare cd" allow agent "$WT" "if cd $WT; then echo ok; fi"
expect "no cd at all" allow agent "$WT" "git status; git log -1"
# --- agent git writes in the main checkout
expect "agent git switch in main (cwd)" deny agent "$MAIN" "git switch -c foo"
expect "agent git commit via -C main" deny agent "$WT" "git -C $MAIN commit -m x"
expect "agent cd main && git merge" deny agent "$WT" "cd $MAIN && git merge fix/x"
expect "agent git push in main" deny agent "$MAIN" "git push origin main"
expect "agent git branch -D in main" deny agent "$MAIN" "git branch -D old"
expect "agent git worktree remove in main" deny agent "$MAIN" "git worktree remove /x"
expect "agent git tag v1 in main" deny agent "$MAIN" "git tag v1"
expect "agent fetch && reset in main" deny agent "$MAIN" "git fetch origin && git reset --hard origin/main"
expect "agent cherry-pick in main" deny agent "$MAIN" "git cherry-pick abc"
expect "agent git fetch in main is allowed" allow agent "$MAIN" "git fetch origin"
expect "agent git status/log/diff in main" allow agent "$MAIN" "git status && git log -3 && git diff HEAD~1"
expect "agent git worktree add in main" allow agent "$MAIN" "git worktree add $TMP/dev-targets/wt/x -b b origin/main"
expect "agent git worktree list/lock in main" allow agent "$MAIN" "git worktree list && git worktree lock /x"
expect "agent git branch --list in main" allow agent "$MAIN" "git branch --list"
expect "agent git tag -l in main" allow agent "$MAIN" "git tag -l 'dyno-*'"
expect "agent git commit in its own worktree" allow agent "$WT" "git commit -m x"
expect "agent git -C own worktree commit" allow agent "$MAIN" "git -C $WT commit -m x"
expect "agent cd own worktree && merge" allow agent "$MAIN" "cd $WT && git merge x"
# --- the coordinator
expect "coordinator ff-merge in main" allow coord "$MAIN" "git merge --ff-only origin/main"
expect "coordinator push from main" allow coord "$MAIN" "git push origin main"

# ---- the reviewer's cases (2026-11-12): every line must match
t() { # want who cwd name cmd
  if [ "$2" = agent ]; then x='{"agent_id":"a1"}'; else x='{}'; fi
  out=$(jq -nc --arg c "$5" --arg d "$3" --argjson x "$x" '{tool_name:"Bash",cwd:$d,tool_input:{command:$c}}+$x' | "$H" 2>&1)
  case "$out" in *'"deny"'*) g=deny;; *Traceback*) g=CRASH;; *) g=allow;; esac
  if [ "$g" = "$1" ]; then echo "ok: $4"; else echo "FAIL: $4 (want $1, got $g)"; fail=1; fi
}
t allow coord $MAIN "heredoc with cd lines" $'cat > /x/s.sh <<\'EOF\'\ncd /a\nmake\nEOF\nchmod +x /x/s.sh'
t allow coord $MAIN "unquoted heredoc with cd" $'cat > /x/s.sh <<EOF\ncd $HOME\nls\nEOF'
t allow coord $MAIN "git commit -m heredoc" $'git commit -m "$(cat <<\'EOF\'\nfix: x\n\ncd foo; bar\nEOF\n)"'
t allow coord $MAIN "cd in single quotes" "echo 'cd /x; ls'"
t allow coord $MAIN "comment mentions cd" $'ls # then cd /x; ls\necho done'
t allow coord $MAIN "sh -c with cd; (inner, FN accepted)" "sh -c 'cd /x; make'"
t allow coord $MAIN "bash -lc with cd && " "bash -lc 'cd /x && make'"
t allow coord $MAIN "cd X || { echo; exit 1; }" "cd /x || { echo no; exit 1; }; make"
t allow coord $MAIN "set -e then cd newline" $'set -e\ncd /x\nmake'
t deny  coord $MAIN "for loop cd; (rule says deny)" "for d in a b; do cd \$d; make; cd ..; done"
t deny  coord $MAIN "cd X && a; b  (b runs in wrong dir)" "cd /missing && git fetch; git merge x"
t allow coord $MAIN "pushd ... (not covered)" "pushd /x; make; popd"
t allow coord $MAIN "cd X 2>/dev/null || exit 1; ls" "cd /x 2>/dev/null || exit 1; ls"
t deny  coord $MAIN "if ...; then cd X; git merge; fi" "if true; then cd /x; git merge y; fi"
t allow coord $MAIN "python -c with ; and cd word" "python3 -c 'import os; os.chdir(\"/x\"); print(1)'"
t allow coord $MAIN "awk with cd text" "awk '/cd /{print}; END{print 1}' f"
t allow coord $MAIN "jq filter with ; and (" "jq -r '.a | (.b; .c)' f; echo"
t allow coord $MAIN "case ... ) inside" $'case $x in a) cd /x && ls ;; esac'
t allow coord $MAIN "arith ((  ))" "(( i++ )); cd /x && ls"
t allow coord $MAIN "\$(cd X && pwd)" "D=\$(cd /x && pwd); echo \$D"
t deny  coord $MAIN "\$(cd X; pwd) unguarded" "D=\$(cd /x; pwd); echo \$D"
t allow coord $MAIN "trailing comment after cd" "cd /x # go there"
t allow coord $MAIN "cd then newline comment only" $'cd /x\n# done'
t deny  agent $MAIN "agent: git -C quoted main commit" "git -C \"$MAIN\" commit -m x"
t deny  agent $MAIN "agent: env VAR=1 git push" "env GIT_SSH=x git push origin y"
t deny  agent $MAIN "agent: VAR=1 git merge (main cwd)" "GIT_TRACE=1 git merge x"
t deny  agent $MAIN "agent: git -c k=v merge" "git -c core.x=1 merge x"
t deny  agent $MAIN "agent: lowercase /volumes path" "git -C $(printf %s "$MAIN" | tr A-Z a-z) merge x"
t allow agent $MAIN "agent: git branch new (create)" "git branch newb origin/main"
t deny  agent $MAIN "agent: git update-ref (FN)" "git update-ref refs/heads/main HEAD~1"
t deny  agent $MAIN "agent: git branch with force flag" "git branch --force main HEAD~1"
t deny  agent $MAIN "agent: git -C main checkout in subshell" "( git -C $MAIN checkout x )"
t allow agent $MAIN "agent: cd wt && commit && status" "cd $WT && git commit -m x && git status"
t allow agent $MAIN "agent: git log in main" "git log --oneline -5"
t allow agent $WT   "agent: cd \$VAR && git merge (unknown, fail open)" "cd \$WT && git merge x"
t deny  agent $MAIN "agent: sudo git reset" "sudo git reset --hard"
t deny  agent $MAIN "agent: xargs git checkout (FN)" "echo a | xargs git checkout"
t allow coord $MAIN "unterminated quote" "echo 'abc; cd /x; ls"
t allow coord $MAIN "unbalanced paren" "echo ) ; cd /x && ls"

# --- fail open
out=$(echo 'not json' | "$H" 2>/dev/null); [ -z "$out" ] && echo "ok: bad input allows" || { echo "FAIL: bad input"; fail=1; }
out=$(jq -nc '{tool_name:"Bash",cwd:"/x",agent_id:"a",tool_input:{command:"git commit -m \"unterminated"}}' | "$H" 2>/dev/null); [ -z "$out" ] && echo "ok: odd quoting allows" || { echo "FAIL: odd quoting"; fail=1; }
# --- messages name the cause and the next step
out=$(run agent "$WT" "cd /missing; git status")
case "$out" in *"unguarded cd"*"cd /missing && ..."*) echo "ok: cd message" ;; *) echo "FAIL: cd message"; fail=1 ;; esac
out=$(run agent "$MAIN" "git commit -m x")
case "$out" in *"main checkout"*"your own worktree"*) echo "ok: main-checkout message" ;; *) echo "FAIL: main message"; fail=1 ;; esac

# ---- size cap and linear time (shared scanner)
big=$(python3 -c 'print("cp " + "a" * 300000 + " /x")')
out=$(run agent "$MAIN" "$big" 2>"${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/wg-err.$$"); case "$out" in *deny*) echo "FAIL: over 200 KB must allow"; fail=1 ;; *) grep -q "too large" "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/wg-err.$$" 2>/dev/null && echo "ok: over 200 KB allows with a warning" || echo "ok: over 200 KB allows" ;; esac
rm -f "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/wg-err.$$"
word=$(python3 -c 'print("echo " + "a" * 150000 + "; git status")')
s0=$(python3 -c 'import time;print(time.time())'); run agent "$MAIN" "$word" >/dev/null
ms=$(python3 -c "import time;print(int((time.time()-$s0)*1000))"); [ "$ms" -lt 1500 ] && echo "ok: a 150 KB token scans in ${ms} ms" || { echo "FAIL: 150 KB token took ${ms} ms"; fail=1; }
body=$(python3 -c 'print("\n".join("cd /x; mkdir y; echo %d" % i for i in range(5000)))')
s0=$(python3 -c 'import time;print(time.time())'); out=$(run agent "$MAIN" "cat > /x/f <<EOF
$body
EOF"); ms=$(python3 -c "import time;print(int((time.time()-$s0)*1000))")
case "$out" in *deny*) echo "FAIL: a heredoc body full of cd lines must be skipped"; fail=1 ;; *) [ "$ms" -lt 1500 ] && echo "ok: a 5000-line heredoc is skipped in ${ms} ms" || { echo "FAIL: heredoc took ${ms} ms"; fail=1; } ;; esac

# ---- a push after an unguarded commit (the commit-msg hook rejected it and the push still ran, twice on 2026-11-12)
expect "commit; push is refused" deny agent "$WT" "git commit -m x; git push origin b"
expect "commit newline push is refused" deny agent "$WT" $'git commit -m x\ngit push origin b'
expect "commit && x; push is refused" deny coord "$WT" "git commit -m x && echo ok; git push"
expect "commit && push is allowed" allow agent "$WT" "git commit -m x && git push origin b"
expect "commit || exit 1; push is allowed" allow agent "$WT" "git commit -m x || exit 1; git push origin b"
expect "commit || { ...; exit 1; }; push is allowed" allow agent "$WT" "git commit -m x || { echo no; exit 1; }; git push"
expect "a push alone is allowed" allow agent "$WT" "git push origin b"
expect "push before commit is allowed" allow agent "$WT" "git push origin a; git commit -m x"
expect "if git commit; then git push is allowed" allow agent "$WT" "if git commit -m x; then git push; fi"
expect "set -e then commit newline push is allowed" allow agent "$WT" $'set -e\ngit commit -m x\ngit push'
out=$(run agent "$WT" "git commit -m x; git push"); case "$out" in *"commit"*"&&"*) echo "ok: message names the next step" ;; *) echo "FAIL: push message"; fail=1 ;; esac

# ---- agents may not bypass the git hooks (lefthook)
expect "agent LEFTHOOK=0 git commit" deny agent "$WT" "LEFTHOOK=0 git commit -m x"
expect "agent env LEFTHOOK=0 git push" deny agent "$WT" "env LEFTHOOK=0 git push origin b"
expect "agent LEFTHOOK_EXCLUDE=x git push" deny agent "$WT" "LEFTHOOK_EXCLUDE=commit-msg git push"
expect "agent git commit --no-verify" deny agent "$WT" "git commit --no-verify -m x"
expect "agent git push --no-verify" deny agent "$WT" "git push --no-verify origin b"
expect "agent git -C wt commit -n --no-verify" deny agent "$WT" "git -C $WT commit -m x --no-verify"
expect "agent export-less LEFTHOOK=0 then git commit on its own line is not an env prefix" allow agent "$WT" $'LEFTHOOK=0\ngit commit -m x'
expect "agent plain commit is allowed" allow agent "$WT" "git commit -m x"
expect "agent LEFTHOOK=1 is allowed" allow agent "$WT" "LEFTHOOK=1 git commit -m x"
expect "coordinator LEFTHOOK=0 git commit is allowed" allow coord "$WT" "LEFTHOOK=0 git commit -m x"
expect "coordinator --no-verify is allowed" allow coord "$WT" "git commit --no-verify -m x"
expect "agent mentions --no-verify in a message" allow agent "$WT" "git commit -m 'never use --no-verify'"
out=$(run agent "$WT" "git commit --no-verify -m x"); case "$out" in *"Hooks must pass: cherry-pick the hook fix or stop and report (no bypass)"*) echo "ok: bypass message" ;; *) echo "FAIL: bypass message"; fail=1 ;; esac

# ---- more bypass forms: commit -n, combined short flags, an exported variable earlier in the command
expect "agent git commit -n" deny agent "$WT" "git commit -n -m x"
expect "agent git commit -nm" deny agent "$WT" "git commit -nm 'x'"
expect "agent git commit -anm" deny agent "$WT" "git commit -anm 'x'"
expect "agent git commit -mn... is a message, not -n" allow agent "$WT" "git commit -m'fix: nothing' -a"
expect "agent git commit -m message with an n" allow agent "$WT" "git commit -m 'run now'"
expect "agent git push -n is a dry run, not a bypass" allow agent "$WT" "git push -n origin b"
expect "agent export LEFTHOOK=0 then commit" deny agent "$WT" "export LEFTHOOK=0 && git commit -m x"
expect "agent export LEFTHOOK_EXCLUDE then push on a later line" deny agent "$WT" $'export LEFTHOOK_EXCLUDE=commit-msg\ngit push origin b'
expect "agent LEFTHOOK=0 then export LEFTHOOK then commit" deny agent "$WT" "LEFTHOOK=0; export LEFTHOOK; git commit -m x"
expect "agent export LEFTHOOK=1 then commit" allow agent "$WT" "export LEFTHOOK=1; git commit -m x"
expect "coordinator export LEFTHOOK=0 then commit" allow coord "$WT" "export LEFTHOOK=0; git commit -m x"
# ---- core.hooksPath is the same bypass as --no-verify (an agent tried `git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null` on 2026-11-17)
expect "agent git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null commit" deny agent "$WT" "git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null commit -m x"
expect "agent git -c core.hookspath (any case) push" deny agent "$WT" "git -c core.hookspath=/x push origin b"
expect "agent git -C wt -c core.hooksPath= status (a read: not judged)" allow agent "$WT" "git -C $WT -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null status"
expect "agent git --config-env=core.hooksPath=V commit" deny agent "$WT" "git --config-env=core.hooksPath=V commit -m x"
expect "agent git config core.hooksPath /dev/null" deny agent "$WT" "git config core.hooksPath /dev/null"
expect "agent git config --local core.hooksPath x" deny agent "$WT" "git config --local core.hooksPath /x"
expect "agent GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS prefix" deny agent "$WT" "GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS=\"'core.hookspath=/dev/null'\" git commit -m x"
expect "agent export GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS then commit" deny agent "$WT" "export GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS=\"'core.hooksPath=/dev/null'\"; git commit -m x"
expect "agent GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=core.hooksPath prefix" deny agent "$WT" "GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1 GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=core.hooksPath GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=/dev/null git commit -m x"
expect "agent env GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS" deny agent "$WT" "env GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS=\"'core.hooksPath=/x'\" git push origin b"
expect "agent reads core.hooksPath" allow agent "$WT" "git config --get core.hooksPath"
expect "agent -c with another key" allow agent "$WT" "git -c user.name=x status"
expect "coordinator -c core.hooksPath is allowed" allow coord "$WT" "git -c core.hooksPath=/x status"
expect "agent mentions core.hooksPath in a message" allow agent "$WT" "git commit -m 'never set core.hooksPath'"
# ---- one outcome rule (ER-39): a commit, push, merge, cherry-pick, rebase, am or revert by an agent carries no config override at all
#      (any -c, --config-env, GIT_CONFIG_*, HOME, XDG_CONFIG_HOME, GIT_DIR, GIT_EXEC_PATH): each of them can point git at other hooks.
expect "agent git -c include.path=/x/g commit" deny agent "$WT" "git -c include.path=/x/g commit -m x"
expect "agent GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/x/g commit" deny agent "$WT" "GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/x/g git commit -m x"
expect "agent HOME=/x/h commit" deny agent "$WT" "HOME=/x/h git commit -m x"
expect "agent XDG_CONFIG_HOME=/x commit" deny agent "$WT" "XDG_CONFIG_HOME=/x git commit -m x"
expect "agent GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM push" deny agent "$WT" "GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM=/x git push origin b"
expect "agent GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM merge" deny agent "$WT" "GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 git merge x"
expect "agent GIT_CONFIG_COUNT rebase" deny agent "$WT" "GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1 GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=hooks.x GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=y git rebase main"
expect "agent GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0 alone cherry-pick" deny agent "$WT" "GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=y git cherry-pick abc1234"
expect "agent GIT_DIR=/x am" deny agent "$WT" "GIT_DIR=/x/.git git am p.patch"
expect "agent GIT_EXEC_PATH=/x revert" deny agent "$WT" "GIT_EXEC_PATH=/x git revert abc1234"
expect "agent export HOME then commit" deny agent "$WT" "export HOME=/x/h; git commit -m x"
expect "agent env HOME= commit" deny agent "$WT" "env HOME=/x/h git commit -m x"
expect "agent git -c user.name=x commit" deny agent "$WT" "git -c user.name=x commit -m x"
expect "agent git -C wt -c include.path=/x merge" deny agent "$WT" "git -C $WT -c include.path=/x merge y"
expect "agent git --config-env=include.path=V push" deny agent "$WT" "git --config-env include.path=V push origin b"
expect "agent git --exec-path=/x commit" deny agent "$WT" "git --exec-path=/x commit -m x"
expect "agent git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null commit (outcome rule)" deny agent "$WT" "git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null commit"
expect "agent git commit, plain" allow agent "$WT" "git commit -m x"
expect "agent git -C wt commit, plain" allow agent "$WT" "git -C $WT commit -m x"
expect "agent integrator merge with -m" allow agent "$WT" "git -C $WT merge --no-ff -m 'chore(train): merge fix/x into train 14' fix/x"
expect "agent plain push" allow agent "$WT" "git push origin fix/x"
expect "agent plain rebase / am / revert" allow agent "$WT" "git rebase origin/main && git am p.patch && git revert abc1234"
expect "agent GIT_TRACE=1 commit is no config override" allow agent "$WT" "GIT_TRACE=1 git commit -m x"
expect "agent HOMEBREW_X=1 commit is not HOME" allow agent "$WT" "HOMEBREW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1 git commit -m x"
expect "agent git -c color.ui=false log (a read: not judged)" allow agent "$WT" "git -c color.ui=false log -1"
expect "agent HOME=/x git status (a read: not judged)" allow agent "$WT" "HOME=/x git status"
expect "coordinator -c on a commit is allowed" allow coord "$WT" "git -c user.name=x commit -m x"
expect "agent git config get core.hooksPath (a read)" allow agent "$WT" "git config get core.hooksPath"
expect "agent git config --get-all core.hooksPath (a read)" allow agent "$WT" "git config --get-all core.hooksPath"
expect "agent git config core.hooksPath (a bare-key read)" allow agent "$WT" "git config core.hooksPath"
expect "agent git config --list (a read)" allow agent "$WT" "git config --list"
expect "agent git config --unset core.hooksPath" deny agent "$WT" "git config --unset core.hooksPath"
expect "agent git config unset core.hooksPath" deny agent "$WT" "git config unset core.hooksPath"
expect "agent git config set core.hooksPath x" deny agent "$WT" "git config set core.hooksPath /x"
expect "agent git config --add core.hooksPath x" deny agent "$WT" "git config --add core.hooksPath /x"
expect "agent git config --edit" deny agent "$WT" "git config --edit"
expect "agent git config --file f core.hooksPath x" deny agent "$WT" "git config --file /x/f core.hooksPath /x"
expect "agent git config user.name x (another key)" allow agent "$WT" "git config user.name x"
# ---- the main checkout is derived, not a default path (disks moved on 2026-11-14 and the old default went stale)
expect "agent git commit in a main checkout at a non-default path is refused" deny agent "$MAIN" "git commit -m x"
expect "agent git commit from a subfolder of that main checkout is refused" deny agent "$MAIN/sub" "git commit -m x"
mkdir -p "$TMP/other" && git init -q "$TMP/other/repo"
expect "another repo is not the main checkout" allow agent "$TMP/other/repo" "git commit -m x"
mkdir -p "$TMP/nogit"
out=$(jq -nc --arg d "$TMP/nogit" '{tool_name:"Bash",cwd:$d,agent_id:"a1",tool_input:{command:"git commit -m x"}}' | CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR="$TMP/nogit" "$H" 2>/dev/null)
case "$out" in *'"deny"'*"Next step"*) echo "ok: underivable main refuses with a next step" ;; *) echo "FAIL: underivable main must refuse"; fail=1 ;; esac
out=$(jq -nc --arg d "$TMP/nogit" '{tool_name:"Bash",cwd:$d,agent_id:"a1",tool_input:{command:"git commit -m x"}}' | CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR="$TMP/nogit" WORKTREE_GUARD_MAIN="$TMP/nogit" "$H" 2>/dev/null)
case "$out" in *'"deny"'*"main checkout"*) echo "ok: WORKTREE_GUARD_MAIN override" ;; *) echo "FAIL: override"; fail=1 ;; esac
# --- paddock.* git config is shared by every worktree (the common config): a subagent never writes it (it retargets the VM, lock
#     and disk folders for everyone, docs/dev-setup.md "Where things live"); reads are fine, and the coordinator may write it.
expect "agent git config paddock.worktreeRoot <v>" deny agent "$WT" "git config paddock.worktreeRoot /srv/x/wt"
expect "agent git -C wt config --local paddock.worktreeRoot <v>" deny agent "$WT" "git -C $WT config --local paddock.worktreeRoot /srv/x/wt"
expect "agent git config --global paddock.x <v>" deny agent "$WT" "git config --global paddock.x y"
expect "agent git config --unset paddock.worktreeRoot" deny agent "$WT" "git config --unset paddock.worktreeRoot"
expect "agent git config set paddock.worktreeRoot <v>" deny agent "$WT" "git config set paddock.worktreeRoot /srv/x/wt"
expect "agent git config --replace-all Paddock.WorktreeRoot <v>" deny agent "$WT" "git config --replace-all Paddock.WorktreeRoot /srv/x/wt"
expect "agent git config --remove-section paddock" deny agent "$WT" "git config --remove-section paddock"
expect "agent git config paddock.worktreeRoot (a read)" allow agent "$WT" "git config paddock.worktreeRoot"
expect "agent git config --get paddock.worktreeRoot" allow agent "$WT" "git config --get paddock.worktreeRoot"
expect "agent git config get paddock.worktreeRoot" allow agent "$WT" "git config get paddock.worktreeRoot"
expect "agent git config --get-regexp ^paddock" allow agent "$WT" "git config --get-regexp ^paddock"
expect "agent git config user.name in its worktree" allow agent "$WT" "git config user.email a@example.invalid"
expect "agent git config --file <f> paddock.worktreeRoot <v>" deny agent "$WT" "git config --file .git/config paddock.worktreeRoot /x"
expect "agent git config -f <f> paddock.worktreeRoot <v>" deny agent "$WT" "git config -f .git/config paddock.worktreeRoot /x"
expect "agent git config --file=<f> paddock.worktreeRoot <v>" deny agent "$WT" "git config --file=.git/config paddock.worktreeRoot /x"
expect "agent git config --type bool paddock.x true" deny agent "$WT" "git config --type bool paddock.x true"
expect "agent git config --blob <b> paddock.x (a read)" allow agent "$WT" "git config --blob HEAD:cfg paddock.x"
expect "agent git config -f <f> paddock.worktreeRoot (a read)" allow agent "$WT" "git config -f .git/config paddock.worktreeRoot"
expect "agent git config --fixed-value paddock.worktreeRoot <v> <old>" deny agent "$WT" "git config --fixed-value paddock.worktreeRoot /x /old"
expect "agent git config --replace-all --fixed-value paddock.worktreeRoot <v> <old>" deny agent "$WT" "git config --replace-all --fixed-value paddock.worktreeRoot /x /old"
expect "agent git config -z paddock.worktreeRoot <v>" deny agent "$WT" "git config -z paddock.worktreeRoot /z"
expect "agent git config --null paddock.worktreeRoot <v>" deny agent "$WT" "git config --null paddock.worktreeRoot /z"
expect "agent git config --includes paddock.worktreeRoot <v>" deny agent "$WT" "git config --includes paddock.worktreeRoot /z"
expect "agent git config --no-includes paddock.worktreeRoot <v>" deny agent "$WT" "git config --no-includes paddock.worktreeRoot /z"
expect "agent git config --show-scope paddock.worktreeRoot <v>" deny agent "$WT" "git config --show-scope paddock.worktreeRoot x"
expect "agent git config --get-all paddock.worktreeRoot (a lookup)" allow agent "$WT" "git config --get-all paddock.worktreeRoot"
expect "agent git config --list (a lookup)" allow agent "$WT" "git config --list"
expect "agent git config -l --show-origin (a lookup)" allow agent "$WT" "git config -l --show-origin"
expect "agent git config list (a lookup)" allow agent "$WT" "git config list"
expect "coordinator git config paddock.worktreeRoot <v>" allow coord "$MAIN" "git config paddock.worktreeRoot /srv/x/wt"

# The shared shell-forms corpus: every scanner bypass and false refusal found so far, judged by every guard.
bash "$here/lib/shell-forms.sh" worktree-guard "$H" || fail=1
exit $fail
.gitea/workflows/ci.yml

# The monorepo's CI (ADR 0014 §6): a plan job decides which projects a change reaches (./dev plan: the Cargo and
# npm graphs plus the frontendDist and config-path edges), then only those run: the shared UI package and its entry points,
# the reference apps, the Rust crates, the conformance, tools and ESLint packages, and one matrix leg per affected app
# (apps/<app>/paddock.ci.json, through .gitea/actions/app-gates). The base of the diff: the last green push run of main for a
# push to main, the `base` input of a manual run; tags and manual runs without a base run everything. No pull_request trigger:
# pull requests are the branch ledger (`./dev pr`, docs/plans/merge-queue.md) and opening one starts no run (the contract test
# no_workflow_runs_on_a_pull_request); branches and trains run by dispatch.
# nightly.yml runs everything, Chromium and WebKit, every night (the safety net for a wrong filter).
# Publishing is not here: a v* tag runs publish.yml (gates, then the cargo and npm registries and the Gitea release); this
# workflow ends with the publish dry run, so a tag never meets a packaging problem first.
#
# Runner labels: ubuntu-latest (jobs in the shared paddock-ci image, ci-image/), windows-latest and macos-latest (host runners, tools used as
# installed), as in Debrief and Pitwall.

name: ci

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    tags: ["v*"]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      base:
        description: "Diff from this commit (empty: run everything)"
        required: false
        default: ""
      webkit:
        description: "Also run the WebKit tests (the WebKit job, and an app's WebKit lines)"
        type: boolean
        default: false
      since_run:
        description: "Rerun only what failed in this finished ci.yml run (its API id, as ./dev ci dispatch and ./dev wait --ci-run print it; not its run number): the failed jobs, and inside a job that failed only in nextest only its failed tests (./dev plan --since-run; ER-10). Passed jobs do not run; a full run before landing catches the rest."
        required: false
        default: ""
  # nightly.yml: everything, with WebKit.
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      webkit:
        description: "Also run the WebKit job"
        type: boolean
        default: false
      app:
        description: "Only this app's legs, every half, whatever changed: the gates of an app's own tag (<app>-release.yml)"
        type: string
        default: ""
      release:
        description: "A release workflow's gates (a rule 54 dispatch counts as a release): ./dev never downloads its tool, whatever the ref"
        type: boolean
        default: false
    secrets:
      BUILD_INPUTS_TOKEN:
        required: false

# Read-only: no job of this workflow writes to the repository or the Actions state (a train's run holds no token that could).
permissions:
  contents: read
  actions: read

# The conformance checks Paddock runs on itself are the `conformance` field of conformance/paddock.ci.json (ADR 0038 §1): one list,
# run by the conformance job and the train-gates job as `./dev ci run conformance paddock`, and read by `./dev check --pre-push`.
env:
  # The fallback switch of conformance/ci/kit.sh (WP-1): set the repository variable to shell and every kit step runs its script.
  PADDOCK_CI_KIT: ${{ vars.PADDOCK_CI_KIT }}

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}-${{ github.event_name }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  # Which projects this run tests. The script's own tests run first: a wrong plan would hide failures.
  plan:
    name: plan (affected projects)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    container:
      image: dev.decryptology.net/decryp7/paddock-ci:v3
    outputs:
      crates: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.crates }}
      ui: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.ui }}
      eslint: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.eslint }}
      conformance: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.conformance }}
      c99: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.c99 }}
      tools: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.tools }}
      icons: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.icons }}
      paddock_dev: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.paddock_dev }}
      apps: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.apps }}
      any_app: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.any_app }}
      base: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.base }}
      # A rerun of a run's failures (the since_run input): the jobs that rerun (empty otherwise; each job's `if` reads an empty
      # list as its own name, so a normal run gates on the projects alone). The crate and paddock-dev legs: in a rerun of their
      # failures the failed ones, each with the nextest filter of its failed tests (empty: the whole leg); otherwise every OS.
      rerun_jobs: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.rerun_jobs }}
      crate_legs: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.crate_legs }}
      paddock_dev_legs: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.paddock_dev_legs }}
    env:
      PADDOCK_DEV_DOWNLOAD: ${{ (inputs.release == true || startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/')) && '0' || '' }}
    steps:
      # The whole history: the base (a merge base, the last green commit of main) can be any older commit.
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          fetch-depth: 0
      # A train run is dispatched at once and waits here, on Linux, until no older run holds the Mac or Windows runner it
      # needs (./dev ci runner-wait); the queued run is what scheduled runs yield to. Other events: nothing.
      - uses: ./.gitea/actions/runner-wait
        with:
          dev-token: ${{ secrets.BUILD_INPUTS_TOKEN }}

      # ADR 0060: C100 cannot be the only guard of its own wiring (a change that deletes the line deletes the check too), so a plain
      # grep on every event checks that the conformance job and the nightly still run it.
      - name: C100 stays wired
        run: |
          for f in .gitea/workflows/ci.yml .gitea/workflows/nightly.yml; do
            grep -Eq '^[[:space:]]*run: \./dev gates check( --warn)?$' "$f" || { echo "::error file=$f::C100 is not wired: no line runs ./dev gates check. Fix: restore the line (ADR 0060 section 4)."; exit 1; }
          done

      - name: Affected projects
        id: plan
        env:
          PLAN_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          PADDOCK_DEV_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.BUILD_INPUTS_TOKEN }}
          PADDOCK_DEV_DOWNLOAD: ${{ (inputs.release == true || startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/')) && '0' || '' }}
          PLAN_BASE: ${{ github.event.inputs.base }}
          PLAN_APP: ${{ inputs.app }}
          PLAN_WEBKIT: ${{ (inputs.webkit == true || inputs.webkit == 'true') && '1' || '' }}
          # The rerun reads the earlier run's jobs and logs through the API (tools/paddock-dev/src/plan_since.rs).
          PLAN_SINCE_RUN: ${{ github.event.inputs.since_run }}
          # The crate and paddock-dev legs when the plan names none of its own (every run but a rerun of their failures).
          PLAN_OS_LEGS: '[{"os":"ubuntu-latest"},{"os":"windows-latest"},{"os":"macos-latest"}]'
          # The scope of this run (tests everything its plan can reach, not a diff from a base or a rerun of failures): a push to
          # main, an app's own gates, a manual run with no base. The line `plan verdict: complete=` at the end of the step is what
          # `./dev ci verdict` reads (plan_since::COMPLETE_LINE); this one is only the scope.
          PLAN_MODE_FULL: ${{ github.event_name == 'push' || inputs.app != '' || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.event.inputs.base == '' && github.event.inputs.since_run == '') }}
        run: |
          echo "plan mode: full=$PLAN_MODE_FULL"
          ./dev plan --ci
          grep -q '^crate_legs=' "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" || echo "crate_legs=$PLAN_OS_LEGS" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          grep -q '^paddock_dev_legs=' "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" || echo "paddock_dev_legs=$PLAN_OS_LEGS" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          # After the plan decided: complete only for a full run that is not a rerun of failures (plan_since::COMPLETE_LINE).
          complete=false
          if [ -z "$PLAN_SINCE_RUN" ] && [ "$PLAN_MODE_FULL" = true ]; then complete=true; fi
          echo "plan verdict: complete=$complete"

  # C102 (ADR 0072): every listen site of the Rust sources is in docs/ipc-endpoints.toml with an ending test or a reason, and the
  # ratchet of connection endings is well formed. Always runs (./dev builds paddock-dev from source here, about a minute; the scan itself takes about 3 s): a listener added anywhere must not
  # land unregistered, whatever the plan thinks it reaches.
  ipc-endpoints:
    name: endpoint register (C102)
    needs: [plan]
    if: ${{ contains(fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.rerun_jobs || '["ipc-endpoints"]'), 'ipc-endpoints') }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    container:
      image: dev.decryptology.net/decryp7/paddock-ci:v3
    env:
      PADDOCK_DEV_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.BUILD_INPUTS_TOKEN }}
      PADDOCK_DEV_DOWNLOAD: ${{ (inputs.release == true || startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/')) && '0' || '' }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      # Before the first ./dev of the job: it hashes and builds itself with the job's pinned compiler (C119).
      - uses: ./.gitea/actions/setup-rust

      - name: Every listen site is registered
        run: ./dev check ipc-endpoints

      - uses: ./.gitea/actions/sccache-stats
        if: always()

  ui:
    needs: [plan]
    if: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.ui == 'true' && contains(fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.rerun_jobs || '["ui"]'), 'ui') }}
    name: ui (tokens, contrast, components, entry points, publish dry run)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    container:
      image: dev.decryptology.net/decryp7/paddock-ci:v3
    env:
      # `./dev ci run` runs the job's commands from its project's paddock.ci.json (ADR 0038 §1): a tag or release run builds the tool from source.
      # The read credential is set on the ./dev steps only.
      PADDOCK_DEV_DOWNLOAD: ${{ (inputs.release == true || startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/')) && '0' || '' }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      # Before the first ./dev of the job: it hashes and builds itself with the job's pinned compiler (C119).
      - env:
          PADDOCK_DEV_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.BUILD_INPUTS_TOKEN }}
        uses: ./.gitea/actions/setup-rust

      - uses: ./.gitea/actions/node-caches

      # One npm workspace for the repo (ADR 0014 §1): the root lock installs every package.
      - name: Install
        working-directory: .
        run: npm ci

      # WCAG contrast of every text/background pair and colour-vision separation of the chart palette.
      - env:
          PADDOCK_DEV_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.BUILD_INPUTS_TOKEN }}
        name: Contrast and CVD checks
        run: ./dev ci run ui tokens

      # The Paddock ESLint preset (rules 27 to 39 and the angular-eslint template and accessibility rules) over every ui project.
      - env:
          PADDOCK_DEV_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.BUILD_INPUTS_TOKEN }}
        name: Lint
        run: ./dev ci run ui lint

      - env:
          PADDOCK_DEV_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.BUILD_INPUTS_TOKEN }}
        name: Component specs
        run: ./dev ci run ui specs

      - env:
          PADDOCK_DEV_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.BUILD_INPUTS_TOKEN }}
        name: Script tests
        run: ./dev ci run ui scripts

      # Every entry point (root, /shell/*, /workbench/*) is built by ng-packagr; the dry run below checks each is exported.
      - env:
          PADDOCK_DEV_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.BUILD_INPUTS_TOKEN }}
        name: Build the library (all entry points)
        run: ./dev ci run ui build

      # The shell's message catalog and the pseudo-locale files match the build (plan S15: `npm run i18n` to refresh).
      - env:
          PADDOCK_DEV_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.BUILD_INPUTS_TOKEN }}
        name: Translation files up to date
        run: ./dev ci run ui i18n

      - env:
          PADDOCK_DEV_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.BUILD_INPUTS_TOKEN }}
        name: Build @decryp7/paddock-e2e
        run: ./dev ci run ui build-e2e

      - env:
          PADDOCK_DEV_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.BUILD_INPUTS_TOKEN }}
        name: Build the shell demo
        run: ./dev ci run ui shell-demo

      - env:
          PADDOCK_DEV_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.BUILD_INPUTS_TOKEN }}
        name: Build the workbench demo
        run: ./dev ci run ui workbench-demo

      # Lists every npm package, entry point and crate with what a tag would publish; publishes nothing.
      - env:
          PADDOCK_DEV_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.BUILD_INPUTS_TOKEN }}
        name: Publish dry run
        run: ./dev ci run ui publish-dry-run

      - uses: ./.gitea/actions/sccache-stats
        if: always()

  # The reference apps in the browser (gallery and shell demo; axe, keyboard, CSP, 320 px), in two shards that run at the
  # same time: the specs run one at a time within a shard (playwright.config.ts), so splitting the files halves the wait.
  # The apps compile from source (tsconfig paths), so a shard needs no library build.
  e2e:
    name: reference apps (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/2)
    needs: [plan]
    if: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.ui == 'true' && contains(fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.rerun_jobs || '["e2e"]'), 'e2e') }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    container:
      image: dev.decryptology.net/decryp7/paddock-ci:v3
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [1, 2]
    env:
      # `./dev ci run` runs the job's commands from its project's paddock.ci.json (ADR 0038 §1): a tag or release run builds the tool from source.
      # The read credential is set on the ./dev steps only.
      PADDOCK_DEV_DOWNLOAD: ${{ (inputs.release == true || startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/')) && '0' || '' }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      # Before the first ./dev of the job: it hashes and builds itself with the job's pinned compiler (C119).
      - env:
          PADDOCK_DEV_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.BUILD_INPUTS_TOKEN }}
        uses: ./.gitea/actions/setup-rust

      # Playwright's browsers and Chrome for Testing are baked into the image (ci-image/): nothing is downloaded per job.
      - uses: ./.gitea/actions/node-caches
        with:
          name: e2e-${{ matrix.shard }}

      - name: Install
        working-directory: .
        run: npm ci

      - name: Reference app checks
        # CI names its ports (@decryp7/paddock-e2e refuses a default there: another job could hold it), one pair per shard.
        env:
          PADDOCK_DEV_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.BUILD_INPUTS_TOKEN }}
          PW_PORT: ${{ matrix.shard == 1 && '4300' || '4310' }}
          SHELL_DEMO_PORT: ${{ matrix.shard == 1 && '4301' || '4311' }}
          WORKBENCH_DEMO_PORT: ${{ matrix.shard == 1 && '4302' || '4312' }}
          E2E_SHARD: ${{ matrix.shard }}/2
        run: ./dev ci run ui e2e

      - uses: ./.gitea/actions/sccache-stats
        if: always()

  # WebKit is the engine of WKWebView, which the macOS apps render in: the three ui Playwright projects run in it on the Mac host runner
  # (Playwright's own WebKit build), for pushes to main, v* tags and nightly.yml only. Branch runs stay Chromium-only (rule 3).
  e2e-webkit:
    name: reference apps in WebKit (macOS)
    needs: [plan]
    if: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.ui == 'true' && (inputs.webkit == true || (github.event_name == 'push' && (github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' || startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v'))) || contains(fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.rerun_jobs || '[]'), 'e2e-webkit')) && contains(fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.rerun_jobs || '["e2e-webkit"]'), 'e2e-webkit') }}
    runs-on: macos-latest
    env:
      # A run for a tag builds the tool from source (ADR 0022: release and tag jobs bypass every cache); other runs may download it.
      PADDOCK_DEV_DOWNLOAD: ${{ (inputs.release == true || startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/')) && '0' || '' }}
      # Read credential for ./dev's prebuilt download (ADR 0022 R0b).
      PADDOCK_DEV_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.BUILD_INPUTS_TOKEN }}
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: ui
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      # CARGO_BUILD_JOBS: this runner's share of the host's cores (before job-isolation, which builds paddock-dev).
      - uses: ./.gitea/actions/build-jobs

      # A slot of the host (job isolation): its own Angular cache and ports, so two runs of this job can share the Mac.
      - uses: ./.gitea/actions/job-isolation

      - uses: ./.gitea/actions/node-caches

      - name: Install
        working-directory: .
        run: npm ci

      # A host runner has no image: the browser is installed once per Playwright version into a kept host folder (outside the
      # checkout and the runner user's own caches, rule 7) and only when that folder is missing.
      - name: WebKit
        run: |
          PW_VERSION=$(node -p "require('playwright-core/package.json').version")
          BROWSERS="${RUNNER_TOOL_CACHE:-$HOME/.cache}/paddock-playwright/$PW_VERSION"
          echo "PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=$BROWSERS" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          if [ ! -f "$BROWSERS/.installed-webkit" ]; then
            PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH="$BROWSERS" npx playwright install webkit
            touch "$BROWSERS/.installed-webkit"
          fi

      - name: Reference app checks in WebKit
        env:
          PADDOCK_WEBKIT: "1"
        run: |
          # The job slot's own block of three ports (conformance/ci/ports.txt `webkit`: 4320-4322 for s1).
          port=$(bash ../conformance/ci/kit.sh isolation port webkit)
          export PW_PORT=$port SHELL_DEMO_PORT=$((port + 1)) WORKBENCH_DEMO_PORT=$((port + 2))
          npx playwright test --project=gallery-webkit --project=shell-demo-webkit --project=workbench-demo-webkit
          npx playwright test -c projects/paddock-e2e/selftest/playwright.config.ts --project=webkit

      - uses: ./.gitea/actions/job-isolation
        if: always()
        with:
          mode: release

  # @decryp7/paddock-conformance (conformance/, plan X9): every check has a good and a bad fixture, the release scripts are
  # tested (latest.json byte-equal to the apps' copy), the shared macOS verify runs against a shimmed bundle. One dependency, `yaml`
  # (C111 parses every workflow), installed from the root package-lock.json (conformance is a root npm workspace).
  conformance:
    name: conformance (checks, release scripts)
    needs: [plan]
    if: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.conformance == 'true' && contains(fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.rerun_jobs || '["conformance"]'), 'conformance') }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    container:
      image: dev.decryptology.net/decryp7/paddock-ci:v3
    env:
      PADDOCK_DEV_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.BUILD_INPUTS_TOKEN }}
      PADDOCK_DEV_DOWNLOAD: ${{ (inputs.release == true || startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/')) && '0' || '' }}
      # The ref the baselines' and allow lists' growth is measured against (ER-21; ADR 0098 amendment): the dispatch's `base` (the
      # queue passes the commit of main the train is built on), else origin/main. This workflow has no pull_request trigger. One reader:
      # check::baseline::target_ref (tools/paddock-dev/tests/it/growth_target.rs pins this line and the train-gates one).
      PADDOCK_BASE_REF: ${{ inputs.base || 'origin/main' }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          # C100 reads the register's history (the Gates-date trailers) and the base revision.
          fetch-depth: 0

      # Before the first ./dev of the job (the commands below are ./dev ci run steps).
      - uses: ./.gitea/actions/setup-rust

      - name: Install (yaml for C111, from the root package-lock.json)
        working-directory: .
        run: npm ci --ignore-scripts -w conformance

      - name: Tests
        run: ./dev ci run conformance tests

      # Paddock runs its own conformance checks (plan X9): the `conformance` field of conformance/paddock.ci.json lists them, with the
      # reason each other check is skipped. The checkout above has the full history (C71 compares its baseline with the merge base's).
      - name: Paddock itself (applicable checks)
        run: ./dev ci run conformance paddock

      # ADR 0060, C100: every check the repository defines is run by a reachable CI line, or registered in docs/gates.toml with a
      # reason, an owner and a review date. Rollback: `./dev gates check --warn`. The nightly has a job of its own (nightly.yml).
      - name: C100 (every check runs somewhere)
        working-directory: .
        run: ./dev gates check

      - uses: ./.gitea/actions/sccache-stats
        if: always()

  # Secret scan (.gitea/actions/gitleaks): the tree and the commits this branch adds on top of origin/main. It runs on every change,
  # whatever the plan reaches, because a secret is a leak wherever it is; .gitleaks.toml lists the known fixtures, one entry each.
  gitleaks:
    name: gitleaks (secret scan)
    needs: [plan]
    if: ${{ contains(fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.rerun_jobs || '["gitleaks"]'), 'gitleaks') }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    container:
      image: dev.decryptology.net/decryp7/paddock-ci:v3
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          # The history scan reads origin/main..HEAD.
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: ./.gitea/actions/gitleaks

  # Conformance C99 (ADR 0057 §3, rule 72): no shipped process uses the macOS Keychain. Its own job, planned on its inputs
  # (every Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock under apps/ and crates/, the scanned sources, capabilities, paddock.ci.json, the check's
  # code; tools/paddock-dev/src/plan.rs C99_INPUT), because it needs cargo and the registry (`cargo fetch`, `cargo tree` for both Apple
  # triples) and the conformance job above does not. Every release path runs the same action, scoped to its app.
  c99:
    name: C99 (no Keychain in a macOS build)
    needs: [plan]
    if: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.c99 == 'true' && contains(fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.rerun_jobs || '["c99"]'), 'c99') }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    container:
      image: dev.decryptology.net/decryp7/paddock-ci:v3
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: ./.gitea/actions/keychain

  # The shared CI actions' scripts and the dev and host tools (plan X10, X47): every script runs in a scratch folder with a
  # PATH of shims, so no launchd, systemd, Docker or installed app is touched. New-app templates are covered by scripts/.
  tools:
    name: tools and shared scripts
    needs: [plan]
    if: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.tools == 'true' && contains(fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.rerun_jobs || '["tools"]'), 'tools') }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    container:
      image: dev.decryptology.net/decryp7/paddock-ci:v3
    env:
      # `./dev ci run` runs the job's commands from its project's paddock.ci.json (ADR 0038 §1): a tag or release run builds the tool from source.
      # The read credential is set on the ./dev steps only.
      PADDOCK_DEV_DOWNLOAD: ${{ (inputs.release == true || startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/')) && '0' || '' }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      # Before the first ./dev of the job: it hashes and builds itself with the job's pinned compiler (C119).
      - env:
          PADDOCK_DEV_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.BUILD_INPUTS_TOKEN }}
        uses: ./.gitea/actions/setup-rust

      - env:
          PADDOCK_DEV_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.BUILD_INPUTS_TOKEN }}
        name: Tools
        run: ./dev ci run tools tests

      - env:
          PADDOCK_DEV_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.BUILD_INPUTS_TOKEN }}
        name: new-app templates
        run: ./dev ci run tools scripts

      # The VM start check's evidence parsers and judges (scripts/vm-smoke): a fake guest, no VM.
      - env:
          PADDOCK_DEV_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.BUILD_INPUTS_TOKEN }}
        name: VM start check
        run: ./dev ci run tools vm-smoke

      # The agent hooks' tests (.claude/hooks/*.test.sh, with the rule-55 parity test of places.rs against lib/paddockpaths.py).
      # Report-only (ER-41): registered as `step:tools/hooks` in docs/gates.toml (review_by, first green run id); `./dev gates check`
      # fails when the date passes or when this step blocks. A change under .claude/hooks/, places.rs or docs/known-copies.toml marks this job.
      - env:
          PADDOCK_DEV_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.BUILD_INPUTS_TOKEN }}
        name: Hooks tests (report-only)
        continue-on-error: true
        run: ./dev ci run tools hooks

      # ER-40: a committed SVG is generated from its .drawio and never hand-edited. The check re-exports every diagram with the pinned
      # draw.io (ci-image/Dockerfile: DRAWIO_VERSION) and fails on a difference that is not the host's fonts (scripts/svg-drift.mjs).
      # A diagram or SVG change marks this job through the declared inputs of the planner (tools/paddock-dev/src/plan.rs, DOC_INPUTS).
      - name: draw.io for the SVG drift check
        run: |
          # The image from v3 on has it (system packages belong to the image, not to a job). Until then: the same pinned package, checked
          # by SHA-256 (the Dockerfile's ARGs are the one source) and unpacked beside the job, not installed; its libraries are the image's.
          if command -v drawio >/dev/null 2>&1; then exit 0; fi
          v=$(sed -n 's/^ARG DRAWIO_VERSION=//p' ci-image/Dockerfile | head -n 1)
          sum=$(sed -n 's/^ARG DRAWIO_SHA256_AMD64=//p' ci-image/Dockerfile | head -n 1)
          echo "::notice::the CI image has no draw.io yet (it comes with the next image rebuild, ci-image/README.md); unpacking the pinned $v"
          bash ci-image/fetch-verified.sh "https://github.com/jgraph/drawio-desktop/releases/download/v${v}/drawio-amd64-${v}.deb" "$sum" "$RUNNER_TEMP/drawio.deb" \
            || { echo "::error::could not fetch the pinned draw.io $v (see the line above). Fix: re-run, or check the release still exists and the SHA-256 in ci-image/Dockerfile."; exit 1; }
          dpkg-deb -x "$RUNNER_TEMP/drawio.deb" "$RUNNER_TEMP/drawio" \
            || { echo "::error::unpacking draw.io $v failed. Fix: run dpkg-deb -x on the same file in the paddock-ci image to see why."; exit 1; }
          echo "DRAWIO=$RUNNER_TEMP/drawio/opt/drawio/drawio" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - env:
          PADDOCK_DEV_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.BUILD_INPUTS_TOKEN }}
        name: SVG drift (ER-40)
        run: ./dev ci run tools svg-drift

      - uses: ./.gitea/actions/sccache-stats
        if: always()

  # The Windows test VM tooling (scripts/vm-lock.sh, vm-win.sh, vm-win/) is a macOS tool: its lock and guard-rail tests have seven cases that
  # need sysctl, BSD stat, the keychain and Fusion's lease file, which the Linux `ui` job skips ("not measured on this OS", ER-33). They run
  # here, on the Mac host, against fakes only (no VM, no Fusion). Gated on the `tools` output, which every scripts/ change turns on.
  tools-macos:
    name: VM tooling tests (macOS)
    needs: [plan]
    if: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.tools == 'true' && contains(fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.rerun_jobs || '["tools-macos"]'), 'tools-macos') }}
    runs-on: macos-latest
    env:
      PADDOCK_DEV_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.BUILD_INPUTS_TOKEN }}
      PADDOCK_DEV_DOWNLOAD: ${{ (inputs.release == true || startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/')) && '0' || '' }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      # CARGO_BUILD_JOBS: this runner's share of the host's cores (the tests build and run ./dev).
      - uses: ./.gitea/actions/build-jobs

      - uses: ./.gitea/actions/job-isolation

      - name: VM lock and Windows test VM guard rails
        run: node --test scripts/vm-lock.test.mjs scripts/vm-win.test.mjs scripts/member-gate.test.mjs

      - uses: ./.gitea/actions/job-isolation
        if: always()
        with:
          mode: release

  # `wiki` (tools/wiki, the LLM-wiki lint, log and page tool): its own Cargo workspace; Linux only (it reads text and runs git).
  # Its tests include a lint of this repository's docs/wiki, so the pilot wiki is checked whenever the tool changes.
  wiki:
    name: wiki tool
    needs: [plan]
    if: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.tools == 'true' && contains(fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.rerun_jobs || '["wiki"]'), 'wiki') }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    container:
      image: dev.decryptology.net/decryp7/paddock-ci:v3
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: tools/wiki
        shell: bash
    env:
      # setup-rust runs ./dev (docs/plans/ci-in-rust.md): the read credential, and a tag or release run builds the tool from source.
      PADDOCK_DEV_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.BUILD_INPUTS_TOKEN }}
      PADDOCK_DEV_DOWNLOAD: ${{ (inputs.release == true || startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/')) && '0' || '' }}
      CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
    steps:
      # The whole history: the lint reads the rules on origin/main and on the open rule branches (origin/docs/*).
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          fetch-depth: 0

      # The engineering rules, one more rules source for the copied-text check. Optional: when the runner's token cannot read
      # that repository the step fails softly and the lint skips the missing file.
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        continue-on-error: true
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          repository: decryp7/engineering-rules
          path: engineering-rules

      # A Linux container: one job per host and no kept folders or ports, so no job-isolation slot is taken (the action does
      # nothing there, ADR 0025).
      - uses: ./.gitea/actions/build-jobs

      # No build-folder action: the job is Linux-container only, so the build folder is tools/wiki/target in the container (git-ignored).
      - uses: ./.gitea/actions/setup-rust
        with:
          components: clippy,rustfmt

      # The engineering rules are optional input of the lint; say loudly when they are missing instead of skipping quietly.
      - name: Engineering rules present
        working-directory: .
        run: |
          if [ -f engineering-rules/RULES.md ]; then
            echo "- wiki lint: engineering-rules checked out, so its RULES.md is a rules source" >> "${GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY:-/dev/null}"
          else
            echo "::warning::wiki lint: engineering-rules is not checked out (the runner's token cannot read decryp7/engineering-rules?), so the copied-rule check skips the ER text. Give the job a token that can read it."
            echo "- wiki lint: engineering-rules NOT checked out; the ER text was not a rules source" >> "${GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY:-/dev/null}"
          fi

      - name: Lockfile is current
        run: |
          cargo metadata --locked --format-version 1 > /dev/null || {
            echo "::error::tools/wiki/Cargo.lock is stale, run cargo update -w in tools/wiki and commit it"; exit 1; }

      - name: Format
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && env.PADDOCK_JOB_ABORTED != '1' }}
        run: cargo fmt --check

      - name: Clippy
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && env.PADDOCK_JOB_ABORTED != '1' }}
        run: cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings

      - name: Tests
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && env.PADDOCK_JOB_ABORTED != '1' }}
        run: cargo nextest run --profile ci --locked --no-fail-fast

      - name: Deny
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && env.PADDOCK_JOB_ABORTED != '1' }}
        run: cargo deny check

      # The tool lints the wiki the way a person runs it (stale pages only warn).
      - name: Lint the wiki
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && env.PADDOCK_JOB_ABORTED != '1' }}
        env:
          # The run log in the workspace, not the container's home, so a failed run's log survives the job (uploaded below).
          WIKI_LOG_DIR: ${{ github.workspace }}/wiki-logs
        run: |
          # The summary line is written whether the lint passes or fails; the step then ends with the lint's own exit code.
          set +e
          cargo run --locked -- --repo ../.. lint --er ../../engineering-rules/RULES.md 2>&1 | tee wiki-lint.out
          rc=${PIPESTATUS[0]}
          echo "- wiki lint (exit $rc): $(tail -1 wiki-lint.out)" >> "${GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY:-/dev/null}"
          exit "$rc"

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@ff15f0306b3f739f7b6fd43fb5d26cd321bd4de5 # v3
        if: failure()
        with:
          name: wiki-logs
          path: wiki-logs
          if-no-files-found: ignore

      # The tools build with a plain Rust toolchain: no GTK -sys crate may reach them through the shared crates (the workspace
      # hack once pulled gtk-sys into paddock-proc on x86_64 Linux, so `cargo install` of wiki and heavy needed GTK headers). The
      # check reads the dependency graph for the Linux target, so it holds on an image that happens to have GTK installed.
      - name: No GTK in the tools' Linux build
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && env.PADDOCK_JOB_ABORTED != '1' }}
        working-directory: .
        run: |
          # bash -e -o pipefail: every command that may legitimately fail is handled by hand. grep exits 1 when it finds nothing,
          # which is the success case here.
          rc=0
          for tool in wiki heavy; do
            tree=$(cd "tools/$tool" && cargo tree --locked --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu -e normal,build --prefix none) || {
              echo "::error::cargo tree failed for tools/$tool (see the lines above). Run it in tools/$tool with the same arguments."
              rc=1; continue; }
            # ER-33: the probe must be able to see the thing. Both tools link paddock-proc, where the hack's GTK crates arrived.
            echo "$tree" | grep -q '^paddock-proc ' || {
              echo "::error::check broken: the dependency graph of tools/$tool has no paddock-proc, so a GTK crate there would not be seen."
              rc=1; continue; }
            hits=$(echo "$tree" | grep -E '^(gtk|gdk|gio|glib|gobject|pango|cairo|atk|gdk-pixbuf|soup|webkit2gtk|javascriptcore-rs)[a-z0-9-]*-(sys|sys-rs) ' | sort -u || true)
            if [ -n "$hits" ]; then
              echo "::error::tools/$tool depends on GTK -sys crates on x86_64 Linux: $(echo "$hits" | tr '\n' ' '). Add them to crates/.config/hakari.toml traversal-excludes, run cargo hakari generate and refresh the lockfiles."
              rc=1
            else
              echo "tools/$tool: no GTK -sys crate in the x86_64 Linux graph"
            fi
          done
          exit "$rc"

      - uses: ./.gitea/actions/sccache-stats
        if: always()

  # The heavy tool (tools/heavy): the machine-wide heavy-step lock. Its own Cargo workspace; a Linux container, so no build-folder action
  # (the build folder is tools/heavy/target in the container, git-ignored).
  heavy:
    name: heavy tool
    needs: [plan]
    if: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.tools == 'true' && contains(fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.rerun_jobs || '["heavy"]'), 'heavy') }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    container:
      image: dev.decryptology.net/decryp7/paddock-ci:v3
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: tools/heavy
        shell: bash
    env:
      # setup-rust runs ./dev (docs/plans/ci-in-rust.md): the read credential, and a tag or release run builds the tool from source.
      PADDOCK_DEV_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.BUILD_INPUTS_TOKEN }}
      PADDOCK_DEV_DOWNLOAD: ${{ (inputs.release == true || startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/')) && '0' || '' }}
      CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: ./.gitea/actions/build-jobs

      - uses: ./.gitea/actions/setup-rust
        with:
          components: clippy,rustfmt

      - name: Lockfile is current
        run: |
          cargo metadata --locked --format-version 1 > /dev/null || {
            echo "::error::tools/heavy/Cargo.lock is stale, run cargo update -w in tools/heavy and commit it"; exit 1; }

      - name: Format
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && env.PADDOCK_JOB_ABORTED != '1' }}
        run: cargo fmt --check

      - name: Clippy
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && env.PADDOCK_JOB_ABORTED != '1' }}
        run: cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings

      - name: Tests
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && env.PADDOCK_JOB_ABORTED != '1' }}
        run: cargo nextest run --profile ci --locked --no-fail-fast

      - name: Deny
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && env.PADDOCK_JOB_ABORTED != '1' }}
        run: cargo deny check

      - uses: ./.gitea/actions/sccache-stats
        if: always()

  # The family icons (icons/): the pipeline's tests (seam scan, coverage, tray shapes, .icns frames, docs copies) and the check that every
  # installed copy in the apps and the docs equals the build. Without the second step a hand edit of an app's icons goes unnoticed.
  icons:
    name: icons (tests, installed copies)
    needs: [plan]
    if: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.icons == 'true' && contains(fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.rerun_jobs || '["icons"]'), 'icons') }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    container:
      image: dev.decryptology.net/decryp7/paddock-ci:v3
    env:
      # `./dev ci run` runs the job's commands from its project's paddock.ci.json (ADR 0038 §1): a tag or release run builds the tool from source.
      # The read credential is set on the ./dev steps only.
      PADDOCK_DEV_DOWNLOAD: ${{ (inputs.release == true || startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/')) && '0' || '' }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      # Before the first ./dev of the job: it hashes and builds itself with the job's pinned compiler (C119).
      - env:
          PADDOCK_DEV_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.BUILD_INPUTS_TOKEN }}
        uses: ./.gitea/actions/setup-rust

      - uses: ./.gitea/actions/node-caches

      - name: Install
        run: npm ci

      - env:
          PADDOCK_DEV_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.BUILD_INPUTS_TOKEN }}
        name: Icon tests
        run: ./dev ci run icons tests

      - env:
          PADDOCK_DEV_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.BUILD_INPUTS_TOKEN }}
        name: Installed icon copies match the build
        run: ./dev ci run icons installed

      - uses: ./.gitea/actions/sccache-stats
        if: always()

  # @decryp7/paddock-eslint (eslint/, plan X11): RuleTester cases per rule and the preset run through ESLint on temp files.
  eslint-preset:
    name: eslint preset (rules 27 to 39)
    needs: [plan]
    if: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.eslint == 'true' && contains(fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.rerun_jobs || '["eslint-preset"]'), 'eslint-preset') }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    container:
      image: dev.decryptology.net/decryp7/paddock-ci:v3
    env:
      # `./dev ci run` runs the job's commands from its project's paddock.ci.json (ADR 0038 §1): a tag or release run builds the tool from source.
      # The read credential is set on the ./dev steps only.
      PADDOCK_DEV_DOWNLOAD: ${{ (inputs.release == true || startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/')) && '0' || '' }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      # Before the first ./dev of the job: it hashes and builds itself with the job's pinned compiler (C119).
      - env:
          PADDOCK_DEV_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.BUILD_INPUTS_TOKEN }}
        uses: ./.gitea/actions/setup-rust

      - uses: ./.gitea/actions/node-caches
        with:
          angular-dir: ''

      - name: Install
        working-directory: .
        run: npm ci

      - env:
          PADDOCK_DEV_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.BUILD_INPUTS_TOKEN }}
        run: ./dev ci run eslint tests

      - uses: ./.gitea/actions/sccache-stats
        if: always()

  crates:
    name: crates (fmt, workspace hack, unused deps, coverage, deny)
    needs: [plan]
    if: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.crates == 'true' && contains(fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.rerun_jobs || '["crates"]'), 'crates') }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    container:
      image: dev.decryptology.net/decryp7/paddock-ci:v3
    env:
      # setup-rust runs ./dev (docs/plans/ci-in-rust.md): the read credential, and a tag or release run builds the tool from source.
      PADDOCK_DEV_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.BUILD_INPUTS_TOKEN }}
      PADDOCK_DEV_DOWNLOAD: ${{ (inputs.release == true || startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/')) && '0' || '' }}
      # The job runs as root in the container, where Chromium refuses to start with its sandbox (the real-browser test of
      # paddock-chromium); the driver drops the sandbox only for root AND with this opt-in.
      PADDOCK_BROWSER_NO_SANDBOX: "1"
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: ./.gitea/actions/setup-rust
      - run: ./dev ci run crates fmt

      # cargo-hakari and cargo-machete come with the image (ci-image/).
      # One feature set per dependency (docs/dev-setup.md): the workspace-hack crate is current and every member uses it.
      - name: Workspace hack up to date
        run: ./dev ci run crates hakari

      # Unused dependencies. A false report goes into `ignored` of [workspace.metadata.cargo-machete] (Cargo.toml) or of the
      # crate's own [package.metadata.cargo-machete], with the reason; the workspace-hack crate is depended on for features.
      - name: Unused dependencies
        run: ./dev ci run crates machete

      # Merged line coverage over all test binaries, adapters included (the per-binary summary counts unused generic instances).
      # Native glue files are left out (crates/README.md: never logic, reviewed by hand), and so are paddock-proc's test child (a
      # re-executed test binary that its parent ends with SIGKILL, so its coverage data is never written) and paddock-ipc's (the same); paddock-ipc's endpoint/{unix,windows}.rs are
      # its native glue (OS error paths; the portable surface in endpoint/mod.rs is covered). paddock-chromium's fake browser
      # runs in re-executed test binaries that are often ended by force (no coverage data), like paddock-proc's test child.
      # paddock-dialogs' `probe.rs` (feature `probe`) is the ADR 0026 section 6 real-window harness: it opens real webview windows and
      # runs only where there is a window system (PADDOCK_REAL_WINDOWS=1: the `dialog-window-probe` job), so no ordinary test reaches it.
      # The gate (scripts/coverage-gate.mjs) leaves out only the `#[tauri::command]` attribute lines: llvm-cov charges every
      # region of the macro's generated wrapper to that line, which no test can all reach.
      # This is also Linux's all-features test run (the crate leg skips its own on Linux): the real-browser tests of
      # paddock-chromium must find the image's Chrome for Testing instead of skipping.
      - name: Coverage (>= 90 % lines; 99 % security target report-only)
        env:
          PADDOCK_REQUIRE_TEST_BROWSER: "1"
        run: ./dev ci run crates coverage
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@ff15f0306b3f739f7b6fd43fb5d26cd321bd4de5 # v3
        if: failure()
        with:
          name: crates-lcov
          path: crates/lcov.info
          if-no-files-found: ignore
      # The container runs as root and the orphan guardian is off for root: run its acting tests as an unprivileged user
      # (ADR 0076 amendment 2026-11-09; ./dev ci guardian-as-user prints one ::error:: per failure; the shell stays behind conformance/ci/kit.sh for tag runs).
      - name: Orphan guardian as a user (Linux)
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && env.PADDOCK_JOB_ABORTED != '1' && runner.os == 'Linux' }}
        working-directory: crates
        run: bash ../conformance/ci/kit.sh host guardian-as-user
      - run: ./dev ci run crates deny
      - uses: ./.gitea/actions/sccache-stats
        if: always()

  # Every crate on Linux, Windows and macOS (platform-only bugs exist: lessons): clippy and tests with every feature, so the
  # `tauri` adapters are built too, the feature-off runs and the doc tests, as a few workspace-wide steps. On Linux the
  # all-features test run is the coverage job's (crates), so this leg runs only what that job does not.
  crate:
    name: crate (${{ matrix.os }})
    needs: [plan]
    if: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.crates == 'true' && contains(fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.rerun_jobs || '["crate"]'), 'crate') }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        # Every OS; a rerun of a run's failures (since_run) only the failed legs, each with the filter of its failed tests.
        include: ${{ fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.crate_legs) }}
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    # Linux runs in the paddock-ci image (Rust, Tauri's libraries, Node, Playwright, Chrome for Testing, cargo-nextest baked in); Windows and
    # macOS run on the host.
    container: ${{ matrix.os == 'ubuntu-latest' && 'dev.decryptology.net/decryp7/paddock-ci:v3' || '' }}
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: crates
        shell: bash
    env:
      # A run for a tag builds the tool from source (ADR 0022: release and tag jobs bypass every cache); other runs may download it.
      PADDOCK_DEV_DOWNLOAD: ${{ (inputs.release == true || startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/')) && '0' || '' }}
      # Read credential for ./dev's prebuilt download (ADR 0022 R0b), only in the jobs that run ./dev (job-isolation).
      PADDOCK_DEV_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.BUILD_INPUTS_TOKEN }}
      CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
      # Root in the Linux container: Chromium needs the opt-in to start without its sandbox (ignored when not root).
      PADDOCK_BROWSER_NO_SANDBOX: "1"
    steps:
      # Linux: the whole tree in the container. Hosts: only the bootstrap folders (the actions, their scripts, paddock-dev's inputs)
      # as a partial clone; the kept-clone step below brings the slot's own clone to this commit (conformance/ci/checkout-profiles.txt).
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'

      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        if: runner.os != 'Linux'
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          sparse-checkout: |
            .cargo
            .gitea
            conformance
            scripts
            tools
            crates
          filter: blob:none

      # Host-mode Windows runner: Git's bash on PATH (`shell: bash` needs it).
      - name: Git bash on PATH (Windows)
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
        shell: cmd
        working-directory: .
        run: |
          if not exist "%ProgramFiles%\Git\bin\bash.exe" (echo Git for Windows is not installed on this runner & exit /b 1)
          echo %ProgramFiles%\Git\bin>>"%GITHUB_PATH%"

      # CARGO_BUILD_JOBS: this runner's share of the host's cores (before job-isolation, which builds paddock-dev).
      - uses: ./.gitea/actions/build-jobs

      # A slot of the host (job isolation; after Git bash on Windows): the job's kept folders end in its slot and its temp
      # folders are the runner's per-job folder, so concurrent jobs on one host never share either.
      - uses: ./.gitea/actions/job-isolation

      # The test browser outside the checkout, the slot's kept folder (the installer stamps the
      # pinned version in it).
      - name: Test browser folder (macOS, Windows)
        if: runner.os != 'Linux'
        working-directory: .
        run: |
          dir="$(bash conformance/ci/kit.sh isolation path browser paddock)"
          if command -v cygpath >/dev/null; then dir="$(cygpath -w "$dir")"; fi
          echo "PADDOCK_TEST_BROWSER_DIR=$dir" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      # Host runners check out into a per-job hashed folder; sccache keys a compile on its folder, so the workspace crates miss
      # on every run. Build from the same physical path every time: PADDOCK_WORKSPACE, the steps' working-directory, is the slot's
      # kept clone at this commit (kept-clone: a fetch of what changed, a clean tree, no screenshots; macOS: the work folder is
      # a link to it; Windows, where act keeps the work folder open: the work folder stays the bootstrap, so every read of the
      # tree goes through PADDOCK_WORKSPACE). On Windows the step comes after the one that puts Git's bash on PATH (before it,
      # `shell: bash` finds WSL's bash.exe).
      - uses: ./.gitea/actions/kept-clone
        if: runner.os != 'Linux'
        with:
          name: paddock-checkout-${{ runner.os }}
          profile: lean

      # A build folder that outlives the job on the hosts (the work folder does not: it is hashed per job), crates/target in
      # the container, as cargo configuration (crates/.cargo/ci.toml, included by crates/.cargo/config.toml), never
      # CARGO_TARGET_DIR: sccache puts every CARGO_* variable into its cache key (the shared build-folder action).
      - uses: ./.gitea/actions/build-folder
        with:
          workspace: ${{ env.PADDOCK_WORKSPACE || github.workspace }}/crates
          name: paddock-${{ github.job }}

      # Toolchain and sccache on every OS: sccache's local disk cache (host runners: the job slot's kept folder sccache-s<n>,
      # containers: the /sccache mount).
      - uses: ./.gitea/actions/setup-rust
        with:
          components: clippy

      - name: Toolchain present
        run: |
          rustc --version && cargo --version
          cargo clippy --version || { echo "::error::clippy is missing on this runner (rustup component add clippy)"; exit 1; }

      # The pinned cargo-nextest: the image's on Linux, a copy in the hosts' shared kept folder tools (downloaded once
      # per version); the step fails when the runner has another version.
      - uses: ./.gitea/actions/host-tools

      # Whole-workspace steps: one build per feature set instead of one per crate (each `-p X --all-features` resolved its own
      # features and rebuilt the shared dependencies). Every step runs even after another failed; nextest and clippy name
      # the crate of every failure. scripts/publish.test.mjs and conformance C37 fail when a workspace member is left out.
      # A leg with a filter (a rerun of failed tests) runs only the test steps below: its other steps passed in the earlier run.
      - name: Clippy (workspace, every feature)
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && env.PADDOCK_JOB_ABORTED != '1' && !matrix.filter }}
        working-directory: ${{ env.PADDOCK_WORKSPACE || github.workspace }}/crates
        run: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings

      # The build chromium.toml pins, on the host runners (the Linux image has it): checked against its SHA-256 and kept in a
      # folder that outlives the job, so it is downloaded once per pin. Sets CHROMIUM_TEST_PATH.
      - name: Chrome for Testing (macOS, Windows)
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && env.PADDOCK_JOB_ABORTED != '1' && runner.os != 'Linux' }}
        uses: ./.gitea/actions/install-test-browser
        with:
          catalogue: ${{ env.PADDOCK_WORKSPACE || github.workspace }}/crates/paddock-chromium/src/chromium.toml
          env-prefix: PADDOCK
          dir: ${{ env.PADDOCK_TEST_BROWSER_DIR }}

      # Every crate's tests with every feature, so the `tauri` adapters are built and tested too (the dialogs and panels on the
      # mock runtime, paddock-chromium against its fake browser and against Chrome for Testing: CHROMIUM_TEST_PATH, never an
      # installed browser, rule 7; a missing browser fails instead of skipping). On Linux the coverage job (crates) runs
      # exactly this run under llvm-cov, so this leg does not run it twice.
      - name: Tests (workspace, every feature)
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && env.PADDOCK_JOB_ABORTED != '1' && runner.os != 'Linux' }}
        working-directory: ${{ env.PADDOCK_WORKSPACE || github.workspace }}/crates
        env:
          PADDOCK_REQUIRE_TEST_BROWSER: "1"
          # Chrome's verbose log of each real-browser test on Windows, kept below when the job fails (ADR 0030: why the
          # network service went away is only in there).
          PADDOCK_TEST_BROWSER_LOG: ${{ runner.os == 'Windows' && format('{0}/chrome-logs', runner.temp) || '' }}
          FILTER: ${{ matrix.filter }}
        run: |
          filter=()
          if [ -n "$FILTER" ]; then echo "::notice::nextest reruns only the failed tests: $FILTER"; filter=(-E "$FILTER" --no-tests=warn); fi
          cargo nextest run --workspace --all-features --profile ci ${filter[@]+"${filter[@]}"}

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@ff15f0306b3f739f7b6fd43fb5d26cd321bd4de5 # v3
        if: failure() && runner.os == 'Windows'
        with:
          name: chrome-logs-${{ runner.os }}
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/chrome-logs
          if-no-files-found: ignore

      # The crates whose code changes with an optional feature off (cfg(not(feature)) paths, a default feature that can be
      # turned off) also run without it. Cargo unifies features across the packages of one run, so a crate that another
      # selected crate depends on with a feature on gets its own run: paddock-shell turns on paddock-diag's, paddock-download's
      # and paddock-updater's `tauri`, and paddock-updater turns on paddock-download's default `http`.
      - name: Tests with the optional features off
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && env.PADDOCK_JOB_ABORTED != '1' && !matrix.filter }}
        working-directory: ${{ env.PADDOCK_WORKSPACE || github.workspace }}/crates
        run: |
          cargo nextest run -p paddock-shell -p paddock-secrets -p paddock-siblings --profile ci
          cargo nextest run -p paddock-diag -p paddock-updater --profile ci
          cargo nextest run -p paddock-download --no-default-features --profile ci
          # paddock-repo-graph's git and cargo adapters sit behind features that only paddock-dev (its own workspace) turns on;
          # its default build, without them, is the one Pacenotes uses.
          cargo nextest run -p paddock-repo-graph --profile ci

      # nextest (and so the coverage job) does not run doc tests.
      - name: Doc tests (workspace, every feature)
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && env.PADDOCK_JOB_ABORTED != '1' && !matrix.filter }}
        working-directory: ${{ env.PADDOCK_WORKSPACE || github.workspace }}/crates
        run: cargo test --workspace --all-features --doc

      - uses: ./.gitea/actions/sccache-stats
        if: always()

      - uses: ./.gitea/actions/job-isolation
        if: always()
        with:
          mode: release

  # Conventional Commits and no AI attribution (rules 4, 8) for every commit of a change, whichever project it touches.
  # Only the commits a change adds are linted (./dev plan commit_lint_range): a push `before..sha`, a manual run from the
  # plan's base. On a push to main that is `--first-parent`: only the commits main
  # itself gets (the landing merge, a direct commit), not the ones a merge brought in. A branch's commits are linted by the
  # integrator before landing (`commit-lint --range origin/main..<branch>`, docs/rules.md rule 50(g)); C23 in the conformance
  # run is the backstop for a branch that landed without that. Tags and an app's tag gates skip it (ER-15).
  commits:
    name: commit messages
    needs: [plan]
    if: ${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch') && contains(fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.rerun_jobs || '["commits"]'), 'commits') }}
