      - name: Fresh npm cache and no kept Angular cache on a tag
        if: ${{ startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/') }}
        working-directory: ${{ env.PADDOCK_WORKSPACE || github.workspace }}
        run: bash conformance/ci/tag-node-caches.sh apps/debrief/app

      - name: libduckdb
        working-directory: ${{ env.PADDOCK_WORKSPACE || github.workspace }}/apps/debrief
        run: bash scripts/ci/libduckdb-env.sh

      # Not on a tag (rule 78): the kept node_modules is written by branch runs. A tag removes a junction a killed job left
      # (only the link, never its target) and the build step runs a fresh npm ci.
      - name: Reuse node_modules for this lockfile (Windows)
        if: ${{ runner.os == 'Windows' && !startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/') }}
        working-directory: ${{ env.PADDOCK_WORKSPACE || github.workspace }}
        run: bash apps/debrief/scripts/ci/windows-node-modules.sh link

      - name: No kept node_modules on a tag (Windows)
        if: ${{ runner.os == 'Windows' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/') }}
        working-directory: ${{ env.PADDOCK_WORKSPACE || github.workspace }}
        run: bash apps/debrief/scripts/ci/windows-node-modules.sh unlink

      # No cargo-about and no notices regeneration here: the licences job fails when the committed notices
      # (app/src-tauri/resources, app/src/app/about/generated) are out of date, and a release needs that job.

      # Signed updater artifacts (docs/releasing.md): with the signing secrets set, Tauri writes a .sig next to
      # every installer (v2 updater artifacts: the installers themselves, plus Debrief.app.tar.gz on macOS; never
      # v1 zips) and the public key is built into the app. Without them (forks, pull requests) the app has no
      # update key and reports "updates are not available in this build".
      - name: Build installers
        working-directory: ${{ env.PADDOCK_WORKSPACE || github.workspace }}/apps/debrief/app
        env:
          # One updater key for the family (ADR 0014, amendment): every release is signed with the shared key only. Copies
          # installed before the move cannot verify it and are reinstalled once by hand (the release notes say so).
          # The private key and its password reach this step on a debrief-v* release tag only (ADR 0085 D7, rule 78); any other
          # run signs with a throw-away key made in the job, and inside the step only `tauri build` sees a key, in its environment
          # (conformance/ci/updater-key.sh). The UI and sidecar builds (beforeBuildCommand) run first, without it.
          TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY: ${{ startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/debrief-v') && secrets.PADDOCK_TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY || '' }}
          TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD: ${{ startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/debrief-v') && secrets.PADDOCK_TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD || '' }}
          TAURI_UPDATER_PUBKEY: ${{ secrets.PADDOCK_TAURI_UPDATER_PUBKEY }}
          # Installers use the size-optimised `dist` profile (thin LTO, one codegen unit, stripped); the sidecars match.
          DEBRIEF_CARGO_PROFILE: dist
        run: |
          # The key leaves the environment before npm ci (its install scripts are branch code); updater-key.sh strips both
          # keys of whitespace (strip-keys.mjs) and fails a run that is not a tag but has the private key.
          source ../../../conformance/ci/updater-key.sh
          updater_key_take
          # A tag installs fresh (rule 78): never a node_modules an earlier run left in a kept checkout.
          case "$GITHUB_REF" in
            refs/tags/*) (cd ../../.. && npm ci) ;;
            *) [ -d ../../../node_modules ] || (cd ../../.. && npm ci) ;;
          esac
          # The app imports the shared library from ui/dist (tsconfig paths), which the app build (beforeBuildCommand) needs. It runs
          # here, after updater_key_take, so no key is in its environment.
          (cd ../../.. && npm run build -w ui)
          updater_key_throwaway .
          # Host runners keep their build folder between runs: drop old installers so an earlier version's (signed)
          # installer can never be collected into this release.
          target="$PADDOCK_BUILD_FOLDER"
          if command -v cygpath >/dev/null; then target="$(cygpath -u "$target")"; fi
          rm -rf "$target/dist/bundle"
          bundles='${{ matrix.bundles }}'
          mkdir -p ../target
          extra=()
          # NSIS (Windows): the pinned NSIS tools in <build folder>/.tauri, useLocalToolsDir, checked after the build (ADR 0085 WP-9).
          case ",$bundles," in *,nsis,* | *,appimage,*)
            node ../../../conformance/ci/tauri-tools.mjs install --bundles "$bundles" --src-tauri src-tauri
            echo '{"bundle":{"useLocalToolsDir":true}}' > ../target/tools.conf.json
            extra=(--config ../target/tools.conf.json) ;;
          esac
          # Ad-hoc builds ship WITHOUT the hardened runtime (tauri.macos.conf.json): with it, library validation refuses the
          # bundled libduckdb even after an ad-hoc re-sign (docs/releasing.md). A Developer ID build turns it back on.
          if [ "$RUNNER_OS" = macOS ] && [ -n "${APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY:-}" ] && [ "$APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY" != "-" ]; then
            echo '{"bundle":{"macOS":{"hardenedRuntime":true}}}' > ../target/hardened.conf.json
            extra=(${extra[@]+"${extra[@]}"} --config ../target/hardened.conf.json)
          fi
          if [ "$updater_key_signing" = true ]; then
            # macOS updates install from the .app bundle's archive.
            if [ "$RUNNER_OS" = macOS ]; then bundles="app,$bundles"; fi
            TAURI_UPDATER_PUBKEY="$updater_pubkey" node -e 'process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify({ bundle: { createUpdaterArtifacts: true }, plugins: { updater: { pubkey: process.env.TAURI_UPDATER_PUBKEY } } }))' > ../target/updater.conf.json
            extra=(--config ../target/updater.conf.json ${extra[@]+"${extra[@]}"})
          else
            echo '::warning::No updater signing secrets: this build cannot update itself.'
          fi
          # The UI and sidecar builds (beforeBuildCommand, merged with tauri.sidecars.conf.json) run here without the key;
          # tauri build gets a configuration that empties the hook (ADR 0085 D7).
          node ../../../conformance/ci/before-build.mjs --app-dir . --config src-tauri/tauri.sidecars.conf.json
          echo '{"build":{"beforeBuildCommand":null}}' > ../target/no-hook.conf.json
          # The key is in the environment of this one command only, never in its arguments (updater_key_exec).
          updater_key_exec npx tauri build --bundles "$bundles" --config src-tauri/tauri.sidecars.conf.json ${extra[@]+"${extra[@]}"} --config ../target/no-hook.conf.json -- --profile dist
          case ",$bundles," in *,nsis,* | *,appimage,*) node ../../../conformance/ci/tauri-tools.mjs check --bundles "$bundles" --src-tauri src-tauri ;; esac
          # Every updater signature verifies against the one public key this build carries.
          if [ "$updater_key_signing" = true ]; then
            sigdir="$target/dist/bundle"
            if command -v cygpath >/dev/null; then sigdir="$(cygpath -m "$sigdir")"; fi
            node ../../../conformance/release/updater-key-check.mjs --pubkey "$updater_pubkey" --dir "$sigdir"
          fi

      # ADR 0032: no binary the installer carries (the app, its sidecars, duckdb.dll, named by the Tauri configuration) imports
      # the VC++ runtime; the runner has the redistributable, a user's PC may not.
      - name: Shipped binaries need no VC++ runtime (Windows)
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
        working-directory: ${{ env.PADDOCK_WORKSPACE || github.workspace }}
        run: |
          # Node on Windows reads C:/... paths, not Git Bash's /c/...
          dir="$PADDOCK_BUILD_FOLDER"
          if command -v cygpath >/dev/null; then dir="$(cygpath -m "$dir")"; fi
          node conformance/release/windows-crt-imports.mjs --src-tauri apps/debrief/app/src-tauri --bin-dir "$dir/dist" \
            --config apps/debrief/app/src-tauri/tauri.sidecars.conf.json

      # The packaged store worker finds libduckdb by run path (crates/debrief-store-worker/build/rpath.rs): a signed,
      # notarized macOS app ignores DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH. Unpack the package and check that one of the worker's run paths
      # reaches the packaged library, so a change to the bundle layout cannot ship a worker that fails to start.
      - name: Packaged store worker finds libduckdb by run path (Linux, macOS)
        if: runner.os != 'Windows'
        working-directory: ${{ env.PADDOCK_WORKSPACE || github.workspace }}/apps/debrief
        run: |
          bundle="$PADDOCK_BUILD_FOLDER/dist/bundle"
          if [ "$RUNNER_OS" = Linux ]; then
            deb=$(find "$bundle/deb" -name '*.deb' | head -n 1)
            tree=$(mktemp -d)
            dpkg-deb -x "$deb" "$tree"
            bin="$tree/usr/bin/debrief-store-worker"; lib=libduckdb.so; origin='$ORIGIN'
            readelf -d "$bin" | grep -E 'R(UN)?PATH' || true
            paths=$(readelf -d "$bin" | sed -n 's/.*(R\(UN\)\{0,1\}PATH).*\[\(.*\)\]/\2/p')
          else
            app=$(find "$bundle/macos" -maxdepth 1 -name '*.app' | head -n 1)
            bin="$app/Contents/MacOS/debrief-store-worker"; lib=libduckdb.dylib; origin='@executable_path'
            otool -L "$bin" | grep duckdb
            paths=$(otool -l "$bin" | awk '/cmd LC_RPATH/ { getline; getline; print $2 }' | paste -sd: -)
          fi
          echo "run paths of $bin: $paths"
          found=
          IFS=: read -ra entries <<< "$paths"
          for p in "${entries[@]}"; do
            p="${p/"$origin"/$(dirname "$bin")}"
            if [ -f "$p/$lib" ]; then found="$p/$lib"; break; fi
          done
          if [ -z "$found" ]; then
            echo "::error::none of the packaged store worker's run paths ($paths) holds $lib"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "the worker loads $found"

      # signingIdentity "-" (tauri.macos.conf.json) must leave an ad-hoc sealed .app, in the bundle and in the DMG:
      # a linker-signed one is reported as "damaged" on a quarantined download.
      # Also checks every nested Mach-O's Team ID against the app's and runs the packaged store worker's --self-test
      # (opens and reopens a tiny store) and the plugin host from the bundle, so dyld's library validation is exercised.
      - name: Verify the .app and the DMG are ad-hoc sealed and load (macOS)
        if: runner.os == 'macOS'
        working-directory: ${{ env.PADDOCK_WORKSPACE || github.workspace }}/apps/debrief
        run: bash scripts/ci/macos-verify-bundle.sh

      - name: Collect installers
        working-directory: ${{ env.PADDOCK_WORKSPACE || github.workspace }}/apps/debrief
        run: |
          mkdir -p dist
          dir="$PADDOCK_BUILD_FOLDER"
          # Git bash on Windows: turn C:/... into a path find understands.
          if command -v cygpath >/dev/null; then dir="$(cygpath -u "$dir")"; fi
          find "$dir/dist/bundle" -type f \( -name '*.deb' -o -name '*.rpm' -o -name '*-setup.exe' -o -name '*.dmg' -o -name '*.app.tar.gz' -o -name '*.sig' \) -exec cp {} dist/ \;
          ls -la dist
          # Every versioned installer must carry this build's version (the .app.tar.gz has none in its name).
          version="$(node -p "require('./app/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json').version")"
          stale="$(ls dist | grep -E '_[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' | grep -v "_${version}_" || true)"
          if [ -n "$stale" ]; then echo "::error::Installers from another version: $stale"; exit 1; fi

      # Gitea Actions supports upload/download-artifact v3.
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v3
        with:
          name: debrief-${{ runner.os }}
          path: ${{ env.PADDOCK_WORKSPACE || github.workspace }}/apps/debrief/dist/*
          if-no-files-found: error

      - name: Unlink the shared node_modules (Windows)
        if: always() && runner.os == 'Windows'
        working-directory: ${{ env.PADDOCK_WORKSPACE || github.workspace }}
        run: bash apps/debrief/scripts/ci/windows-node-modules.sh unlink

      - uses: ./.gitea/actions/sccache-stats
        if: always()

      # The slot goes back last, after everything that uses its folders and its sccache port.
      - uses: ./.gitea/actions/job-isolation
        if: always()
        with:
          mode: release

  # Conformance C99 (ADR 0057 §3.4, rule 72): the shared keychain action, scoped to Debrief and crates/ (ER-31); the release
  # waits for it. Tags and manual runs only; ci.yml's c99 job covers pull requests, main and the nightly.
  keychain:
    name: C99 (no Keychain in a macOS build)
    needs: [plan]
    if: (startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/debrief-v') || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch') && contains(fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.rerun_jobs || '["keychain"]'), 'keychain')
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    container:
      image: dev.decryptology.net/decryp7/paddock-ci:v3
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: ./.gitea/actions/keychain
        with:
          scope: apps/debrief

  release:
    name: release
    if: needs.plan.outputs.run == 'true' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/debrief-v')
    needs: [plan, bundle, tauri-smoke, rust-lint, rust-test, rust-test-macos, plugin-sdk, licences, frontend, e2e, keychain]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    container:
      image: dev.decryptology.net/decryp7/paddock-ci:v3
    env:
      # A release job: ./dev ci steps never download a stored tool binary here (conformance/ci/kit.sh keeps the shell scripts too).
      PADDOCK_DEV_DOWNLOAD: "0"
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      # CARGO_BUILD_JOBS: this runner's share of the host (`./dev ci build-jobs` through conformance/ci/kit.sh; Linux keeps cargo's default).
      - uses: ./.gitea/actions/build-jobs

      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v3
        with:
          path: apps/debrief/artifacts

      # git-cliff comes with the image.
      - name: Release notes (git-cliff)
        run: |
          command -v git-cliff >/dev/null || cargo install git-cliff --locked
          # Debrief's commits and the shared ones it ships (ADR 0014 §4), between its own debrief-v* tags.
          git cliff -r ../.. --config cliff.toml --tag-pattern 'debrief-v.*' --include-path 'apps/debrief/**' \
            --include-path 'crates/**' --include-path 'ui/**' --latest --strip header -o artifacts/RELEASE_NOTES.md
          # Not signed or notarized yet (decision 2026-10-23): every release explains the first launch. Copies installed
          # before the move to the monorepo cannot verify the family's updater key: they are reinstalled once by hand.
          cat >> artifacts/RELEASE_NOTES.md <<'FIRST_LAUNCH'

          ### First launch

          Debrief is not code-signed yet, so your system may warn the first time you open it.

          - **Existing installs:** download this version once by hand and install it over the old one. Copies installed before Debrief moved to the Paddock repository cannot update themselves to it; later versions update as usual.
          - **macOS:** first drag Debrief from the disk image to Applications and open it from there. The first time, macOS says "“Debrief” Not Opened": choose **Done** (not Move to Trash). Open System Settings > Privacy & Security, scroll down to "“Debrief” was blocked to protect your Mac." and choose **Open Anyway**. macOS asks once more, "Open “Debrief”?": choose **Open Anyway** again, then enter an administrator's name and password. You do this once; later starts open normally. If the button is missing, open Debrief again first.
          - **Windows:** if SmartScreen says "Windows protected your PC", choose **More info > Run anyway**.
          FIRST_LAUNCH

      # cargo-cyclonedx comes with the image.
      - name: SBOMs (CycloneDX)
        run: |
          command -v cargo-cyclonedx >/dev/null || cargo install cargo-cyclonedx --locked
          cargo cyclonedx --manifest-path app/src-tauri/Cargo.toml --format json --override-filename debrief-rust.cdx
          cp app/src-tauri/debrief-rust.cdx.json artifacts/
          (cd ../.. && npm ci && npx --yes @cyclonedx/cyclonedx-npm --workspace debrief-app --omit dev --output-file apps/debrief/artifacts/debrief-ui.cdx.json)

.gitea/workflows/tag.yml

# Release tags are made here (ER-15, rule 9): an agent or a person requests a tag, this workflow checks the commit and the release
# bot pushes it. Tag protection (pattern * allowing only release-bot) is switched on by the repository's owner, so a tag pushed by
# hand is refused by the server.
#
# THIS IS A GUARD RAIL AGAINST MISTAKES, NOT A SECURITY BOUNDARY. Any repository writer can dispatch a workflow from their own
# ref, and repository secrets reach every non-fork run, so a hostile writer could read RELEASE_BOT_TOKEN. The setup is single-user
# (ER-37, common practice for a personal repository); the job below runs only from main so a slip cannot use an old copy of it.
#
# Two jobs. `check` runs the checker from the DISPATCH ref's checkout (main, in `trusted/`) and reads the tag's commit only as
# data: `git show <sha>:path` for the version source and paddock.ci.json, and a `git archive` extraction for the tag gates, which
# the main-built ./dev reads. No script of the tagged tree is ever run. `push` is a fresh container with no checkout and the bot's
# token, which is the only place the token exists. Checked, each failing with one ::error:: and the next step
# (conformance/ci/request-tag.mjs):
#   - the tag's name; the sha is on origin/main or origin/release/*; it is not a skip-ci commit (ER-16); the tag does not exist;
#   - the app's version source says the tag's version;
#   - the newest FULL run of the app's gate workflow on exactly that sha is green, asked of `./dev ci verdict` (built from main;
#     tools/paddock-dev/src/ci_runs/verdict.rs, the one reader of the runs for this answer). Full means its plan job logged
#     `plan verdict: complete=true` after deciding (plan_since::COMPLETE_LINE; debrief.yml and ci.yml print it, the other app workflows through the shared plan action given `full:`), a push to main
#     included: a push whose plan skipped it tested nothing, and the refusal names the last fully tested commit. A since_run rerun or
#     a base dispatch is never full, so it cannot clear a red full run; unreadable is not measured, never a pass;
#   - for an app tag, the tag gates the release workflows also run (`./dev gates ratchet`, `./dev check ipc-endpoints --tag`).
# The ADR 0093 scheduled-CI gate (WP-5) is not built yet; it joins here when it is.
# Not covered (TOCTOU): a run can change between the check and the push (a rerun going red); the tag's own release workflow runs
# the gates again on the tag. A tag that already exists is refused by the server, never moved.
#
# The push uses RELEASE_BOT_TOKEN, a personal token of the user release-bot. A tag pushed with it starts the release workflow
# (an <app>-v* push); one pushed with the job's own token would not (Gitea ignores events whose doer is the Actions user:
# services/actions/notifier_helper.go, notify()). The token reaches git through GIT_ASKPASS from an env var, never argv, and is masked.
#
# Request a tag: POST /api/v1/repos/decryp7/paddock/actions/workflows/tag.yml/dispatches
#                with {"ref":"main","inputs":{"tag":"...","sha":"..."}}

name: tag

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      tag:
        description: "The tag to make: <app>-vX.Y.Z[-pre] or vX.Y.Z[-pre]"
        type: string
        required: true
      sha:
        description: "The full 40-hex commit id to tag (the commit CI tested)"
        type: string
        required: true

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: tag-${{ inputs.tag }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  check:
    name: check
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # actions: read lists runs and reads the plan job's log; unnamed scopes are None on this Gitea, so it must be named.
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: read
    container:
      image: dev.decryptology.net/decryp7/paddock-ci:v3
    env:
      TAG: ${{ inputs.tag }}
      SHA: ${{ inputs.sha }}
      PADDOCK_DEV_DOWNLOAD: "0"
    steps:
      # Inputs first, as plain text in the environment (never spliced into a script): a bad value fails before anything is fetched.
      - name: Inputs
        shell: bash
        run: |
          if ! [[ "$TAG" =~ ^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*-v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+(-[0-9A-Za-z.]+)?$ || "$TAG" =~ ^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+(-[0-9A-Za-z.]+)?$ ]]; then
            echo "::error::tag: the tag is not <app>-vX.Y.Z or vX.Y.Z. Run the workflow again with a tag like dyno-v1.2.0."
            exit 1
          fi
          if ! [[ "$SHA" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]]; then
            echo "::error::tag: the sha is not a full 40-hex commit id. Run the workflow again with the whole sha."
            exit 1
          fi

      # The trusted code: main, the dispatch ref, in its own folder. The tagged commit is never checked out.
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: main
          path: trusted
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Checks
        shell: bash
        working-directory: trusted
        env:
          GITEA_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          node conformance/ci/request-tag.mjs --tag "$TAG" --sha "$SHA" --root . \
            --api "${{ github.server_url }}/api/v1" --repo "${{ github.repository }}"

      # The gates read the tagged commit as data: an extracted archive (no hooks, no checkout), looked at by the ./dev built from main.
      - name: Tag gates (apps)
        shell: bash
        working-directory: trusted
        run: |
          if [[ "$TAG" =~ ^v[0-9] ]]; then
            echo "The shared-package tag $TAG has no app tag gates."
            exit 0
          fi
          target="$RUNNER_TEMP/target"
          rm -rf "$target"
          mkdir -p "$target"
          git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null archive "$SHA" | tar -x -C "$target"
          git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null -C "$target" init -q
          git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null -C "$target" fetch -q "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/trusted" main:refs/remotes/origin/main
          ./dev gates ratchet --root "$target" --release-tag "$TAG"
          ./dev check ipc-endpoints --root "$target" --tag "$TAG"

  # The bot's push: a fresh container, no checkout of any tree, nothing of the repository to run. It fetches the sha with the job's
  # own read token, makes the annotated tag and pushes it with the bot's token. Hooks are off for every git command.
  push:
    name: push
    needs: [check]
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    container:
      image: dev.decryptology.net/decryp7/paddock-ci:v3
    env:
      TAG: ${{ inputs.tag }}
      SHA: ${{ inputs.sha }}
    steps:
      - name: Make the tag as release-bot and push it
        shell: bash
        env:
          RELEASE_BOT_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_BOT_TOKEN }}
          JOB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if [ -z "$RELEASE_BOT_TOKEN" ]; then
            echo "::error::tag: the secret RELEASE_BOT_TOKEN is not set. Ask the repository owner to add the release-bot token as a secret."
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "::add-mask::$RELEASE_BOT_TOKEN"
          # The inputs are checked again here: this job does not trust the other one's word for them.
          if ! [[ "$TAG" =~ ^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*-v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+(-[0-9A-Za-z.]+)?$ || "$TAG" =~ ^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+(-[0-9A-Za-z.]+)?$ ]] || ! [[ "$SHA" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]]; then
            echo "::error::tag: the tag or the sha is malformed. Run the workflow again with valid inputs."
            exit 1
          fi
          # Credentials reach git through an askpass script that reads the environment: nothing secret is on a command line.
          askpass="$RUNNER_TEMP/askpass.sh"
          printf '%s\n' '#!/bin/sh' 'case "$1" in Username*) echo "$GIT_AUTH_USER" ;; *) echo "$GIT_AUTH_PASS" ;; esac' > "$askpass"
          chmod 700 "$askpass"
          export GIT_ASKPASS="$askpass" GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0
          url="${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}.git"
          dir="$RUNNER_TEMP/tagrepo"
          rm -rf "$dir"
          git init -q "$dir"
          cd "$dir"
          if ! GIT_AUTH_USER=gitea-actions GIT_AUTH_PASS="$JOB_TOKEN" git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null fetch -q --no-tags "$url" "$SHA"; then
            echo "::error::tag: the commit $SHA could not be fetched. Check the sha is on origin and the job may read the repository."
            exit 1
          fi
          git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null -c user.name=release-bot -c user.email=release-bot@users.noreply.dev.decryptology.net tag -a "$TAG" "$SHA" -m "Release $TAG"
          if ! GIT_AUTH_USER=release-bot GIT_AUTH_PASS="$RELEASE_BOT_TOKEN" git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null push "$url" "refs/tags/$TAG" 2>push.err; then
            tail -n 5 push.err
            echo "::error::tag: the push of $TAG was refused. Check that release-bot has Write on the repository, is on the tag protection allow-list, and the token has write:repository."
            exit 1
          fi
          {
            echo "## Tag $TAG made"
            echo "Pushed \`$TAG\` at \`$SHA\` as release-bot. The release workflow for the tag starts from this push."
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

#!/bin/bash
# usage: perf-post.sh LABEL STORE_DIR [IDLE_S]
# Reopens a store an import wrote with the perf_idle harness (crates/debrief-store-duck/tests/perf_idle.rs, ignored by
# default) and samples it with procsample.py; prints the per-phase summary.
# Environment: DEBRIEF_PERF_BIN (release target folder; the newest perf_idle-* binary under deps/ (cargo before 1.100) or build/<package>/<hash>/out/ (1.100) is used), DEBRIEF_LIB_DIR
# (libduckdb folder), DEBRIEF_PERF_OUT (results folder). macOS only.
set -eu
LABEL=$1; STORE=$2; IDLE=${3:-60}
HERE=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
CRATE=$(cd "$HERE/../../crates/debrief-store-duck" && pwd)
B=${DEBRIEF_PERF_BIN:?set DEBRIEF_PERF_BIN to the release target folder}
L=${DEBRIEF_LIB_DIR:?set DEBRIEF_LIB_DIR to the libduckdb folder}
OUT=${DEBRIEF_PERF_OUT:?set DEBRIEF_PERF_OUT to a results folder}
# Both cargo build-folder layouts: deps/ (before 1.100) and build/<package>/<hash>/out/ (1.100).
# conformance: layout-guess — searches `deps` and `build` both, so it finds the test binary in either cargo layout
T=$(find "$B/deps" "$B/build" -type f -name 'perf_idle-*' ! -name '*.d' ! -name '*.o' ! -name '*.rlib' -perm -u+x 2>/dev/null | xargs ls -t 2>/dev/null | head -1)
[ -n "$T" ] || { echo "::error::no perf_idle-* test binary under $B (deps/ or build/*/*/out/); next step: build it with cargo test --release -p debrief-store-duck --no-run"; exit 1; }
export DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH=$L DEBRIEF_PERF_STORE=$STORE DEBRIEF_PERF_IDLE_S=$IDLE
mkdir -p "$OUT"
cd "$CRATE"
uptime > "$OUT/$LABEL-post.uptime"
"$T" --ignored --nocapture --test-threads 1 > "$OUT/$LABEL-post.log" 2>&1 &
P=$!
python3 -I "$HERE/procsample.py" $P "$OUT/$LABEL-post.csv" 0.25 &
S=$!
rc=0; wait $P || rc=$?
echo "rc=$rc"; wait $S
uptime >> "$OUT/$LABEL-post.uptime"
grep -v '^PHASE\|^test \|^$\|^running' "$OUT/$LABEL-post.log" || true
python3 -I "$HERE/perfsum.py" "$OUT/$LABEL-post.csv" "$OUT/$LABEL-post.log"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Job isolation on a host runner (.gitea/actions/README.md, "Job isolation"; ADR 0025): any number of jobs may run on one
# host at once (several capacity-1 runners of a Pitcrew pool, all sharing ONE CI home) without one touching another's
# folders, processes or ports. The one way an action or workflow reaches a folder of the CI home.
#
#   job-isolation.sh acquire                 the job's slot (first bash step); exports PADDOCK_CI_SLOT, PADDOCK_CI_SLOT_TOKEN,
#                                            PADDOCK_JOB_TEMP, TMPDIR; sweeps idle slots and checks the free-disk floor
#   job-isolation.sh release                 gives the slot back (last step, if: always()); fails when the slot's holder
#                                            died during the job (its isolation was then not guaranteed)
#   job-isolation.sh status                  which slots are held, by which job folder (the stalled-holder recovery)
#   job-isolation.sh slots                   PADDOCK_CI_SLOTS with its default (setup-rust divides sccache's cap by it)
#   job-isolation.sh path <kind> [<name>]    a kept folder of kept-folders.txt (created, its time stamp renewed), for this slot
#   job-isolation.sh temp                    the job's own temp folder (the runner's $RUNNER_TEMP)
#   job-isolation.sh owns <folder> [<kind>]  exit 0 when <folder> is a kept folder (of that kind) of this job's slot
#   job-isolation.sh port <name>             the first port of this slot's block for <name> in ports.txt
#   job-isolation.sh pattern <regex>         a process pattern with {tmp}, {build} and {slot} filled in; exit 1 when it
#                                            names none of them (it would match other jobs' processes), or when {slot}
#                                            does not end the pattern right after a kept folder's name
#   job-isolation.sh sweep-slot [all]        (internal) deletes an idle slot's kept folders; runs only under
#                                            `dev ci slot idle-run`, which holds that slot's lock while it runs
#
# Two kinds of state:
# - Job-scoped (temp folders, the clean-up's temp sweep and process patterns): the runner's own per-job folder. The Gitea
#   runner gives every job <workdir_parent>/<16 random hex>/{hostexecutor,tmp,tool_cache,act}, sets RUNNER_TEMP to its tmp,
#   and deletes the whole folder after the job. acquire points TMPDIR (TMP and TEMP on Windows) at it, and on Unix makes a short
#   socket folder (PADDOCK_SOCKET_BASE) that release removes, both through job-tmpdir.sh.
# - Kept (kept-folders.txt): a stable absolute path per slot, so caches stay warm. A slot s<n> (n = 1..PADDOCK_CI_SLOTS) is
#   an OS file lock on <ci-home>/slots/s<n>.lock, held by a detached holder process (`./dev ci slot acquire`, ADR 0022's
#   paddock-dev) that lives until the job's RUNNER_TEMP is gone or release asks it to stop. The kernel drops the lock when
#   the holder dies, so there is no stale lock and nothing is ever reclaimed: two jobs never hold one slot.
# - Disk: a slot's kept folders are deleted only under `dev ci slot idle-run` (the slot's lock held for the whole deletion,
#   so no job can take the slot meanwhile): at acquire and release, the folders of idle slots above PADDOCK_CI_KEEP_SLOTS
#   (default: PADDOCK_CI_SLOTS, the pool's maximum), kept folders no job used for PADDOCK_CI_ORPHAN_DAYS (default 14; `path`
#   renews a folder's time stamp, so a folder no workflow names any more ages out) and, below the free-disk floor
#   PADDOCK_CI_MIN_FREE_GB (default 30), every idle slot's folders from the highest slot down. The first job in slot s1
#   renames a kept folder of the old unslotted layout to its -s1 name (a warm cache, no second copy).
#
# PADDOCK_CI_SLOTS: the most slots one host hands out (default 4); set it in every runner's environment (config.yaml
# runner.envs) to the pool's maximum number of runners on the host. Linux containers take no slot (one job per Linux host
# today; see ADR 0025 before running more): acquire and release do nothing there and everything else uses s1.
# Output: a value command (path, temp, owns, port, pattern, slots, status) prints exactly its value on stdout; every message
# goes to stderr, so a caller's "$(job-isolation.sh path ...)" is the path and nothing else (never capture it with 2>&1).
# PADDOCK_DEV: the paddock-dev program to run (tests); default the repository's ./dev wrapper, which keeps its binary in the
# shared kept folder tools/ (outside every job folder, so a Windows job folder can still be deleted while the holder runs).
set -euo pipefail
shopt -s inherit_errexit 2>/dev/null || true # bash 4.4+: command substitutions stop on errors too
here="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
table="$here/kept-folders.txt"
ports="$here/ports.txt"
shopt -s extglob

die() { echo "::error::job-isolation: $*" >&2; exit 1; }
is_linux() { [ "${RUNNER_OS:?RUNNER_OS is not set}" = Linux ]; }

job_temp() {
  local t="${RUNNER_TEMP:?RUNNER_TEMP is not set (the per-job temp folder of the runner)}"
  if command -v cygpath >/dev/null 2>&1; then t="$(cygpath -u "$t")"; fi
  printf '%s\n' "${t%/}"
}

# The CI home: ci-home.sh is the one implementation (PADDOCK_CI_HOME or ~/.paddock-ci; a missing relocated home fails).
ci_home() {
  local h
  # A caller's home="$(ci_home)" must fail, never go on with an empty home (paths at the root of the disk): bash before 4.4
  # keeps -e here, later ones with inherit_errexit (set above), and the empty check covers any other shell.
  h="$(bash "$here/ci-home.sh")"
  [ -n "$h" ] || exit 1
  printf '%s\n' "$h"
}

slot() {
  local s="${PADDOCK_CI_SLOT:-}"
  if [ -z "$s" ] && is_linux; then s=s1; fi
  [[ "$s" =~ ^s[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] || die "this job holds no slot: run the job-isolation action before any step that uses a kept folder"
  printf '%s\n' "$s"
}

# layout <kind>: "<layout> <scope>" from the table.
layout() {
  local line
  line="$(awk -v k="$1" '$1 == k && $1 !~ /^#/ { print $2, $3; exit }' <(tr -d '\r' < "$table"))"
  [ -n "$line" ] || die "no kept folder '$1' in kept-folders.txt"
  printf '%s\n' "$line"
}

# cachedir_tag <folder>: cargo's CACHEDIR.TAG in a target folder cargo did not make (ADR 0107 D1; the twin of
# paddock_env::cachedir::ensure). A file whose first line is the signature is a tag and is kept; a missing, empty or partial one
# is written to a temporary file and renamed over it.
cachedir_tag() {
  local sig='Signature: 8a477f597d28d172789f06886806bc55' f="$1/CACHEDIR.TAG" tmp
  [ "$(head -c "${#sig}" "$f" 2>/dev/null)" = "$sig" ] && return 0
  tmp="$f.tmp$$"
  printf '%s\n# This file is a cache directory tag created by cargo.\n# For information about cache directory tags see https://bford.info/cachedir/\n' "$sig" > "$tmp" \
    && mv -f "$tmp" "$f" || { rm -f "$tmp"; die "cannot write $f"; }
}

cmd_path() {
  local kind="${1:?usage: job-isolation.sh path <kind> [<name>]}" name="${2:-}" spec lay scope home rel
  spec="$(layout "$kind")"; lay="${spec% *}"; scope="${spec#* }"
  case "$lay" in *'{name}'*)
    [ -n "$name" ] || die "the kept folder '$kind' needs a name"
    case "$name" in *[!A-Za-z0-9._-]* | . | ..) die "the name '$name' may only hold letters, digits, '.', '_' and '-'" ;; esac ;;
  esac
  rel="${lay//\{name\}/$name}"
  if [ "$scope" = slot ]; then rel="${rel//\{slot\}/$(slot)}"; fi
  home="$(ci_home)"
  # One-time migration: the folder of the old layout (before slots) becomes slot s1's, so it stays warm and is not kept twice.
  if [ "$scope" = slot ] && [ "$(slot)" = s1 ] && [ ! -e "$home/$rel" ]; then
    local old="${lay//-\{slot\}/}"
    old="${old//\{name\}/$name}"
    if [ "$old" != "$rel" ] && [ -d "$home/$old" ] && [ ! -L "$home/$old" ]; then
      mkdir -p "$(dirname "$home/$rel")"
      mv "$home/$old" "$home/$rel" 2>/dev/null && echo "job-isolation: moved $old to $rel (kept folders are per slot now)" >&2
    fi
  fi
  mkdir -p "$home/$rel"
  if [ "$kind" = target ]; then cachedir_tag "$home/$rel"; fi
  touch "$home/$rel" 2>/dev/null || true  # in use: the orphan sweep removes only folders no job asked for in ORPHAN_DAYS
  printf '%s\n' "$home/$rel"
}

# slot_folders <home> <n>: every kept folder of slot s<n> (all names), one per line.
slot_folders() {
  local home="$1" n="$2" kind lay scope glob f
  while read -r kind lay scope; do
    case "$kind" in '' | \#*) continue ;; esac
    [ "$scope" = slot ] || continue
    glob="${lay//\{name\}/*}"; glob="${glob//\{slot\}/s$n}"
    for f in "$home"/$glob; do [ -d "$f" ] && [ ! -L "$f" ] && printf '%s\n' "$f"; done
  done < <(tr -d '\r' < "$table")
}

# legacy_folders <home>: kept folders of the old unslotted layout (a slot layout without its -{slot}; names that end in a slot
# are the new layout's), one per line.
legacy_folders() {
  local home="$1" kind lay scope glob f
  while read -r kind lay scope; do
    case "$kind" in '' | \#*) continue ;; esac
    [ "$scope" = slot ] || continue
    glob="${lay//-\{slot\}/}"; glob="${glob//\{name\}/*}"
    for f in "$home"/$glob; do
      [ -d "$f" ] && [ ! -L "$f" ] || continue
      [[ "$(basename "$f")" =~ -s[0-9]+$ ]] && continue
      printf '%s\n' "$f"
    done
  done < <(tr -d '\r' < "$table")
}

keep_slots() {
  local keep="${PADDOCK_CI_KEEP_SLOTS:-}"
  case "$keep" in '' | *[!0-9]*) keep="$(max_slots)" ;; esac
  printf '%s\n' "$keep"
}

max_slots() {
  local max="${PADDOCK_CI_SLOTS:-4}"
  case "$max" in '' | 0 | *[!0-9]*) die "PADDOCK_CI_SLOTS must be a whole number above 0 (got '$max')" ;; esac
  printf '%s\n' "$max"
}

# old <folder> <days>: true when the folder's time stamp is older than <days> days (path renews it on every use).
old() { [ -n "$(find "$1" -maxdepth 0 -mtime +"$2" 2>/dev/null)" ]; }

# due <home> <n> [all]: the kept folders of slot s<n> (and, for s1, the old layout's) that a sweep removes now, one per line
# as "<folder>\t<why>": all of them with `all` (below the free-disk floor) or above the kept slots, else those no job used
# for ORPHAN_DAYS. Read twice: before taking the slot's lock (so a slot with nothing due is never locked, and no new job is
# pushed to a colder slot by a sweep that removes nothing) and again under the lock (the answer may have changed).
due() {
  local home="$1" n="$2" mode="${3:-}" keep days f
  keep="$(keep_slots)"
  days="${PADDOCK_CI_ORPHAN_DAYS:-14}"
  case "$days" in '' | *[!0-9]*) days=14 ;; esac
  while IFS= read -r f; do
    [ -n "$f" ] || continue
    if [ "$mode" = all ]; then printf '%s\t%s\n' "$f" "the disk is below its free floor"
    elif [ "$n" -gt "$keep" ]; then printf '%s\t%s\n' "$f" "slot s$n is above the $keep kept slots"
    elif old "$f" "$days"; then printf '%s\t%s\n' "$f" "no job used it for $days days"
    fi
  done < <(slot_folders "$home" "$n"; if [ "$n" = 1 ]; then legacy_folders "$home"; fi)
}

# sweep-slot [all]: removes what `due` lists for the idle slot. Only under `dev ci slot idle-run`, which holds the slot's lock
# throughout: no job can take the slot while its folders go.
cmd_sweep_slot() {
  local s="${PADDOCK_CI_IDLE_SLOT:-}" mode="${1:-}" home f why
  [[ "$s" =~ ^s[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] || die "sweep-slot runs only under \`dev ci slot idle-run\` (which holds the slot's lock)"
  home="$(ci_home)"
  while IFS=$'\t' read -r f why; do
    [ -n "$f" ] || continue
    rm -rf "$f" && echo "job-isolation: removed $(basename "$f") ($why)" >&2
  done < <(due "$home" "${s#s}" "$mode")
}

# dev_tool <args>: paddock-dev (PADDOCK_DEV, else the repository's ./dev with its binary cached in the shared tools folder).
# Always without the job's compiler wrapper: ./dev builds paddock-dev when its cached binary is missing, and at release the
# job's sccache server is stopped and its temp folder removed, so a build through RUSTC_WRAPPER=sccache fails (runs 7773 to
# 7775: "No such file or directory ... gitea-runner/tmp/<job>/sccache..."). The tool's build has its own target folder anyway.
dev_tool() {
  (
    unset RUSTC_WRAPPER RUSTC_WORKSPACE_WRAPPER CARGO_BUILD_RUSTC_WRAPPER CARGO_BUILD_RUSTC_WORKSPACE_WRAPPER
    if [ -n "${PADDOCK_DEV:-}" ]; then exec "$PADDOCK_DEV" "$@"; fi
    tools="$(cmd_path tools)"
    repo="$(cd "$here/../.." && pwd)"
    cd "$repo" && PADDOCK_DEV_HOME="$tools/paddock-dev" PADDOCK_DEV_TARGET_DIR="$tools/paddock-dev-target" exec bash ./dev "$@"
  )
}

# native <path>: the path as the operating system's own programs take it (Windows form under Git bash).
native() { if command -v cygpath >/dev/null 2>&1; then cygpath -w "$1"; else printf '%s\n' "$1"; fi; }

# sweep <home> [all [<floor>]]: runs sweep-slot on every idle slot that has kept folders (the slot's lock held throughout);
# the job's own held slot is never touched (its lock is held). With `all`, from the highest slot down, stopping once the free
# disk is back above <floor>.
sweep() {
  local home="$1" mode="${2:-}" floor="${3:-}" max n
  max="$(max_slots)"
  for ((n = max; n >= 1; n--)); do
    # Nothing due: never take the slot's lock (an acquirer meeting it locked would move to a colder slot).
    [ -n "$(due "$home" "$n" "$mode")" ] || continue
    dev_tool ci slot idle-run --slot "s$n" --root "$(native "$home")" -- bash "$here/job-isolation.sh" sweep-slot ${mode:+"$mode"} >/dev/null \
      || echo "::warning::job-isolation: the sweep of slot s$n failed" >&2
    if [ -n "$floor" ] && [ "$(free_gb "$home")" -ge "$floor" ]; then return 0; fi
  done
  # Slots above the limit hold no folders the loop above did not see; a held slot's folders stay with its job.
  for ((n = max + 1; n <= max + 8; n++)); do
    [ -n "$(due "$home" "$n" all)" ] || continue
    dev_tool ci slot idle-run --slot "s$n" --root "$(native "$home")" -- bash "$here/job-isolation.sh" sweep-slot all >/dev/null || true
  done
}

# free_gb <folder>: whole gigabytes free on the folder's disk (PADDOCK_DF replaces df in tests).
free_gb() {
  "${PADDOCK_DF:-df}" -Pk "$1" 2>/dev/null | awk 'NR == 2 { print int($4 / 1048576) }'
}

cmd_owns() {
  local dir="${1:-}" only="${2:-}" home real rel s kind lay scope glob
  [ -n "$dir" ] && [ -d "$dir" ] && [ ! -L "$dir" ] || return 1
  if command -v cygpath >/dev/null 2>&1; then dir="$(cygpath -u "$dir")"; fi
  s="$(slot 2>/dev/null)" || return 1
  home="$(ci_home)"
  real="$(cd "$(dirname "$dir")" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)/$(basename "$dir")" || return 1
  case "$real" in "$home"/*) rel="${real#"$home"/}" ;; *) return 1 ;; esac
  while read -r kind lay scope; do
    case "$kind" in '' | \#*) continue ;; esac
    [ "$scope" = slot ] || continue
    [ -z "$only" ] || [ "$kind" = "$only" ] || continue
    [ "${rel//[!\/]/}" = "${lay//[!\/]/}" ] || continue
    glob="${lay//\{slot\}/$s}"; glob="${glob//\{name\}/?*}"
    # shellcheck disable=SC2053  # the layout is a glob on purpose
    if [[ "$rel" == $glob ]]; then return 0; fi
  done < <(tr -d '\r' < "$table")
  return 1
}

# A path as a pkill -f regex: every separator matches / and \, a Windows drive (C: or /c) is left out, metacharacters escaped.
path_regex() {
  local p="$1" out="" c i
  if [ "${RUNNER_OS:-}" = Windows ]; then
    case "$p" in [A-Za-z]:*) p="${p:2}" ;; /[A-Za-z]/*) p="${p:2}" ;; esac
  fi
  for ((i = 0; i < ${#p}; i++)); do
    c="${p:i:1}"
    case "$c" in
      / | \\) out+='[/\\]' ;;
      [].[*+?\(\){}\|^\$]) out+="\\$c" ;;
      *) out+="$c" ;;
    esac
  done
  printf '%s' "$out"
}

# fill <text> <placeholder> <value>: every <placeholder> in <text> replaced by <value>, as plain text. Not ${text//p/v}: bash
# 5.2's patsub_replacement treats a backslash in v as an escape there, which turned the separator class [/\\] into [/\].
fill() {
  local text="$1" key="$2" value="$3" out=""
  while [[ "$text" == *"$key"* ]]; do
    out+="${text%%"$key"*}$value"
    text="${text#*"$key"}"
  done
  printf '%s' "$out$text"
}

cmd_pattern() {
  local pat="${1:-}" scoped=0 v
  case "$pat" in *'{tmp}'*)
    v="${PADDOCK_JOB_TEMP:-}"; [ -n "$v" ] || return 1
    pat="$(fill "$pat" '{tmp}' "$(path_regex "$v")")"; scoped=1 ;;
  esac
  case "$pat" in *'{build}'*)
    v="${PADDOCK_BUILD_FOLDER:-}"; [ -n "$v" ] || return 1
    pat="$(fill "$pat" '{build}' "$(path_regex "$v")")"; scoped=1 ;;
  esac
  case "$pat" in *'{slot}'*)
    v="$(slot 2>/dev/null)" || return 1
    slot_anchored "$pat" || return 1
    # A boundary after the slot: s1 must not match s12.
    pat="$(fill "$pat" '{slot}' "$v([^0-9]|\$)")"; scoped=1 ;;
  esac
  [ "$scoped" = 1 ] || return 1
  # Never the slot's own holder: its command line names the job's temp folder (--owner) and the CI home (--root), so a
  # pattern such as "{tmp}" alone would end it and free the slot in the middle of the job.
  if holder_matches "$pat"; then
    echo "job-isolation: the pattern '$1' would also match this job's slot holder (\`ci slot hold --owner <job temp>\`)" >&2
    return 1
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$pat"
}

# holder_matches <regex>: true when the regex matches the slot holder's command line as this job starts it (Unix and Windows
# spellings of its paths).
holder_matches() {
  local re="$1" temp home line t h bs="\\"
  temp="${PADDOCK_JOB_TEMP:-${RUNNER_TEMP:-/job-temp}}"
  home="$(bash "$here/ci-home.sh")"
  [ -n "$home" ] || home="/ci-home" # (in an `if`, so -e does not apply: no CI home leaves a stand-in)
  for t in "$temp" "$(fill "$temp" / "$bs")"; do
    for h in "$home" "$(fill "$home" / "$bs")"; do
      line="$h/tools/paddock-dev/bin/0/paddock-dev ci slot hold --max 4 --owner $t --root $h --poll-ms 500 --max-hold-secs 12600"
      if printf '%s\n' "$line" | grep -Eq -- "$re" 2>/dev/null; then return 0; fi
    done
  done
  return 1
}

# slot_anchored <pattern>: {slot} occurs once, ends the pattern, and comes right after a slot kept folder's name: the
# layout's text before {name} (after a separator or at the start), a name, and a dash (e.g. [/\\]test-browser-spotter-{slot}).
slot_anchored() {
  local pat="$1" before kind lay scope stem
  [[ "$pat" == *'{slot}' ]] || return 1
  before="${pat%'{slot}'}"
  [[ "$before" != *'{slot}'* ]] || return 1
  while read -r kind lay scope; do
    case "$kind" in '' | \#*) continue ;; esac
    [ "$scope" = slot ] || continue
    stem="${lay%%'{name}'*}"
    stem="${stem//\//[/\\\\]}"
    if [[ "$before" == *@(/|\])"$stem"+([A-Za-z0-9._-])- ]] || [[ "$before" == "$stem"+([A-Za-z0-9._-])- ]]; then return 0; fi
  done < <(tr -d '\r' < "$table")
  return 1
}

cmd_port() {
  local name="${1:?usage: job-isolation.sh port <name>}" line base _width stride s
  line="$(awk -v k="$name" '$1 == k && $1 !~ /^#/ { print $2, $3, $4; exit }' <(tr -d '\r' < "$ports"))"
  [ -n "$line" ] || die "no port block '$name' in ports.txt"
  read -r base _width stride <<< "$line"
  s="$(slot)"
  printf '%s\n' $((base + (${s#s} - 1) * stride))
}

# ---- slots ----

# The env lines a slot gives the job's later steps.
export_slot() {
  local out="$1" slot="$2" token="$3" temp="$4"
  {
    echo "PADDOCK_CI_SLOT=$slot"
    echo "PADDOCK_CI_SLOT_TOKEN=$token"
  } >> "$out"
  # The job's temp and socket folders (PADDOCK_JOB_TEMP, TMPDIR, PADDOCK_SOCKET_BASE): one implementation, shared with the
  # job-tmpdir action. $temp is the same folder (the runner's RUNNER_TEMP).
  bash "$here/job-tmpdir.sh" sweep || echo "::warning::job-isolation: the socket folders of finished jobs could not be swept" >&2
  GITHUB_ENV="$out" bash "$here/job-tmpdir.sh" setup
}

cmd_acquire() {
  if is_linux; then echo "job-isolation: no slot in a Linux container (one job per Linux host; ADR 0025)" >&2; return 0; fi
  local out="${GITHUB_ENV:?GITHUB_ENV is not set}" temp home max said code=0 slot token tries=0 wait floor free
  temp="$(job_temp)"
  [ -d "$temp" ] || die "the runner's per-job temp folder $temp does not exist"
  max="$(max_slots)"
  if [[ "${PADDOCK_CI_SLOT:-}" =~ ^s[1-9][0-9]*$ ]]; then echo "job-isolation: this job already holds $PADDOCK_CI_SLOT" >&2; return 0; fi
  home="$(ci_home)"
  wait="${PADDOCK_SLOT_WAIT_TRIES:-20}"
  # A full house is refused (exit 4). It is real (more runners than PADDOCK_CI_SLOTS) or brief (a sweep holds an idle slot's
  # lock while it deletes that slot's folders): wait a little, then fail and name the holders.
  while :; do
    code=0
    said="$(dev_tool ci slot acquire --max "$max" --owner "$(native "$temp")" --root "$(native "$home")")" || code=$?
    if [ "$code" = 0 ] || [ "$code" != 4 ] || [ "$tries" -ge "$wait" ]; then break; fi
    tries=$((tries + 1))
    echo "job-isolation: all $max slots are held; trying again ($tries of $wait)" >&2
    sleep "${PADDOCK_SLOT_WAIT_SECONDS:-6}"
  done
  if [ "$code" != 0 ]; then
    echo "::error::job-isolation: no slot (paddock-dev exit $code). Held slots (./dev ci slot status):" >&2
    cmd_status >&2 || true
    echo "Set PADDOCK_CI_SLOTS on every runner of this host to the pool's maximum (it is $max), or see ADR 0025, \"Stalled holder\"." >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  read -r slot token <<< "$said"
  [[ "$slot" =~ ^s[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] && [ -n "$token" ] || die "paddock-dev answered '$said', not a slot and a token"
  export_slot "$out" "$slot" "$token" "$temp"
  # Pin the tool this job started with. The wrapper's hash covers files a job writes itself (the paddock-dev job's
  # tools/paddock-dev/.cargo/ci.toml), so at the end the release would want another build, with the job's temp folder already
  # gone (sccache then fails); the pinned binary needs none.
  if bin="$(dev_tool --print-binary 2>/dev/null)" && [ -n "$bin" ]; then
    echo "PADDOCK_DEV=$bin" >> "$out"
  else
    echo "::warning::job-isolation: the tool could not be pinned (no cached binary: uncommitted inputs, or no build); the release step will run ./dev again, and fails if that needs a build after the job's temp folder is gone. PADDOCK_DEV is not set." >&2
  fi
  echo "job-isolation: slot $slot (kept folders end in -$slot); temp folders in $temp" >&2
  sweep "$home"
  floor="${PADDOCK_CI_MIN_FREE_GB:-30}"
  case "$floor" in '' | *[!0-9]*) floor=30 ;; esac
  free="$(free_gb "$home")"
  if [ -n "$free" ] && [ "$free" -lt "$floor" ]; then
    echo "::warning::job-isolation: $free GB free on the CI home's disk, below the floor of $floor GB (PADDOCK_CI_MIN_FREE_GB); removing idle slots' kept folders, highest slot first" >&2
    sweep "$home" all "$floor"
    free="$(free_gb "$home")"
    if [ "$free" -lt "$floor" ]; then
      echo "::error::job-isolation: still only $free GB free on $home's disk after removing every idle slot's kept folders (floor $floor GB). Free disk on the host, then re-run the job." >&2
      PADDOCK_CI_SLOT="$slot" PADDOCK_CI_SLOT_TOKEN="$token" cmd_release >/dev/null || true
      exit 1
    fi
  fi
  # `./dev disk check`: one warning under 200 GiB (with the largest folders) and a refusal under 50 GiB, on the CI home's disk and
  # the job's workspace disk (PADDOCK_DISK_WARN_GIB, PADDOCK_DISK_REFUSE_GIB). Exit 1 is the refusal; any other failure (an older
  # cached tool without `disk`) is a warning, never a refusal: the check did not run.
  local disk_code=0
  dev_tool disk check --path "$(native "$home")" ${GITHUB_WORKSPACE:+--path "$(native "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE")"} >&2 || disk_code=$?
  if [ "$disk_code" = 1 ]; then
    PADDOCK_CI_SLOT="$slot" PADDOCK_CI_SLOT_TOKEN="$token" cmd_release >/dev/null || true
    exit 1
  elif [ "$disk_code" != 0 ]; then
    echo "::warning::job-isolation: ./dev disk check did not run (exit $disk_code); free space was not checked. Next step: run './dev disk check' on the runner." >&2
  fi
}

# held_by_us <home> <slot> <token>: 0 when the slot's lock is held and its holder is the one this job started, 1 when not,
# 2 when paddock-dev could not be asked (its own message is on stderr): that says nothing about the holder.
held_by_us() {
  local home="$1" slot="$2" token="$3" status
  [ "$(sed -n 's/^token=//p' "$home/slots/$slot.owner" 2>/dev/null | head -1)" = "$token" ] || return 1
  status="$(dev_tool ci slot status --max "${slot#s}" --root "$(native "$home")")" || return 2
  [ "$(printf '%s\n' "$status" | awk -v s="$slot" '$1 == s { print $2 }')" = busy ]
}

cmd_release() {
  is_linux && return 0
  # The job's socket folder goes whether or not this job got a slot (acquire made it).
  bash "$here/job-tmpdir.sh" remove || echo "::warning::job-isolation: the job's socket folder could not be removed" >&2
  local s="${PADDOCK_CI_SLOT:-}" token="${PADDOCK_CI_SLOT_TOKEN:-}" home ok=1
  [[ "$s" =~ ^s[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] || { echo "job-isolation: this job holds no slot" >&2; return 0; }
  home="$(ci_home)" || return 0
  local held=0
  held_by_us "$home" "$s" "$token" || held=$?
  if [ "$held" = 2 ]; then
    ok=0
    echo "::error::job-isolation: could not ask paddock-dev whether the holder of $s is still there (its message is above), so this job's isolation could not be checked. Next step: run './dev ci slot status' in the repository on the runner to see why paddock-dev fails." >&2
  elif [ "$held" != 0 ]; then
    ok=0
    echo "::error::job-isolation: the holder of $s ended before the job did (killed with the job's processes?), so another job could have taken $s meanwhile: this job's isolation was not guaranteed. See ADR 0025, \"Stalled holder\"." >&2
  fi
  # Only this job's own holder: release honours only its token.
  dev_tool ci slot release --slot "$s" --token "$token" --root "$(native "$home")" --timeout-secs 30 >/dev/null \
    || echo "::warning::job-isolation: $s did not let go in time (./dev ci slot status shows its holder)" >&2
  echo "job-isolation: released $s" >&2
  sweep "$home"
  [ "$ok" = 1 ]
}

cmd_status() {
  local home max n state owner pid
  home="$(ci_home)"; max="$(max_slots)"
  dev_tool ci slot status --max "$max" --root "$(native "$home")" | while read -r n state; do
    owner="$(sed -n 's/^owner=//p' "$home/slots/$n.owner" 2>/dev/null | head -1)" || owner=""
    pid="$(sed -n 's/^pid=//p' "$home/slots/$n.owner" 2>/dev/null | head -1)" || pid=""
    if [ "$state" = busy ]; then echo "  $n busy: job folder ${owner:-?} (holder pid ${pid:-?})"
    else echo "  $n free"; fi
  done
}

case "${1:-}" in
  acquire) cmd_acquire ;;
  release) cmd_release ;;
  status) cmd_status ;;
  slots) max_slots ;;
  sweep-slot) shift; cmd_sweep_slot "$@" ;;
  path) shift; cmd_path "$@" ;;
  temp) job_temp ;;
  owns) shift; cmd_owns "$@" ;;
  port) shift; cmd_port "$@" ;;
  pattern) shift; cmd_pattern "$@" ;;
  *) echo "usage: job-isolation.sh acquire|release|status|slots|path <kind> [<name>]|temp|owns <folder>|port <name>|pattern <regex>" >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac
conformance/ci/kit.sh

#!/bin/sh
# The CI kit's bootstrap shim (docs/plans/ci-in-rust.md, WP-1 and section 5): runs a kit step in Rust (`./dev ci <step>`) or, on the
# release path, through the shell script that step had until the release-path lane deletes it. This is the one place that picks the
# implementation (setup-rust's Implementation step asks `kit.sh which`), so a workflow or action says
# `bash conformance/ci/kit.sh <step> ...` and nothing else.
#
#   kit.sh which                     prints dev or shell (the reason goes to stderr)
#   kit.sh isolation <args>          `./dev ci isolation <args>` (or job-isolation.sh <args>)
#   kit.sh build-jobs [<split>]      `./dev ci build-jobs [<split>]` (or build-jobs.sh [<split>])
#   kit.sh build-env                 `./dev ci build-env` (or node build-env.mjs): PADDOCK_BUILD_COMMIT and PADDOCK_BUILD_DATE
#   kit.sh host <step> <args>        a host-runner step (WP-4), in Rust or in the shell it had:
#     stable-workspace <name>                     ci stable-workspace --name | host/stable-workspace.sh (NAME)
#     node-caches <angular-dir> <name>            ci node-caches --angular-dir --name | host/node-caches.sh (ANGULAR_DIR, NAME)
#     host-tools | sccache-stats                  ci host-tools | ci sccache-stats | host/<step>.sh
#     build-folder <workspace> <name>             ci build-folder | build-folder.sh
#     prune-build-folder <max-gb> [drop-bundles]  ci prune-build-folder --max-gb [--drop-bundles] | tools/prune-ci-build-folder.sh
#     prune-folder <folder> <max-gb>              ci prune-folder | tools/prune-build-folders.sh
#     host-cleanup <host-cleanup options>         ci host-cleanup | tools/host-cleanup.sh
#     kept-clone <name> <profile> [<fresh>]       ci kept-clone --name --profile [--fresh] | kept-clone.sh (NAME, PROFILE, FRESH)
#     guardian-as-user                            ci guardian-as-user | guardian-as-user.sh (the Linux crates job, from crates/)
#   (`ci boot-volume external|temp` has no shim route: job-tmpdir.sh sources boot-volume.sh, and paddock_testkit and Dyno's
#   check-bundle.sh run it; the Rust copy is job-tmpdir's rule in process. WP-5, docs/plans/ci-in-rust.md.)
#
# The shell is used for: PADDOCK_CI_KIT=shell (the fallback switch: one variable away, plan section 7), a tag run, a run that never
# downloads the tool (PADDOCK_DEV_DOWNLOAD=0: release and rule 54 jobs), a checkout without tools/paddock-dev (another repository
# using the actions) and a machine without rustc (./dev hashes and builds itself with it). Every call prints one `kit:` line on
# standard error naming the choice and why (ER-27). The scripts stay until WP-11 deletes them with this shim; both implementations are
# held equal by tools/paddock-dev/tests/it/build_jobs.rs, tools/paddock-dev/tests/it/host_steps.rs and
# conformance/test/job-isolation.test.mjs (ISOLATION_CMD).
#
# One tool per job: on a host runner the tool is fetched or built in the CI home's shared `tools` folder, never in the runner's own
# home (a Windows job folder must stay deletable while the slot's holder runs). The folder is asked of job-isolation.sh in shell, so
# no tool is needed to find where the tool goes. `isolation acquire` pins the tool as PADDOCK_DEV for the later steps and for
# release, which must not build it after the job's temp folder is gone. A Linux container takes no slot: acquire and release do
# nothing there, and the wrapper keeps the tool on the /sccache mount.
#
# The job's compiler wrapper is unset before every ./dev call: ./dev builds the tool when its binary is missing, and at release the
# job's sccache server is stopped and its temp folder removed (runs 7773 to 7775).
#
# build-jobs: the tool's own first build needs a core limit before CARGO_BUILD_JOBS exists; it gets the default of 4 (the share of
# a runner on the shared Mac; on Linux measured in docs/benchmarks.md, "Kit shim default"), and `./dev ci build-jobs` then writes
# the job's real value.
set -eu

here=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
root=$(cd "$here/../.." && pwd)

# kit.sh portable <what> <path>: the one place the shell kit tells GNU tools from BSD ones. The flavour is probed once from the tool
# itself (`stat -c` and `find -printf` exist only in GNU), never from the exit status of the real call: `stat -c ... || stat -f ...`
# ran BSD's form on GNU whenever the first call failed (a vanished file, an unreadable folder), and GNU `stat -f` prints the file
# system's lines, which a sum read as a size of about 1.2e10 (review of fix/c125-and-arm64-tests, P1-1; the old
# `du -A || du --apparent-size` was the same shape). Answered before anything else here runs: no toolchain, no kit choice.
#   portable volume-of <path>    the device number of the volume that holds <path> (fails, printing nothing, when it cannot be read)
#   portable file-bytes <dir>    the length in bytes of the regular files below <dir>, hard links once; what cannot be read counts 0
#   portable file-allocated <dir>  the bytes allocated to those files, the same way: folders are not files, and ext4 gives each
#                                folder 4 KiB, so `du` called a folder of empty folders 20 KiB (CI run 8138). GNU find's %b and
#                                BSD stat's %b (st_blocks) count 512-byte blocks; GNU stat's %b counts blocks of %B bytes
#   portable file-sizes <dir>    both, from one pass: `<bytes> <allocated>` (a pass is a find and a stat of every file)
if [ "${1:-}" = portable ]; then
  gnu_stat() { stat -c %s / >/dev/null 2>&1; }
  case "${2:-}" in
    volume-of)
      if gnu_stat; then exec stat -c %d "${3:?volume-of needs a path}" 2>/dev/null; fi
      exec stat -f %d "${3:?volume-of needs a path}" 2>/dev/null
      ;;
    file-bytes | file-allocated | file-sizes)
      d="${3:?$2 needs a folder}"
      {
        if find / -maxdepth 0 -printf '' >/dev/null 2>&1; then find "$d" -type f -printf '%D:%i %s %b\n'
        elif gnu_stat; then find "$d" -type f -exec stat -c '%d:%i %s %b %B' {} +
        else find "$d" -type f -exec stat -f '%d:%i %z %b' {} +
        fi
      } 2>/dev/null | grep -E '^[0-9]+:[0-9]+ [0-9]+ [0-9]+( [0-9]+)?$' | sort -u |
        awk -v what="$2" '{ b += $2; a += $3 * ($4 == "" ? 512 : $4) }
          END { if (what == "file-bytes") printf "%.0f\n", b; else if (what == "file-allocated") printf "%.0f\n", a; else printf "%.0f %.0f\n", b, a }'
      exit 0
      ;;
    *)
      echo "usage: kit.sh portable volume-of <path> | file-bytes <dir> | file-allocated <dir> | file-sizes <dir>" >&2
      exit 2
      ;;
  esac
fi

# kit_choice: prints "<dev|shell> <reason>".
kit_choice() {
  if [ "${PADDOCK_CI_KIT:-}" = shell ]; then echo "shell PADDOCK_CI_KIT=shell"; return; fi
  case "${GITHUB_REF:-}" in refs/tags/*) echo "shell a tag run"; return ;; esac
  if [ "${PADDOCK_DEV_DOWNLOAD:-}" = 0 ]; then echo "shell PADDOCK_DEV_DOWNLOAD=0 (a release or rule 54 run)"; return; fi
  # ./dev runs the tool of the checkout it is started in (as setup-rust does): another repository using these actions, or a
  # sparse checkout without tools/, has none.
  top=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || true)
  if [ -z "$top" ] || [ ! -f "$top/tools/paddock-dev/Cargo.toml" ]; then echo "shell no tools/paddock-dev in this checkout"; return; fi
  if [ ! -f "$root/dev" ]; then echo "shell no ./dev wrapper beside this script"; return; fi
  if ! command -v rustc >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "shell no rustc on PATH"; return; fi
  # A rustup shim passes `command -v` and still cannot run when the pinned toolchain is missing: the steps that must always work
  # (host-cleanup, prune, release) then use the shell kit instead of exiting 2 and hiding it behind `|| true`.
  if [ "${PADDOCK_TOOLCHAIN_FAILED:-}" = 1 ] || ! (cd "$top/tools/paddock-dev" && rustc -vV >/dev/null 2>&1); then
    echo "shell rustc does not run in this checkout (the pinned toolchain is not installed)"
    return
  fi
  echo "dev ./dev ci steps are available"
}

# The toolchain the repository pins is installed before the first ./dev or rustc call of the job (run 8034: on Windows build-jobs ran
# before setup-rust, the pinned version was not there yet, `rustc` could not run and the wrapper fell back). `./dev --ensure-toolchain`
# installs it with rustup when rustc does not run (bounded, logged); a machine without rustup is left to the choice below.
if [ "${GITHUB_ACTIONS:-}" = true ] && [ "${PADDOCK_TOOLCHAIN_FAILED:-}" != 1 ] && command -v rustup >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -f "$root/dev" ] && [ -f "$root/tools/paddock-dev/Cargo.toml" ]; then
  if ! bash "$root/dev" --ensure-toolchain; then
    # Remembered for the rest of the job: later steps do not try again (900 s each) and use the shell kit, which needs no Rust.
    PADDOCK_TOOLCHAIN_FAILED=1
    PADDOCK_CI_KIT=shell
    export PADDOCK_TOOLCHAIN_FAILED PADDOCK_CI_KIT
    if [ -n "${GITHUB_ENV:-}" ]; then printf 'PADDOCK_TOOLCHAIN_FAILED=1\nPADDOCK_CI_KIT=shell\n' >> "$GITHUB_ENV" || true; fi
    echo "::warning::kit.sh: the pinned Rust toolchain could not be installed (see above); the rest of this job uses the shell kit, and steps that need Rust will fail with their own message." >&2
  fi
fi

choice=$(kit_choice)
kit=${choice%% *}
echo "kit: $kit (${choice#* })" >&2

# Without the read credential ./dev builds itself from source and never takes a binary from the store (ADR 0022 section 3.3).
dev_env() {
  if [ -z "${PADDOCK_DEV_TOKEN-}${GITHUB_TOKEN-}" ]; then PADDOCK_DEV_DOWNLOAD=0; export PADDOCK_DEV_DOWNLOAD; fi
  unset RUSTC_WRAPPER RUSTC_WORKSPACE_WRAPPER CARGO_BUILD_RUSTC_WRAPPER CARGO_BUILD_RUSTC_WORKSPACE_WRAPPER
}

# tools_home: in a CI job on a host runner, PADDOCK_DEV_HOME and PADDOCK_DEV_TARGET_DIR under the CI home's tools folder (unless the caller
# chose them), found without the tool.
tools_home() {
  # Only a CI job has a CI home: a person's machine keeps the tool where ./dev puts it (a RUNNER_OS in a shell profile must not move it).
  [ "${GITHUB_ACTIONS:-}" = true ] || return 0
  [ "${RUNNER_OS:-}" != Linux ] || return 0
  [ -z "${PADDOCK_DEV_HOME:-}" ] || return 0
  tools="$(bash "$here/job-isolation.sh" path tools)"
  PADDOCK_DEV_HOME="$tools/paddock-dev"
  PADDOCK_DEV_TARGET_DIR="$tools/paddock-dev-target"
  export PADDOCK_DEV_HOME PADDOCK_DEV_TARGET_DIR
}

dev_isolation() {
  dev_env
  case "${1:-}" in
    acquire | release)
      [ "${RUNNER_OS:-}" != Linux ] || exit 0
      if [ "$1" = release ] && [ -n "${PADDOCK_DEV:-}" ]; then exec "$PADDOCK_DEV" ci isolation release; fi
      tools_home
      if [ "$1" = release ]; then exec bash "$root/dev" ci isolation release; fi
      bin="$(bash "$root/dev" --print-binary)" || bin=""
      if [ -n "$bin" ]; then
        PADDOCK_DEV="$bin"
        export PADDOCK_DEV
        job_setup "$bin" ci isolation acquire
      fi
      job_setup bash "$root/dev" ci isolation acquire
      ;;
    *)
      # The pinned tool when the job has one (acquire pinned it), else the wrapper.
      if [ -n "${PADDOCK_DEV:-}" ]; then exec "$PADDOCK_DEV" ci isolation "$@"; fi
      tools_home
      exec bash "$root/dev" ci isolation "$@"
      ;;
  esac
}

# job_setup <command>: runs a job's setup step (build-jobs, the isolation acquire) and never returns. When it fails the job must not go
# on: later steps that run after a failure (`if: !cancelled()`, so one run reports every failed check) would test without the
# job's slot, temp folders or core share (run 8027, crate on Windows ran its tests after ./dev could not be built). The failure
# is written to GITHUB_ENV as PADDOCK_JOB_ABORTED=1, which those steps test, and said once as an annotation.
job_setup() {
  "$@" && exit 0
  rc=$?
  echo "::error::A job setup step failed (exit $rc: $*). The job's later steps are skipped, because they would run without the slot, temp folders and core share that step sets up. Read the error above it, fix that, and rerun the job." >&2
  if [ -n "${GITHUB_ENV:-}" ]; then echo "PADDOCK_JOB_ABORTED=1" >> "$GITHUB_ENV" || true; fi
  exit "$rc"
}

# first_build_jobs: the core limit for the tool's own first build (see the header: build-jobs).
first_build_jobs() {
  CARGO_BUILD_JOBS="${CARGO_BUILD_JOBS:-4}"
  export CARGO_BUILD_JOBS
}

# dev_run <args>: `./dev ci <args>`: the pinned tool when the job has one, else the wrapper (which builds it in the shared tools folder).
dev_run() {
  dev_env
  if [ -n "${PADDOCK_DEV:-}" ]; then exec "$PADDOCK_DEV" ci "$@"; fi
  tools_home
  first_build_jobs
  exec bash "$root/dev" ci "$@"
}

host_usage() {
  echo "usage: kit.sh host stable-workspace <name> | node-caches <angular-dir> <name> | host-tools | sccache-stats | build-folder <workspace> <name> | prune-build-folder <max-gb> [drop-bundles] | prune-folder <folder> <max-gb> | host-cleanup <options> | kept-clone <name> <profile> [<fresh>] | guardian-as-user" >&2
  exit 2
}

# kit_host <step> <args>: a host step in Rust or in its shell (the runner's `bash -e -o pipefail` for the inline ones it had).
kit_host() {
  step="${1:-}"
  [ -n "$step" ] || host_usage
  shift
  # Nothing to do, so no tool is fetched or built for it: a Linux container has a fixed workspace, and without sccache there are no
  # statistics.
  case "$step" in
    stable-workspace | kept-clone) [ "${RUNNER_OS:-}" != Linux ] || exit 0 ;;
    sccache-stats) command -v sccache >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 0 ;;
  esac
  if [ "$kit" = dev ]; then
    case "$step" in
      stable-workspace) dev_run stable-workspace --name "${1:?stable-workspace needs a name}" ;;
      node-caches) dev_run node-caches --angular-dir "${1-}" --name "${2:?node-caches needs a name}" ;;
      host-tools | sccache-stats | guardian-as-user) dev_run "$step" ;;
      kept-clone)
        if [ "${3:-}" = true ]; then dev_run kept-clone --name "${1:?kept-clone needs a name}" --profile "${2:?kept-clone needs a profile}" --fresh; fi
        dev_run kept-clone --name "${1:?kept-clone needs a name}" --profile "${2:?kept-clone needs a profile}"
        ;;
      build-folder | prune-folder | host-cleanup) dev_run "$step" "$@" ;;
      prune-build-folder)
        if [ "${2:-}" = true ]; then dev_run prune-build-folder --max-gb "${1:-20}" --drop-bundles; fi
        dev_run prune-build-folder --max-gb "${1:-20}"
        ;;
      *) host_usage ;;
    esac
  fi
  case "$step" in
    stable-workspace) NAME="${1:?stable-workspace needs a name}" exec bash -e -o pipefail "$here/host/stable-workspace.sh" ;;
    node-caches) ANGULAR_DIR="${1-}" NAME="${2:?node-caches needs a name}" exec bash -e -o pipefail "$here/host/node-caches.sh" ;;
    host-tools | sccache-stats) exec bash -e -o pipefail "$here/host/$step.sh" ;;
    kept-clone) NAME="${1:?kept-clone needs a name}" PROFILE="${2:?kept-clone needs a profile}" FRESH="${3:-false}" exec bash "$here/kept-clone.sh" ;;
    guardian-as-user) exec bash "$here/guardian-as-user.sh" ;;
    build-folder) exec bash "$here/build-folder.sh" "$@" ;;
    prune-folder) exec bash "$root/tools/prune-build-folders.sh" "$@" ;;
    host-cleanup) exec bash "$root/tools/host-cleanup.sh" "$@" ;;
    prune-build-folder)
      dir="${PADDOCK_BUILD_FOLDER:-}"
      if [ -n "$dir" ] && command -v cygpath >/dev/null; then dir="$(cygpath -u "$dir")"; fi
      extra=""; if [ "${2:-}" = true ]; then extra="--drop-bundles"; fi
      exec bash "$root/tools/prune-ci-build-folder.sh" "$dir" "${1:-20}" ${extra:+"$extra"}
      ;;
    *) host_usage ;;
  esac
}

case "${1:-}" in
  which) echo "$kit" ;;
  host)
    shift
    kit_host "$@"
    ;;
  isolation)
    shift
    if [ "$kit" = dev ]; then dev_isolation "$@"; fi
    exec bash "$here/job-isolation.sh" "$@"
    ;;
  build-jobs)
    shift
    if [ "$kit" = dev ]; then
      dev_env
      tools_home
      first_build_jobs
      job_setup bash "$root/dev" ci build-jobs "$@"
    fi
    job_setup bash "$here/build-jobs.sh" "$@"
    ;;
  build-env)
    if [ "$kit" = dev ]; then dev_run build-env; fi
    exec node "$here/build-env.mjs"
    ;;
  *)
    echo "usage: kit.sh which | isolation <args> | build-jobs [<split>] | build-env | host <step> <args> | portable <what> <path>" >&2
    exit 2
    ;;
esac

 "exceptions": [
  {"path": "dev", "id": "E1", "reason": "stage-0 launcher: something must start before any Rust binary exists; about 20 lines once WP-1 lands", "owner": "shell-to-rust plan section 2"},
