#!/usr/bin/env bash
# MANUAL USE ONLY. The other-os member gate (`./dev merge check --gates`, tools/paddock-dev/src/merge_check/other_os.rs) runs on the
# real CI runners since the user's decision of 2026-11-16; this script no longer belongs to it. It stays to run one package
# natively on the Windows test VM by hand (for a Windows-only investigation, with the guest's own differences: Arm, Prism, a
# runner-style PATH that is not the runner's). Its packages build and run NATIVELY on the test VM the way the Gitea Windows runner starts a step
# (`vm-win.sh run --ci-like`: runner-style temp folder, a fresh checkout with core.autocrlf=true, Git bash, CI env), under the test
# machines lock. Tests that run cargo (paddock-dev's) therefore work: the guest has the pinned Rust toolchain.
#
#   scripts/member-gate-windows.sh <tree> <spec>...      <tree>: the tree of HEAD; spec: `nextest <workspace> <package> [filter]`
#
# What is where (docs/adr/amendments/0087-member-gate-other-os-2026-11-16.md): the MSVC Build Tools are in the VM image, snapshot
# `buildtools-baseline` (`vm-win.sh toolchain-setup`, once). The Rust toolchain of rust-toolchain.toml is copied in per run from a
# host-side cache (scripts/vm-win/member-gate-tools.lock) with the pinned aarch64 cargo-nextest; no rustup runs in the guest, so
# nothing can auto-install a toolchain, and the registries are read anonymously (.cargo/config.toml).
# The guest is Arm, the runner is x64: the native Arm rustc builds x86_64-pc-windows-msvc by default (the runner's architecture; the
# programs run under Prism emulation, only cargo-nextest.exe is the native Arm build), the control line says so, and
# PADDOCK_MEMBER_GATE_WIN_TARGET=aarch64-pc-windows-msvc builds natively.
#
# Exit: 0 passed, 100 tests failed, 75 not measured (the VM is busy or broken, the toolchain could not be fetched or unpacked).
# The control line `other-os-control: os=windows tree=<tree> ...` and the verdict line `other-os-result: failed=<n>` are printed by
# the guest command itself (the ci-like wrapper turns a guest exit 100 into 1, so the verdict travels as a line).
# Environment: PADDOCK_MEMBER_GATE_SCRATCH (default <dev disk>/dev-targets/scratch/member-gate-windows), PADDOCK_MEMBER_GATE_SNAPSHOT
# (default buildtools-baseline).
set -uo pipefail
here="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
root="$(cd "$here/.." && pwd)"
tree="${1:?usage: member-gate-windows.sh <tree> <spec>...}"; shift
[ $# -gt 0 ] || { echo "::error::member-gate-windows: no spec given. Usage: member-gate-windows.sh <tree> <spec>..." >&2; exit 2; }
# The whole run holds the lock (busy is exit 75 with the holder named); a holder that started us passes it on.
if ! bash "$here/vm-lock-run.sh" --check; then
  exec bash "$here/vm-lock-run.sh" member-gate-windows -- bash "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" "$tree" "$@"
fi
fail() { echo "::error::member-gate-windows: $1. Next step: $2" >&2; exit 75; }
lock() { sed -n "s/^$1=//p" "$here/vm-win/member-gate-tools.lock" | head -1 | tr -d "\""; }

[ "$(git -C "$root" rev-parse 'HEAD^{tree}')" = "$tree" ] || fail "HEAD's tree is not $tree" "run it from the worktree that holds the merge"
commit=$(git -C "$root" rev-parse HEAD)
scratch="${PADDOCK_MEMBER_GATE_SCRATCH:-/Volumes/vault-dev/dev-targets/scratch/member-gate-windows}"
cache="$scratch/cache"; mkdir -p "$cache" || fail "cannot make $cache" "check the disk"
snapshot="${PADDOCK_MEMBER_GATE_SNAPSHOT:-buildtools-baseline}"

# Every spec is native now; the only thing to check is the shape.
for spec in "$@"; do
  read -r kind _ _ <<<"$spec"
  [ "$kind" = nextest ] || fail "unknown spec kind '$kind' (the Windows run takes nextest specs only)" "use nextest"
done

# The host-side cache: the toolchain of rust-toolchain.toml as one archive, and the aarch64 cargo-nextest.exe.
channel=$(python3 -I -c 'import sys,tomllib; print(tomllib.load(open(sys.argv[1],"rb"))["toolchain"]["channel"])' "$root/rust-toolchain.toml") \
  || fail "cannot read the channel of rust-toolchain.toml" "check the file"
case "$channel" in [0-9]*.[0-9]*.[0-9]*) ;; *) fail "rust-toolchain.toml names '$channel', not an exact version" "pin an exact version (ER-26)" ;; esac
host=$(lock rust_host); dist=$(lock rust_dist)
gate_target="${PADDOCK_MEMBER_GATE_WIN_TARGET:-$(lock gate_target)}"
prefix_tgz="$cache/rust-prefix-$channel-$host-std-$(lock rust_extra_std | tr " " "+").tar.gz"
if [ ! -f "$prefix_tgz" ]; then
  echo "member-gate-windows: filling the host cache with Rust $channel for $host" >&2
  dl="$cache/rust-$channel-$host.tar.xz"; work="$cache/unpack-$$"
  curl -fsSL --retry 3 -o "$dl" "$dist/rust-$channel-$host.tar.xz" && want=$(curl -fsSL "$dist/rust-$channel-$host.tar.xz.sha256" | awk '{print $1}') \
    || fail "cannot download Rust $channel from $dist" "check the network"
  [ "$(shasum -a 256 "$dl" | awk '{print $1}')" = "$want" ] || { rm -f "$dl"; fail "the Rust $channel archive does not match $dist's .sha256" "try again; if it repeats, the dist changed"; }
  mkdir -p "$work/prefix" && tar -xf "$dl" -C "$work" || fail "cannot unpack the Rust archive" "check the disk"
  for c in $(lock rust_components); do cp -R "$work/rust-$channel-$host/$c/." "$work/prefix/" || fail "the Rust archive has no component $c" "check rust_components in member-gate-tools.lock"; done
  for x in $(lock rust_extra_std); do
    xdl="$cache/$x-$channel.tar.xz"; xt=${x#rust-std-}
    curl -fsSL --retry 3 -o "$xdl" "$dist/rust-std-$channel-$xt.tar.xz" && xwant=$(curl -fsSL "$dist/rust-std-$channel-$xt.tar.xz.sha256" | awk '{print $1}') || fail "cannot download $x" "check the network"
    [ "$(shasum -a 256 "$xdl" | awk '{print $1}')" = "$xwant" ] || { rm -f "$xdl"; fail "$x does not match its .sha256" "try again"; }
    tar -xf "$xdl" -C "$work" && cp -R "$work/rust-std-$channel-$xt/$x/." "$work/prefix/" || fail "cannot unpack $x" "check the archive"
    rm -f "$xdl"
  done
  find "$work/prefix" \( -name '*.pdb' -o -name 'manifest.in' \) -delete
  tar -czf "$prefix_tgz.part" -C "$work/prefix" . && mv "$prefix_tgz.part" "$prefix_tgz" || fail "cannot pack the toolchain" "check the disk"
  rm -rf "$work" "$dl"
fi
nx_zip="$cache/cargo-nextest-$(lock nextest_version)-aarch64.zip"
if [ ! -f "$nx_zip" ]; then
  curl -fsSL --retry 3 -o "$nx_zip" "$(lock nextest_url)" || fail "cannot download $(lock nextest_url)" "check the network"
fi
[ "$(shasum -a 256 "$nx_zip" | awk '{print $1}')" = "$(lock nextest_sha256)" ] || { rm -f "$nx_zip"; fail "cargo-nextest does not match the pinned SHA-256" "the lock file is the reference"; }
nx_exe="$cache/nextest-aarch64/cargo-nextest.exe"
[ -f "$nx_exe" ] || { mkdir -p "$cache/nextest-aarch64" && unzip -q -o "$nx_zip" cargo-nextest.exe -d "$cache/nextest-aarch64" || fail "cannot unpack cargo-nextest" "check the archive"; }

# Node, from the same kind of cache: the exact release the lock file pins, whose major must be .nvmrc's.
[ "$(lock node_version | cut -d. -f1)" = "$(tr -d '[:space:]v' <"$root/.nvmrc")" ] || fail "the pinned Node $(lock node_version) is not .nvmrc's major" "bump node_version in scripts/vm-win/member-gate-tools.lock"
node_zip="$cache/node-$(lock node_version)-win-arm64.zip"
[ -f "$node_zip" ] || curl -fsSL --retry 3 -o "$node_zip" "$(lock node_url)" || fail "cannot download $(lock node_url)" "check the network"
[ "$(shasum -a 256 "$node_zip" | awk '{print $1}')" = "$(lock node_sha256)" ] || { rm -f "$node_zip"; fail "Node does not match the pinned SHA-256" "the lock file is the reference"; }

"$here/vm-win.sh" revert --snapshot "$snapshot" >&2 || fail "cannot revert the VM to $snapshot (is vm-win.sh toolchain-setup done?)" "see docs/testing/windows-test-vm.md"
trap '"$here/vm-win.sh" stop >&2 || true; "$here/vm-win.sh" revert >&2 || true' EXIT
t0=$SECONDS
"$here/vm-win.sh" start >&2 || fail "the VM did not start" "see docs/testing/windows-test-vm.md"
echo "member-gate-windows: VM started from $snapshot in $((SECONDS - t0)) s" >&2

# In the guest (Git bash, runner-like): control line, the toolchain unpacked from what was copied in, then each spec.
specs=$(printf '%s\n' "$@")
step='set +e
d=$(cygpath -u "$CI_LIKE_DIR")
echo "other-os-control: os=windows tree=$(git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}) autocrlf=$(git config core.autocrlf) shell=bash temp=$TEMP ci-env=${CI:-unset} target=$TARGET vm-arch=aarch64 runner-arch=x86_64"
mkdir -p "$d/rust" && tar -xf "$d"/rust-prefix-*.tar.gz -C "$d/rust" || { echo "other-os-fatal: cannot unpack the toolchain"; echo "other-os-result: failed=-1"; exit 0; }
mkdir -p "$d/node" && /c/Windows/System32/tar.exe -xf "$(cygpath -w "$(ls "$d"/node-*-win-arm64.zip)")" -C "$(cygpath -w "$d/node")" --strip-components 1 || { echo "other-os-fatal: cannot unpack node"; echo "other-os-result: failed=-1"; exit 0; }
export CARGO_BUILD_TARGET="$TARGET" PATH="$d/rust/bin:$d/node:$d:$PATH" CARGO_HOME="$d/cargo-home" CARGO_TARGET_DIR="$d/target" RUSTUP_AUTO_INSTALL=0 PADDOCK_JOB_TEMP="$TEMP"
echo "other-os-guest: $(rustc --version) / $(cargo --version) / $(cargo-nextest.exe nextest --version | head -1) / node $(node --version) / link=$(command -v link.exe || echo none)"
fail=0
while IFS= read -r spec; do
  read -r kind ws pkg filter <<<"$spec"
  echo "::group::nextest $ws $pkg"
  # The other tools whose cargo metadata the paddock-dev tests read offline (ci.yml: "Fetch the other tools dependencies").
  if [ "$pkg" = paddock-dev ]; then for tl in heavy wiki; do (cd "tools/$tl" && cargo fetch --locked >/dev/null 2>&1) || echo "other-os-warn: cargo fetch --locked failed in tools/$tl"; done; fi
  (cd "$ws" && cargo nextest run -p "$pkg" --profile ci --locked --no-fail-fast ${filter:+-E "$filter"} 2>&1)
  c=$?
  echo "::endgroup::"
  case "$c" in 0) ;; 100) fail=1 ;; *) echo "other-os-fatal: $pkg exited $c (a build or setup failure, not failed tests)"; fail=-1 ;; esac
done <<<"$SPECS"
echo "other-os-result: failed=$fail"'
step="SPECS='$specs'; TARGET='$gate_target'; WARM='${PADDOCK_MEMBER_GATE_MEASURE_WARM:-0}'; export CARGO_TERM_COLOR=never NO_COLOR=1
$step"
log="$scratch/guest.log"
t1=$SECONDS
timeout "${PADDOCK_MEMBER_GATE_WIN_MAX:-2700}" "$here/vm-win.sh" run --ci-like --ref "$commit" --tools-provided --with "$prefix_tgz" --with "$nx_exe" --with "$node_zip" -- "$step" 2>&1 | tee "$log"
rc=${PIPESTATUS[0]}
echo "member-gate-windows: guest run took $((SECONDS - t1)) s" >&2
[ "$rc" != 124 ] || { echo "::error::member-gate-windows: the guest run was ended after ${PADDOCK_MEMBER_GATE_WIN_MAX:-2700} s (a hang or a starved guest). Next step: read the output above; set PADDOCK_MEMBER_GATE_WIN_MAX to allow longer" >&2; exit 75; }
[ "$rc" = 0 ] || { echo "::error::member-gate-windows: the guest run exited $rc, not a verdict" >&2; exit 75; }
case "$(tr -d '\r' <"$log" | sed -n 's/^other-os-result: failed=\(-*[0-9]*\)$/\1/p' | tail -1)" in
  0) exit 0 ;;
  "") echo "::error::member-gate-windows: the guest printed no other-os-result line" >&2; exit 75 ;;
  -1) echo "::error::member-gate-windows: the guest could not set up or build (see other-os-fatal above)" >&2; exit 75 ;;
  *) exit 100 ;;
esac

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Holds the TRAIN CI RESERVATION while a command runs: the integrator wraps a train's whole CI sequence in it, so no member run (a
# trial, the member gate, any dispatch that is not a train's) takes the gap between two workflows of the sequence (run 8166,
# 2026-11-16: it did, and train 12's Pitwall gate waited behind it on the macOS runner). `./dev ci dispatch` of a non-train ref and
# the member gate (`merge check --gates`) wait on it, bounded; a `train/*` dispatch never does. It is the machine's test-machines
# lock mechanism (scripts/vm-lock.sh: one kernel file lock, freed when the holder dies) on its own folder, <lock root>/train-ci
# (PADDOCK_TRAIN_CI_LOCK_ROOT overrides it). The lock has no time cap of its own, so wrap a sequence that ends (`timeout 8h`, as
# below): the hold is bounded by the command it wraps.
#
#   scripts/train-ci-hold.sh <label> -- <command...>          for example:
#   scripts/train-ci-hold.sh train-12 -- timeout 8h bash -c './dev ci dispatch pitwall.yml --ref train/x --max 30m && ./dev wait --ci-run <id> --max 3h'
#   scripts/train-ci-hold.sh --status                          the holder, if any
#
# Exit codes are the lock's: 75 when another train sequence holds it (a second sequence waits or reports), the command's own otherwise.
set -u
here="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
if [ -z "${PADDOCK_TRAIN_CI_LOCK_ROOT:-}" ]; then
  default="$(cd "$here/.." && bash ./dev places --get lock-root 2>/dev/null)" || { echo "::error::train-ci-hold: the lock folder cannot be derived. Next step: set PADDOCK_TRAIN_CI_LOCK_ROOT" >&2; exit 3; }
  PADDOCK_TRAIN_CI_LOCK_ROOT="$(dirname "$default")/train-ci"
fi
mkdir -p "$PADDOCK_TRAIN_CI_LOCK_ROOT" || exit 3
export PADDOCK_TRAIN_CI_LOCK_ROOT
export PADDOCK_VM_LOCK_ROOT="$PADDOCK_TRAIN_CI_LOCK_ROOT"
if [ "${1:-}" = "--status" ]; then
  cd "$here/.." && bash ./dev ci slot status --max 1 --root "$PADDOCK_TRAIN_CI_LOCK_ROOT"
  exit $?
fi
exec bash "$here/vm-lock-run.sh" "${1:?usage: train-ci-hold.sh <label> -- <command...>}" "${@:2}"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# The cross-account pipe check of ADR 0092 DF-3 (the test plan in docs/adr/0092-*.md), run on the local Windows test VM (ER-14: local only,
# never CI; the VM lock of scripts/vm-lock.sh applies). Account A (paddock-admin) serves a pipe that EVERY account may open, with
# `paddock-ipc-test-child serve-open`; account B (paddock-test) runs the test `a_pipe_served_by_another_account_is_refused_before_the_token_is_sent`.
# Because the pipe's access list lets B in, B reaches `Client::connect_on`'s `check_server_is_me`: with the check the test passes ("not
# served by your account"); with the call deleted (the `ipc_it_mut` build) the client is let in and the test must FAIL (ER-33). A pipe with the
# default owner-only access list would prove nothing: B would be refused at open and the check would never run.
#
# Inputs (built beforehand, paths below): $L/t-crates/... holds the test binary `it-*.exe` and `paddock-ipc-test-child.exe`; $L/t-mut/... the
# same test binary built with the `check_server_is_me` call removed. Output: $O/{server.log,xacct-*.log}.
set -u
ROOT=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)
export PADDOCK_AGENT_ID=${PADDOCK_AGENT_ID:-implementer:dyno-vm}
L=${DYNO_VM_DIR:-$("$ROOT/dev" places --get dev-targets --repo "$ROOT")/dyno-vm} || exit 2
V="bash $ROOT/scripts/vm-win.sh"
A=$L/t-crates/aarch64-pc-windows-msvc/debug
M=$L/t-mut/aarch64-pc-windows-msvc/debug
IT=${IT_EXE:-it-d04254c346498c95.exe}
O=$L/run/p4; mkdir -p "$O"
PIPE='\\.\pipe\paddock-xacct-open'
ph() { echo "[$(date +%H:%M:%S)] $*"; }
g() { $V ssh "$@" 2>&1 | grep -v -E "post-quantum|store now|upgraded"; }
die() { echo "::error::$*"; exit 1; }

ph "revert and start the VM"
$V revert clean-baseline >"$O/rv.log" 2>&1 || die "the VM could not be reverted to clean-baseline; next step: see $O/rv.log and scripts/vm-lock.sh"
$V start >"$O/start.log" 2>&1 </dev/null || die "the VM did not start; next step: see $O/start.log, check the VM lock and the host's load"
[ "$(g 'echo up' | tr -d '\r' | tail -1)" = "up" ] || die "the VM started but does not answer over ssh; next step: see $O/start.log, then stop and revert it by hand"
ph "status $($V status)"
g 'New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force C:\paddock-test\dv | Out-Null; "up"' >/dev/null
# The test program is in deps/ (cargo before 1.100) or build/<package>/<hash>/out/ (1.100): whichever layout built it.
# conformance: layout-guess — searches `deps` and `build` both, so it finds the test binary in either cargo layout
find_test() { find "$1/deps" "$1/build" -type f -name "$2" 2>/dev/null | head -1; }
for p in "$(find_test "$A" "$IT") ipc_it.exe" "$(find_test "$M" "$IT") ipc_it_mut.exe" "$A/paddock-ipc-test-child.exe child.exe"; do
  set -- $p; [ -f "$1" ] || die "missing build output $1; next step: build it (see the header)"
  $V put paddock-test "$1" "C:/paddock-test/dv/$2" 2>&1 | tail -1
done

ph "A = paddock-admin: serve a pipe every account may open"
( $V ssh --admin "& C:\\paddock-test\\dv\\child.exe serve-open $PIPE" > "$O/server.log" 2>&1 </dev/null & echo $! > "$O/server.pid" )
for i in $(seq 1 30); do grep -q "^ready" "$O/server.log" 2>/dev/null && break; sleep 2; done
grep -q "^ready" "$O/server.log" || die "the pipe server did not report ready; next step: see $O/server.log"

result=0
for v in ipc_it ipc_it_mut; do
  ph "=== B = paddock-test, $v"
  g "cd C:\\paddock-test\\dv; \$env:PADDOCK_OTHER_ACCOUNT_PIPE='$PIPE'; whoami; & .\\$v.exe a_pipe_served_by_another_account --nocapture 2>&1 | Select-Object -Last 25; 'EXIT=' + \$LASTEXITCODE" | tee "$O/xacct-$v.log" | cut -c1-330
  code=$(grep -o 'EXIT=[0-9]*' "$O/xacct-$v.log" | tail -1 | cut -d= -f2)
  # With the check the test passes (EXIT=0); without it the test must fail (ER-33).
  case $v in ipc_it) [ "$code" = "0" ] || { echo "::error::with the check the cross-account test did not pass (EXIT=$code); next step: see $O/xacct-$v.log"; result=1; } ;;
             ipc_it_mut) [ "$code" != "0" ] || { echo "::error::the probe cannot see the difference: the build without the check also passed (ER-33)"; result=1; } ;;
  esac
done

ph "stop the pipe server, stop and revert the VM"
kill "$(cat "$O/server.pid")" 2>/dev/null
g 'Get-Process child -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Stop-Process -Force; "server stopped"'
$V stop >/dev/null 2>&1; $V revert clean-baseline 2>&1 | tail -1
ph "status $($V status); result=$result"
exit $result

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Drives the local Windows 11 Arm test VM (VMware Fusion, headless through vmrun; commands inside it over SSH).
# Local only, never CI. Setup and the update test: docs/testing/windows-test-vm.md.
#
#   scripts/vm-win.sh start [--no-wait]       start headless and wait until SSH answers
#   scripts/vm-win.sh stop                    shut Windows down (over SSH), power off if it does not stop in time
#   scripts/vm-win.sh ssh [--admin] [cmd...]  SSH as paddock-test (or paddock-admin); a shell without a command
#   scripts/vm-win.sh put|get <user> <src> <dst>   scp a file to / from the guest (user paddock-test or paddock-admin; dst/src guest path)
#   scripts/vm-win.sh gui-setup               one-time: auto-logon of paddock-test + the in-session job runner, snapshot gui-baseline
#   scripts/vm-win.sh job <file.ps1> [secs]   run a script ON the desktop of paddock-test (UI Automation works), print its output; exit = its code
#   scripts/vm-win.sh snapshot <name>         take a snapshot
#   scripts/vm-win.sh revert [name]           revert to a snapshot (default clean-baseline); the VM is then off
#   scripts/vm-win.sh revert --snapshot <name>   the same, named with a flag (for example admin-baseline)
#   scripts/vm-win.sh admin-setup             one-time: from clean-baseline, paddock-test joins Administrators, UAC consent on the normal
#                                             desktop (+ auto-logon and job runner as gui-setup), snapshot admin-baseline; reverts at the end
#   scripts/vm-win.sh run --ci-like [--ref <commit>] [--with <file>]... [--tools-provided] [--] <bash command...>
#                                             in the RUNNING guest, run the command the way the Gitea Windows CI runner starts a step: runner-style
#                                             temp folder (Authenticated Users may write), a git checkout of <ref> (default HEAD) with core.autocrlf=true
#                                             sent as a git bundle of its tree, --with files (built on the Mac: the guest has no toolchain) copied to the
#                                             folder named by $CI_LIKE_DIR (a Windows path; cygpath -u in bash), Git bash (--noprofile --norc -e -o pipefail) with Git's bin first on PATH, CI env;
#                                             prints a self-check first; exit = the command's (75: not measured). scripts/vm-win/ci-like.ps1
#   scripts/vm-win.sh toolchain-setup         one-time: snapshot pre-buildtools-<date> (the rollback point), then from clean-baseline install the VS 2022
#                                             Build Tools LTSC 17.12 (pinned installer, checksum, Authenticode) as paddock-admin, snapshot buildtools-baseline;
#                                             reverts to clean-baseline at the end. The member gate (scripts/member-gate-windows.sh) starts from buildtools-baseline
#   scripts/vm-win.sh status | ip             running or stopped / the guest's address
#   scripts/vm-win.sh install                 one-time: install Windows headless, wait for setup to power off
#   scripts/vm-win.sh baseline                one-time: check setup finished, detach the discs, take clean-baseline
#
# Only ever acts on <dev disk>/vm-data/paddock-win11-test (docs/dev-setup.md): any other folder in PADDOCK_WIN_VM_DIR is refused before vmrun,
# ssh or scp run (vm-win/target.sh), except a fake VM under $TMPDIR with a fake FUSION_APP, for this script's own tests.
# Any other VM on this Mac is never started, stopped or changed. Only if the VM is encrypted (option A, virtual TPM) is its password read
# from the login keychain (service paddock-win11-test-vm, account vmrun) and passed to vmrun as -vp.
set -euo pipefail
. "$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)/vm-win/target.sh"

dir=${PADDOCK_WIN_VM_DIR:-$WIN_VM_DIR}
fusion=${FUSION_APP:-/Applications/VMware Fusion.app}
lib="$fusion/Contents/Library"
name=paddock-win11-test
vmx="$dir/vm/$name.vmwarevm/$name.vmx"
mac=00:50:56:2a:d0:c7
leases=/var/db/vmware/vmnet-dhcpd-vmnet8.leases # PADDOCK_VM_LEASES only in fake mode (guard)
max_load=${PADDOCK_VM_MAX_LOAD:-25}
ssh_deadline=${PADDOCK_VM_SSH_DEADLINE:-300}
install_deadline=${PADDOCK_VM_INSTALL_DEADLINE:-7200}
off_deadline=${PADDOCK_VM_OFF_DEADLINE:-180} # the guest's clean power-off after gui-setup and admin-setup
cleanup_deadline=${PADDOCK_VM_CLEANUP_DEADLINE:-120} # each vmrun call of admin-setup's cleanup
step_deadline=${PADDOCK_VM_STEP_DEADLINE:-300} # one PowerShell step in the guest (gui-setup, admin-setup)
baseline=clean-baseline

die() { echo "vm-win: $*" >&2; exit 1; }
usage() { sed -n '2,30p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; }

guard() {
  case "$dir/" in "$HOME"/*) die "PADDOCK_WIN_VM_DIR must not be under \$HOME (ER-14): $dir" ;; esac
  check_target "$dir" "$fusion"
  [ "$FAKE_VM" = 1 ] && leases=${PADDOCK_VM_LEASES:-$leases}
  [ -f "$vmx" ] || die "no test VM at $vmx; run scripts/vm-win/prepare.sh first"
  [ -x "$lib/vmrun" ] || die "vmrun not found in $lib (set FUSION_APP)"
}

# An encrypted VM (option A: TPM files encrypted) has encryption.* keys in its .vmx and needs the password from the login
# keychain; an unencrypted VM (option B, the default set-up) never reads the keychain.
encrypted() { grep -q '^encryption\.' "$vmx"; }

vmrun() {
  local cmd=$1; shift
  if encrypted; then
    local pw
    pw=$(security find-generic-password -s paddock-win11-test-vm -a vmrun -w 2>/dev/null) ||
      die "the VM is encrypted but the keychain has no item paddock-win11-test-vm/vmrun (docs/testing/windows-test-vm.md, TPM)"
    ${vmrun_prefix:-} "$lib/vmrun" -T fusion -vp "$pw" "$cmd" "$vmx" "$@"
  else
    ${vmrun_prefix:-} "$lib/vmrun" -T fusion "$cmd" "$vmx" "$@"
  fi
}

running() { "$lib/vmrun" -T fusion list | grep -Fxq "$vmx"; }

load_ok() {
  local load
  load=$(sysctl -n vm.loadavg | awk '{print $2}')
  awk -v l="$load" -v m="$max_load" 'BEGIN{exit !(l<m)}' || die "1-minute load $load is not under $max_load; try again later"
}

# The guest's IPv4 address: the newest NAT DHCP lease for the VM's fixed MAC address (vmrun getGuestIPAddress needs
# VMware Tools, which Arm guests may lack).
ip() {
  [ -r "$leases" ] || die "cannot read $leases"
  awk -v mac="$mac" '
    /^lease / { addr = $2 }
    /hardware ethernet/ { m = tolower($3); sub(/;$/, "", m); if (m == mac) found = addr }
    END { if (found == "") exit 1; print found }
  ' "$leases" || die "no DHCP lease for $mac yet (is the VM running?)"
}

ssh_to() { # user, then ssh arguments
  local user=$1; shift
  local host; host=$(ip)
  # ssh_prefix=exec (set by a caller that runs this in a background subshell) makes the subshell BE ssh, so a kill reaches it.
  ${ssh_prefix:-} ssh -i "$dir/keys/$user" -o IdentitiesOnly=yes -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=5 -o ServerAliveInterval=5 -o ServerAliveCountMax=3 \
    -o UserKnownHostsFile="$dir/keys/known_hosts" -o StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new "$user@$host" "$@"
}

scp_via() { # user, then scp arguments with @ placeholders for user@host
  local user=$1; shift
  local host; host=$(ip)
  scp -q -i "$dir/keys/$user" -o IdentitiesOnly=yes -o BatchMode=yes -o ServerAliveInterval=5 -o ServerAliveCountMax=3 -o UserKnownHostsFile="$dir/keys/known_hosts" -o StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new "${@//@HOST@/$user@$host}"
}

wait_ssh() {
  local end=$((SECONDS + ssh_deadline))
  until (ssh_to paddock-test 'exit 0') >/dev/null 2>&1; do # subshell: no lease yet is not fatal
    [ $SECONDS -lt $end ] || die "SSH did not answer within ${ssh_deadline}s"
    running || die "the VM stopped while waiting for SSH"
    sleep 3
  done
}

wait_off() { # deadline in seconds, label
  local end=$((SECONDS + $1)) next=$((SECONDS + 60))
  while running; do
    [ $SECONDS -lt $end ] || return 1
    if [ $SECONDS -ge $next ]; then echo "  $2: still working ($((SECONDS / 60)) min)"; next=$((SECONDS + 60)); fi
    sleep 5
  done
}

# A warning, never a refusal (ADR 0087 amendment, d8-quiet guard): heavy work on the disk that holds the VM slows its boot and the tests.
quiet_warn() {
  local load disk phys mbs
  load=$(sysctl -n vm.loadavg | awk '{print $2}') || true
  disk=$(df "$dir" 2>/dev/null | awk 'NR==2{print $1}' | sed 's|^/dev/||; s/s[0-9]*$//') || true
  # An APFS volume sits on a synthesized disk that iostat cannot watch; measure its physical store.
  phys=$(diskutil info "$disk" 2>/dev/null | awk '/APFS Physical Store/{print $NF}' | sed 's/s[0-9]*$//') || true
  mbs=$(iostat -d -c 2 -w 1 "${phys:-$disk}" 2>/dev/null | awk 'END{print $3}') || true
  echo "  before boot: 1-minute load $load, disk $disk busy ${mbs:-unknown} MB/s"
  awk -v m="${mbs:-0}" 'BEGIN{exit !(m+0>50)}' && echo "::warning::the VM's disk ($disk) is busy ($mbs MB/s); the boot and the tests will be slow and slow numbers mean little. Next step: wait for the other work to end, or go on knowing this." >&2
  return 0
}

has_snapshot() { vmrun listSnapshots | tail -n +2 | grep -Fxq "$1"; }

# A shutdown request over SSH, in the background: the session can hang while Windows shuts down (seen 2026-11-11, 13 min). The caller
# waits for the VM to be off (wait_off), then reaps the request with reap_shutdown, which ends it if it is still open.
shut_pid=""; shut_err=""
shutdown_guest() { # one PowerShell command line to run as paddock-admin (it must end in the shutdown)
  shut_err=$(mktemp)
  (ssh_prefix="exec" ssh_to paddock-admin "$1") >/dev/null 2>"$shut_err" &
  shut_pid=$!
}
reap_shutdown() { # ends the request if still open, waits (bounded: it was killed), and reports a failed request (ER-27)
  [ -n "$shut_pid" ] || return 0
  local rc=0 killed=0
  if kill -0 "$shut_pid" 2>/dev/null; then
    killed=1; kill "$shut_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
    for _ in 1 2 3 4 5; do kill -0 "$shut_pid" 2>/dev/null || break; sleep 1; done
    kill -9 "$shut_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
  fi
  wait "$shut_pid" 2>/dev/null || rc=$?
  if [ $killed = 1 ]; then echo "  the shutdown request was still open after the VM went off; ended it"
  elif [ $rc -ne 0 ]; then echo "::warning::shutdown request: exit $rc; ssh said: $(tail -n 3 "$shut_err" | tr '\n' ' ')" >&2; fi
  rm -f "$shut_err"; shut_pid=""
}

# bounded <secs> <command...>: run it in the background and give up after <secs> (the command must exec its last program, so a kill reaches it).
bounded() {
  local limit=$1 p end; shift
  "$@" & p=$!
  end=$((SECONDS + limit))
  while kill -0 "$p" 2>/dev/null; do
    if [ $SECONDS -ge $end ]; then
      kill "$p" 2>/dev/null || true; sleep 1; kill -9 "$p" 2>/dev/null || true
      wait "$p" 2>/dev/null || true
      echo "::error::no answer within ${limit}s: $*" >&2
      return 124
    fi
    sleep 1
  done
  wait "$p"
}
vmrun_exec() { vmrun_prefix="exec" vmrun "$@"; } # for bounded: the subshell becomes vmrun, so a kill reaches it
ssh_admin_exec() { ssh_prefix="exec" ssh_to paddock-admin "$@"; }

# The refused state before a snapshot: a run-win.mjs VNC password must never end up in a baseline (vmx-edit.mjs strips it after a run).
vmx_vnc_free() { ! grep -q '^RemoteDisplay\.vnc\.' "$vmx"; }

# Shared by gui-setup and admin-setup: the auto-logon of paddock-test and the in-session job runner (gui-setup.ps1 + logon-runner.ps1).
# Returns 1 and sets runner_step when a step fails. $1: the VM-local paddock-test password. $2...: more scripts to copy (run by the caller).
runner_step=""
install_gui_runner() {
  local pw=$1 here; shift
  here=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
  local f
  for f in logon-runner.ps1 gui-setup.ps1 "$@"; do
    runner_step="copy $f"
    (scp_via paddock-admin "$here/vm-win/$f" "@HOST@:C:/paddock-test/$f") || return 1
  done
  runner_step="gui-setup.ps1"
  bounded "$step_deadline" ssh_admin_exec "powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File C:\\paddock-test\\gui-setup.ps1 -TestPassword '$pw' -RunnerSource C:\\paddock-test\\logon-runner.ps1" || return 1
}
# The last guest step of both: delete the setup scripts, then shut down (the request runs in the background, see shutdown_guest).
SETUP_SHUTDOWN='Remove-Item C:\paddock-test\gui-setup.ps1, C:\paddock-test\admin-setup.ps1 -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; shutdown /s /t 0'

# admin-setup's cleanup: whatever ends it early (a failed step, TERM, INT, HUP, a hang that was killed), the VM ends stopped and reverted to
# clean-baseline. It is the EXIT trap, set before the lock (scripts/vm-lock.sh runs it FIRST, with the lock still held, then releases the
# lock). Each vmrun call is bounded (PADDOCK_VM_CLEANUP_DEADLINE). Not covered: SIGKILL of this script and a lost host; then run
# `vm-win.sh stop && vm-win.sh revert`.
admin_active=0; admin_ok=0
admin_cleanup() {
  [ "$admin_active" = 1 ] && [ "$admin_ok" != 1 ] || return 0
  jobs -p | xargs kill 2>/dev/null || true # a background step (bounded, a shutdown request) must not outlive this script
  echo "::error::admin-setup did not finish: stopping the VM and reverting to $baseline ($baseline itself was never changed)" >&2
  if running; then
    bounded "$cleanup_deadline" vmrun_exec stop hard >&2 || echo "::error::could not power the VM off. Next step: stop it in Fusion (never leave it running), then scripts/vm-win.sh revert" >&2
  fi
  bounded "$cleanup_deadline" vmrun_exec revertToSnapshot "$baseline" >&2 || echo "::error::could not revert to $baseline. Next step: scripts/vm-win.sh revert" >&2
}
trap admin_cleanup EXIT
admin_fail() { echo "::error::admin-setup failed at: $1 (read the output above); the cleanup follows" >&2; exit 1; }

cmd=${1:-}
[ $# -gt 0 ] && shift
# One user of the test VM at a time (interim lock, scripts/vm-lock.sh): only the commands that change or load the guest.
case $cmd in
  start | stop | ssh | put | get | run | gui-setup | admin-setup | toolchain-setup | job | snapshot | revert | install | baseline)
    . "$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)/vm-lock.sh"; vm_lock_acquire "vm-win-$cmd" ;;
esac
case $cmd in
  start)
    guard
    if running; then echo "already running"; else load_ok; quiet_warn; vmrun start nogui; fi
    [ "${1:-}" = "--no-wait" ] || { wait_ssh; echo "ready: $(ip)"; }
    ;;
  stop)
    guard
    running || { echo "already stopped"; exit 0; }
    shutdown_guest 'shutdown /s /t 0'
    wait_off 120 "shutting down" || { echo "  no clean shutdown in 120 s; powering off"; vmrun stop hard; }
    reap_shutdown
    echo "stopped"
    ;;
  ssh)
    guard
    user=paddock-test
    [ "${1:-}" = "--admin" ] && { user=paddock-admin; shift; }
    ssh_to "$user" "$@"
    ;;
  put)
    guard
    [ $# -eq 3 ] || die "usage: vm-win.sh put <user> <local file> <guest path>"
    scp_via "$1" "$2" "@HOST@:$3"
    ;;
  get)
    guard
    [ $# -eq 3 ] || die "usage: vm-win.sh get <user> <guest path> <local file>"
    scp_via "$1" "@HOST@:$2" "$3"
    ;;
  run)
    guard
    [ "${1:-}" = "--ci-like" ] || die "usage: vm-win.sh run --ci-like [--ref <commit>] [--] <bash command...> (--ci-like is the only mode)"
    shift
    ref=HEAD
    tools_provided=""
    withs=()
    while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
      case $1 in
        --ref) ref=${2:-}; [ -n "$ref" ] || die "usage: vm-win.sh run --ci-like --ref <commit> ..."; shift 2 ;;
        --tools-provided) tools_provided="-ToolsProvided"; shift ;;
        --with) [ -f "${2:-}" ] || die "--with needs a file: ${2:-}"; withs+=("$2"); shift 2 ;;
        *) break ;;
      esac
    done
    [ "${1:-}" = "--" ] && shift
    [ $# -gt 0 ] || die "usage: vm-win.sh run --ci-like [--ref <commit>] [--] <bash command...>"
    running || die "the VM is not running: scripts/vm-win.sh start first (clean-baseline; revert and stop when done)"
    here=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
    sha=$(git -C "$here" rev-parse --verify --quiet "$ref^{commit}") || die "no commit $ref in this repository"
    work=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ci-like.XXXXXX")
    # A bundle needs a ref. It is built in a temporary bare repository that borrows the objects of this one (alternates), so no ref is written
    # in the user's repository (whose refs every worktree shares). The ref names a parentless commit with the tree of <ref> (the whole history is
    # 1.7 GB, the tree is small); the guest's git still applies .gitattributes and core.autocrlf to it.
    objs=$(git -C "$here" rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-path objects) || die "cannot find the object folder of this repository"
    git init -q --bare "$work/repo" && echo "$objs" >"$work/repo/objects/info/alternates" || die "cannot make the bundle repository"
    refname=refs/vm-ci-like/head
    commit=$(GIT_AUTHOR_NAME=ci-like GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL=ci-like@localhost GIT_COMMITTER_NAME=ci-like GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL=ci-like@localhost \
      git --git-dir="$work/repo" commit-tree "$sha^{tree}" -m "ci-like checkout of $sha") || die "cannot make the checkout commit for $ref"
    git --git-dir="$work/repo" update-ref "$refname" "$commit"
    git --git-dir="$work/repo" bundle create "$work/src.bundle" "$refname" >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "git bundle failed for $ref"
    printf 'set -e\n%s\n' "$*" >"$work/step.sh" # LF, no CR: bash in the guest reads it as is
    echo "ci-like: tree of ${sha:0:12} ($(du -h "$work/src.bundle" | awk '{print $1}') bundle), ${#withs[@]} extra file(s)"
    gdir=C:/Users/paddock-test/ci-like
    # shellcheck disable=SC2016 # the $env: is PowerShell's
    ssh_to paddock-test 'New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $env:USERPROFILE\ci-like | Out-Null' || die "cannot make the guest folder"
    for f in "$work/src.bundle" "$work/step.sh" "$here/vm-win/ci-like.ps1" ${withs[@]+"${withs[@]}"}; do
      scp_via paddock-test "$f" "@HOST@:$gdir/$(basename "$f")" || die "copy of $(basename "$f") to the guest failed"
    done
    set +e
    ssh_to paddock-test "powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File C:\\Users\\paddock-test\\ci-like\\ci-like.ps1 -Bundle C:\\Users\\paddock-test\\ci-like\\src.bundle -Ref $refname -ScriptFile C:\\Users\\paddock-test\\ci-like\\step.sh $tools_provided" |
      grep -v -e 'post-quantum' -e 'store now' -e 'openssh.com/pq'
    rc=${PIPESTATUS[0]}
    set -e
    rm -rf "$work"
    [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || echo "::error::ci-like run exited $rc (75 = not measured: a control, a missing tool or a PowerShell error, nothing passed; other = the command's own code). Next step: read the output above" >&2
    exit $rc
    ;;
  gui-setup)
    guard
    running || { load_ok; vmrun start nogui; }
    wait_ssh
    pw=$(sed -n 's/^paddock-test=//p' "$dir/keys/setup-passwords")
    [ -n "$pw" ] || die "no paddock-test password in $dir/keys/setup-passwords"
    install_gui_runner "$pw" || die "gui-setup failed at: $runner_step; the VM may still be running: scripts/vm-win.sh stop && scripts/vm-win.sh revert"
    shutdown_guest "$SETUP_SHUTDOWN"
    wait_off "$off_deadline" "shutting down" || { reap_shutdown; vmrun stop hard; die "no clean shutdown in ${off_deadline}s; gui-baseline was not taken from a VM powered off hard. Next step: scripts/vm-win.sh revert, then run gui-setup again"; }
    reap_shutdown
    vmx_vnc_free || die "the .vmx has RemoteDisplay.vnc.* lines (a run-win.mjs run left them?); remove them before a snapshot (scripts/vm-smoke/vmx-edit.mjs stripVnc)"
    has_snapshot gui-baseline && vmrun deleteSnapshot gui-baseline
    vmrun snapshot gui-baseline
    echo "snapshot gui-baseline taken (clean-baseline + auto-logon + job runner); use: vm-win.sh revert gui-baseline"
    ;;
  admin-setup)
    guard
    here=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
    admin_snap=admin-baseline
    running && die "the VM is running; stop it first (admin-setup starts from $baseline and never touches a running VM)"
    has_snapshot "$baseline" || die "no snapshot named $baseline"
    vmx_vnc_free || die "the .vmx has RemoteDisplay.vnc.* lines (a run-win.mjs run left them?); remove them first (scripts/vm-smoke/vmx-edit.mjs stripVnc)"
    pw=$(sed -n 's/^paddock-test=//p' "$dir/keys/setup-passwords")
    [ -n "$pw" ] || die "no paddock-test password in $dir/keys/setup-passwords"
    load_ok
    admin_active=1 # from here on, any exit but the last line stops the VM and reverts it (admin_cleanup, the EXIT trap)
    vmrun revertToSnapshot "$baseline" || admin_fail "revert to $baseline"
    vmrun start nogui || admin_fail "start"
    (wait_ssh) || admin_fail "wait for SSH"
    install_gui_runner "$pw" admin-setup.ps1 || admin_fail "$runner_step"
    bounded "$step_deadline" ssh_admin_exec "powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File C:\\paddock-test\\admin-setup.ps1" || admin_fail "admin-setup.ps1"
    shutdown_guest "$SETUP_SHUTDOWN"
    wait_off "$off_deadline" "shutting down" || { reap_shutdown; admin_fail "clean shutdown (the VM did not power off in ${off_deadline}s; a snapshot of a hard power-off is not taken)"; }
    reap_shutdown
    vmx_vnc_free || admin_fail "the .vmx got RemoteDisplay.vnc.* lines during the run"
    has_snapshot "$admin_snap" && { vmrun deleteSnapshot "$admin_snap" || admin_fail "delete the old $admin_snap"; }
    vmrun snapshot "$admin_snap" || admin_fail "snapshot $admin_snap"
    vmrun revertToSnapshot "$baseline" || admin_fail "final revert to $baseline"
    admin_ok=1
    echo "snapshot $admin_snap taken (clean-baseline + paddock-test in Administrators + UAC consent on the normal desktop + auto-logon and job runner); reverted to $baseline; use: vm-win.sh revert --snapshot $admin_snap"
    ;;
  toolchain-setup)
    guard
    here=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
    bt_snap=buildtools-baseline
    pre_snap=${PADDOCK_VM_PRE_SNAPSHOT:-pre-buildtools-$(date +%Y-%m-%d)}
    bt_exe=${PADDOCK_BUILDTOOLS_INSTALLER:?set PADDOCK_BUILDTOOLS_INSTALLER to the downloaded vs_BuildTools.exe (the host checks it too)}
    bt_sha=${PADDOCK_BUILDTOOLS_SHA256:?set PADDOCK_BUILDTOOLS_SHA256 to its pinned SHA-256}
    [ "$(shasum -a 256 "$bt_exe" | awk '{print $1}')" = "$bt_sha" ] || die "the installer's SHA-256 is not the pinned $bt_sha"
    bt_deadline=${PADDOCK_BUILDTOOLS_DEADLINE:-5400}
    running && die "the VM is running; stop it first (toolchain-setup starts from $baseline and never touches a running VM)"
    has_snapshot "$baseline" || die "no snapshot named $baseline"
    vmx_vnc_free || die "the .vmx has RemoteDisplay.vnc.* lines; remove them first"
    load_ok
    admin_active=1 # the cleanup (EXIT trap) stops the VM and reverts it to clean-baseline on any early exit
    vmrun revertToSnapshot "$baseline" || admin_fail "revert to $baseline"
    has_snapshot "$pre_snap" || vmrun snapshot "$pre_snap" || admin_fail "snapshot $pre_snap"
    echo "rollback point: snapshot $pre_snap (a copy of $baseline's state taken before the change)"
    vmrun start nogui || admin_fail "start"
    (wait_ssh) || admin_fail "wait for SSH"
    started=$SECONDS
    for f in "$bt_exe:vs_BuildTools.exe" "$here/vm-win/buildtools-setup.ps1:buildtools-setup.ps1"; do
      (scp_via paddock-admin "${f%%:*}" "@HOST@:C:/paddock-test/${f##*:}") || admin_fail "copy ${f##*:}"
    done
    # Detached in the guest (a scheduled task as SYSTEM: it survives the SSH session and has the rights), then polled with short SSH
    # calls that may fail while the installer starves the guest. Each poll prints the installer's own last log line (ER-18).
    bt_cmd="powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File C:\\paddock-test\\buildtools-setup.ps1 -Installer C:\\paddock-test\\vs_BuildTools.exe -Sha256 $bt_sha"
    ssh_to paddock-admin "schtasks /create /tn paddock-buildtools /tr \"$bt_cmd\" /sc once /st 00:00 /ru SYSTEM /rl HIGHEST /f; schtasks /run /tn paddock-buildtools" || admin_fail "start buildtools-setup.ps1"
    bt_end=$((SECONDS + bt_deadline)); bt_next=$((SECONDS + 60)); bt_code=""; bt_started=0
    while [ -z "$bt_code" ]; do
      [ $SECONDS -lt $bt_end ] || admin_fail "buildtools-setup.ps1 did not finish within ${bt_deadline}s"
      sleep 15
      bt_out=$(ssh_to paddock-admin 'if (Test-Path C:\paddock-test\buildtools.done) { "DONE " + (Get-Content C:\paddock-test\buildtools.done).Trim() } else { $l = Get-ChildItem C:\Windows\Temp, $env:TEMP -Filter dd_*.log -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Sort LastWriteTime | Select -Last 1; if ($l) { "LOG " + $l.Name + " " + $l.Length + " bytes, " + $l.LastWriteTime.ToString("HH:mm:ss") + ": " + ((Get-Content $l.FullName -Tail 1) -replace "\s+", " ") } elseif (Test-Path C:\paddock-test\buildtools.log) { "LOG buildtools.log: " + (Get-Content C:\paddock-test\buildtools.log -Tail 1) } else { "NOLOG the task has written nothing yet" } }' 2>/dev/null | grep -E '^(DONE|LOG|NOLOG)' | head -1) || true
      case "$bt_out" in DONE\ [01]) bt_code=${bt_out#DONE } ;; esac
      if [ $SECONDS -ge $bt_next ]; then echo "  buildtools ($(( (SECONDS - started) / 60 )) min): ${bt_out:-no answer from the guest (it may be busy)}" | cut -c1-240; bt_next=$((SECONDS + 60)); fi
    done
    ssh_to paddock-admin 'Get-Content C:\paddock-test\buildtools.log' 2>/dev/null | grep -E 'buildtools-setup:' || true
    [ "$bt_code" = 0 ] || admin_fail "buildtools-setup.ps1 reported failure (exit $bt_code)"
    echo "buildtools-setup took $((SECONDS - started)) s"
    shutdown_guest 'Remove-Item C:\paddock-test\vs_BuildTools.exe, C:\paddock-test\buildtools-setup.ps1 -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; schtasks /delete /tn paddock-buildtools /f; shutdown /s /t 0'
    wait_off "$off_deadline" "shutting down" || { reap_shutdown; admin_fail "clean shutdown (a snapshot of a hard power-off is not taken)"; }
    reap_shutdown
    vmx_vnc_free || admin_fail "the .vmx got RemoteDisplay.vnc.* lines during the run"
    has_snapshot "$bt_snap" && { vmrun deleteSnapshot "$bt_snap" || admin_fail "delete the old $bt_snap"; }
    vmrun snapshot "$bt_snap" || admin_fail "snapshot $bt_snap"
    vmrun revertToSnapshot "$baseline" || admin_fail "final revert to $baseline"
    admin_ok=1
    echo "snapshot $bt_snap taken (clean-baseline + VS Build Tools); rollback point $pre_snap; reverted to $baseline; use: vm-win.sh revert --snapshot $bt_snap"
    ;;
  job)
    guard
    [ -f "${1:-}" ] || die "usage: vm-win.sh job <file.ps1> [timeout secs]"
    limit=${2:-300}
    id="job-$(date +%s)-$$"
    # The runner starts at the console logon of paddock-test; wait for it (a heartbeat file newer than 10 s).
    end=$((SECONDS + 300))
    until ssh_to paddock-test '$f=Get-Item C:\paddock-test\runner.alive -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; if ($f -and ((Get-Date)-$f.LastWriteTime).TotalSeconds -lt 10) { exit 0 } else { exit 1 }' >/dev/null 2>&1; do
      [ $SECONDS -lt $end ] || die "the in-session runner is not alive (is this the gui-baseline snapshot? vm-win.sh gui-setup)"
      sleep 3
    done
    scp_via paddock-test "$1" "@HOST@:C:/paddock-test/jobs/$id.ps1"
    end=$((SECONDS + limit))
    until ssh_to paddock-test "if (Test-Path C:\\paddock-test\\jobs\\$id.done) { exit 0 } else { exit 1 }" >/dev/null 2>&1; do
      [ $SECONDS -lt $end ] || die "job $id did not finish within ${limit}s"
      sleep 2
    done
    ssh_to paddock-test "Get-Content C:\\paddock-test\\jobs\\$id.out" 2>/dev/null | grep -v -e 'post-quantum' -e 'store now' -e 'openssh.com/pq' || true
    code=$(ssh_to paddock-test "(Get-Content C:\\paddock-test\\jobs\\$id.done).Trim()" 2>/dev/null | tail -n 1 | tr -d '\r')
    ssh_to paddock-test "Remove-Item C:\\paddock-test\\jobs\\$id.* -Force" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    exit "${code:-1}"
    ;;
  snapshot)
    guard
    [ -n "${1:-}" ] || die "usage: vm-win.sh snapshot <name>"
    vmrun snapshot "$1"
    echo "snapshot $1 taken"
    ;;
  revert)
    guard
    snap=$baseline
    if [ "${1:-}" = "--snapshot" ]; then snap=${2:-}; [ -n "$snap" ] || die "usage: vm-win.sh revert --snapshot <name>"; elif [ -n "${1:-}" ]; then snap=$1; fi
    has_snapshot "$snap" || die "no snapshot named $snap"
    vmrun revertToSnapshot "$snap"
    echo "reverted to $snap"
    ;;
  status)
    guard
    if running; then echo "running"; else echo "stopped"; fi
    ;;
  ip)
    guard
    ip
    ;;
  install)
    guard
    win_iso=$(sed -n 's/^sata0:0.fileName = "\(.*\)"$/\1/p' "$vmx")
    [ -z "$win_iso" ] || [ -f "$win_iso" ] || die "Windows ISO missing at $win_iso; run scripts/vm-win/prepare.sh (docs/testing/windows-test-vm.md)"
    [ -f "$dir/iso/paddock-setup.iso" ] || die "setup disc missing; run scripts/vm-win/prepare.sh"
    has_snapshot "$baseline" && die "the VM already has $baseline; revert to it instead of reinstalling"
    running && die "the VM is running; stop it first"
    for dev in sata0:0 sata0:1; do "$lib/vmcli" "$vmx" ConfigParams SetEntry "$dev.present" TRUE >/dev/null; done
    load_ok
    echo "Installing Windows headless from the no-prompt ISO (no window, no key to press); the VM powers off when done."
    started=$SECONDS
    vmrun start nogui
    wait_off "$install_deadline" "installing Windows" || die "setup did not finish within ${install_deadline}s; see $(dirname "$vmx")/vmware.log"
    took=$(((SECONDS - started) / 60))
    # Setup takes far longer than this; an earlier stop is a crash or a boot failure, never a finished install.
    [ $took -ge "${PADDOCK_VM_MIN_INSTALL_MIN:-10}" ] || die "the VM stopped after $took min, too early for a finished setup; see $(dirname "$vmx")/vmware.log"
    echo "the VM powered off after $took min; next: scripts/vm-win.sh baseline (it checks that setup finished)"
    ;;
  baseline)
    guard
    running && die "the VM is running; baseline is taken from a powered-off VM"
    has_snapshot "$baseline" && die "$baseline already exists"
    load_ok
    # Check first, with the discs still attached: Windows Setup puts Windows Boot Manager first in the boot order, so
    # the disk boots; if setup had not finished, nothing is lost and install can be run again.
    vmrun start nogui
    wait_ssh
    ssh_to paddock-admin 'if (-not (Test-Path C:\paddock-setup\done.marker)) { exit 3 }' ||
      die "setup did not finish (no C:\\paddock-setup\\done.marker); read C:\\paddock-setup\\setup.log in the VM"
    (ssh_to paddock-admin 'shutdown /s /t 0') >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    wait_off 180 "shutting down" || vmrun stop hard
    for dev in sata0:0 sata0:1; do "$lib/vmcli" "$vmx" ConfigParams SetEntry "$dev.present" FALSE >/dev/null; done
    vmrun snapshot "$baseline"
    echo "snapshot $baseline taken; the install discs are detached and the VM is off"
    ;;
  -h | --help | help) usage ;;
  *) usage >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac

# One-time, as paddock-admin, for the buildtools-baseline snapshot (scripts/vm-win.sh toolchain-setup; ADR 0087 amendment of
# 2026-11-16): installs the Visual Studio 2022 Build Tools, LTSC 17.12, with the MSVC and Windows SDK pieces a Rust build links
# against (the repo's .cargo/config.toml links with rust-lld but "still links against the MSVC and Windows SDK libraries"). The
# bootstrapper is Microsoft's own, fetched on the host, checked against its pinned SHA-256 there AND here, and checked for a
# Microsoft Authenticode signature; the components come from Microsoft's CDN through that bootstrapper. No token, no account.
param(
  [Parameter(Mandatory)] [string] $Installer,
  [Parameter(Mandatory)] [string] $Sha256
)
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
# Runs detached from the SSH session that started it (vm-win.sh toolchain-setup polls): the installer starves the guest for minutes and
# an SSH session over a stalled guest is dropped by its keep-alive (seen 2026-11-16). It writes a log and, last, a done file with 0 or 1.
$log = 'C:\paddock-test\buildtools.log'
Remove-Item 'C:\paddock-test\buildtools.done' -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
Start-Transcript -Path $log -Force | Out-Null
try {
function Say($m) { Write-Output "buildtools-setup: $m" }
$got = (Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256 $Installer).Hash.ToLower()
if ($got -ne $Sha256.ToLower()) { throw "installer SHA-256 is $got, not the pinned $Sha256" }
$sig = Get-AuthenticodeSignature $Installer
if ($sig.Status -ne 'Valid' -or $sig.SignerCertificate.Subject -notmatch 'Microsoft Corporation') { throw "installer signature: $($sig.Status) $($sig.SignerCertificate.Subject)" }
Say "installer ok: sha256 $got, signed by $($sig.SignerCertificate.Subject)"
$free0 = (Get-PSDrive C).Free
$started = Get-Date
$args = @('--quiet', '--wait', '--norestart', '--nocache', '--noUpdateInstaller', '--installPath', 'C:\BuildTools',
  '--add', 'Microsoft.VisualStudio.Component.VC.Tools.x86.x64',
  '--add', 'Microsoft.VisualStudio.Component.VC.Tools.ARM64',
  '--add', 'Microsoft.VisualStudio.Component.Windows11SDK.22621')
$p = Start-Process -FilePath $Installer -ArgumentList $args -Wait -PassThru
Say "installer exit $($p.ExitCode) after $([int]((Get-Date) - $started).TotalSeconds) s"
if ($p.ExitCode -ne 0 -and $p.ExitCode -ne 3010) { throw "the installer failed (exit $($p.ExitCode)); its logs are in %TEMP%\dd_*" }
$vswhere = "${env:ProgramFiles(x86)}\Microsoft Visual Studio\Installer\vswhere.exe"
$info = & $vswhere -products '*' -latest -format json | ConvertFrom-Json
Say "installed: $($info.displayName) $($info.installationVersion) at $($info.installationPath)"
$links = Get-ChildItem -Recurse 'C:\BuildTools\VC\Tools\MSVC' -Filter link.exe | ForEach-Object { $_.FullName }
Say "link.exe: $($links -join '; ')"
if (-not ($links | Where-Object { $_ -match 'arm64' })) { throw 'no arm64 link.exe was installed' }
$sdk = Get-ChildItem 'C:\Program Files (x86)\Windows Kits\10\Lib' -Directory | Select-Object -ExpandProperty Name
Say "Windows SDK libs: $($sdk -join ', ')"
$used = [math]::Round(($free0 - (Get-PSDrive C).Free) / 1MB)
Say "disk used on C: about $used MB"
Say 'done'
Set-Content 'C:\paddock-test\buildtools.done' '0'
} catch {
  Write-Output "buildtools-setup: FAILED: $_"
  Set-Content 'C:\paddock-test\buildtools.done' '1'
} finally { Stop-Transcript | Out-Null }

# Sourced by vm-win.sh and prepare.sh: the one Windows test VM these scripts may ever act on (ADR 0040 §1; review P1-1,
# 2026-11-08). The user's own VMs (Fusion keeps them in the same app) must be impossible to target, whatever the environment.
#
# Allowed: the folder <dev disk>/vm-data/paddock-win11-test (after resolving links; derived from the repository's own git config
# with an empty environment, `./dev places --pinned`, so no variable can move it; docs/dev-setup.md), or, for the scripts' own tests only,
# "fake mode", which nothing in the environment can switch on by itself: the folder resolves under the per-user temp root
# (`getconf DARWIN_USER_TEMP_DIR`, /tmp where there is none; never $TMPDIR), carries the marker file `.paddock-fake-vm`
# the test created, is not under $HOME, its .vmx has one hard link, and FUSION_APP's vmrun resolves outside the installed Fusion, is a script and never names the app.
# Anything else is refused before vmrun, ssh, scp or any file is touched. FAKE_VM=1 is set only in fake mode.
WIN_VM_NAME=paddock-win11-test
# The repository's own ./dev, never PADDOCK_DEV: the program that names the target must not come from the environment either.
_win_vm_repo="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)"
# ./dev runs from the repository with the caller's environment minus what picks or places the binary or the checkout it is built from:
# every PADDOCK_* variable (PADDOCK_DEV, PADDOCK_DEV_HOME, PADDOCK_CI_MOUNT, PADDOCK_DEV_TARGET_DIR ...) and every GIT_* one (GIT_DIR,
# GIT_WORK_TREE). Three PADDOCK_* values only restrict the build and stay: PADDOCK_DEV_DOWNLOAD=0 (a release job never downloads, ADR
# 0022 amendment), PADDOCK_TOOLCHAIN_FAILED=1 and PADDOCK_DEV_FRESH=1; a caller cannot switch a download on; the read token PADDOCK_DEV_TOKEN stays too (it cannot choose the program). PATH and the toolchain's
# variables stay, because ./dev finds its compiler the way it does for the caller (CI's cargo is not under $HOME/.cargo/bin; a fixed
# PATH made it stop with "no Rust compiler runs here", run 8138). This keeps the environment from choosing the program; it is not a
# sandbox. The first run after the tool's inputs change builds paddock-dev once into the default cache.
_win_vm_dev() {
  local unset=() v
  while IFS= read -r v; do
    case "$v" in
      PADDOCK_DEV_DOWNLOAD) [ "${!v}" = 0 ] && continue ;;
      PADDOCK_TOOLCHAIN_FAILED) [ "${!v}" = 1 ] && continue ;;
      PADDOCK_DEV_FRESH) [ "${!v}" = 1 ] && continue ;;
      PADDOCK_DEV_TOKEN) continue ;; # the read token cannot choose the program; without it CI's downloads miss and the build is slow
    esac
    unset+=(-u "$v")
  done < <(compgen -e | grep -E '^(PADDOCK_|GIT_)')
  (cd "$_win_vm_repo" && env ${unset[@]+"${unset[@]}"} "$_win_vm_repo/dev" "$@")
}
# Empty when it cannot be derived: then only fake mode passes, and the real VM is refused with the reason (fail closed).
WIN_VM_DIR_UNKNOWN=""
if _win_vm_data="$(_win_vm_dev places --pinned --get vm-data --repo "$_win_vm_repo" 2>/dev/null)" && [ -n "$_win_vm_data" ]; then
  WIN_VM_DIR="$_win_vm_data/$WIN_VM_NAME"
else
  WIN_VM_DIR=""
  # `|| true`: the callers run under `set -euo pipefail`, and ./dev's refusal (exit 2, as in a checkout without paddock.worktreeRoot,
  # every CI checkout) must not end them: the reason is what this line is for.
  WIN_VM_DIR_UNKNOWN="$(_win_vm_dev places --pinned --get vm-data --repo "$_win_vm_repo" 2>&1 >/dev/null | tail -1 || true)"
fi

# A path with links resolved; a missing last part is resolved through its parent (prepare.sh creates the folder).
resolve_path() {
  realpath "$1" 2>/dev/null && return 0
  local parent
  parent=$(realpath "$(dirname "$1")" 2>/dev/null) || return 1
  printf '%s/%s\n' "$parent" "$(basename "$1")"
}

# The temp root the tests use; not taken from the caller's $TMPDIR.
temp_root() {
  local r
  r=$(getconf DARWIN_USER_TEMP_DIR 2>/dev/null) && [ -n "$r" ] || r=/tmp
  realpath "$r" 2>/dev/null || echo /nonexistent-temp-root
}

# check_target <vm folder> <fusion app>: exits with a message unless the folder is the test VM (or fake mode).
check_target() {
  local want="only drives ${WIN_VM_DIR:-the test VM, whose folder cannot be derived (${WIN_VM_DIR_UNKNOWN#::error::})} (or, in the scripts' own tests, a marked fake VM under the per-user temp root with a fake vmrun script)"
  local real vmx realvmx links tmp realhome vmrun realvmrun realfus
  FAKE_VM=0
  real=$(resolve_path "$1") || { echo "vm-win: refusing $1: it does not resolve; this tool $want" >&2; exit 1; }
  realhome=$(realpath "$HOME" 2>/dev/null) || realhome=$HOME
  case "$real/" in "$realhome"/*) echo "vm-win: refusing $1: it resolves to $real, under \$HOME (ER-14); this tool $want" >&2; exit 1 ;; esac
  vmx="$1/vm/$WIN_VM_NAME.vmwarevm/$WIN_VM_NAME.vmx"
  if [ -n "$WIN_VM_DIR" ] && [ "$real" = "$WIN_VM_DIR" ]; then
    if [ -e "$vmx" ] || [ -L "$vmx" ]; then
      realvmx=$(realpath "$vmx" 2>/dev/null) || { echo "vm-win: refusing $vmx: it does not resolve; this tool $want" >&2; exit 1; }
      [ "$realvmx" = "$WIN_VM_DIR/vm/$WIN_VM_NAME.vmwarevm/$WIN_VM_NAME.vmx" ] || { echo "vm-win: refusing $vmx: it links to $realvmx; this tool $want" >&2; exit 1; }
    fi
    return 0
  fi
  tmp=$(temp_root)
  case "$real/" in "$tmp"/*) ;; *) echo "vm-win: refusing $1 (resolves to $real): this tool $want" >&2; exit 1 ;; esac
  [ -f "$real/.paddock-fake-vm" ] || { echo "vm-win: refusing $1: no .paddock-fake-vm marker; this tool $want" >&2; exit 1; }
  vmrun="$2/Contents/Library/vmrun"
  realvmrun=$(realpath "$vmrun" 2>/dev/null) || { echo "vm-win: refusing fake mode: $vmrun does not resolve; this tool $want" >&2; exit 1; }
  realfus=$(realpath "/Applications/VMware Fusion.app" 2>/dev/null) || realfus="/Applications/VMware Fusion.app"
  case "$realvmrun" in "$realfus"/*) echo "vm-win: refusing fake mode: $vmrun resolves into the installed Fusion; this tool $want" >&2; exit 1 ;; esac
  case "$realvmrun/" in "$tmp"/*) ;; *) echo "vm-win: refusing fake mode: $vmrun is not under the temp root; this tool $want" >&2; exit 1 ;; esac
  [ "$(head -c 2 "$realvmrun" 2>/dev/null)" = "#!" ] || { echo "vm-win: refusing fake mode: $vmrun is not a script; this tool $want" >&2; exit 1; }
  # A wrapper around the installed Fusion is a script too: its text must never name the app.
  if grep -qF "/Applications/VMware Fusion.app" "$realvmrun" 2>/dev/null; then
    echo "vm-win: refusing fake mode: $vmrun names the installed Fusion (/Applications/VMware Fusion.app); this tool $want" >&2; exit 1
  fi
  if [ -e "$vmx" ] || [ -L "$vmx" ]; then
    realvmx=$(realpath "$vmx" 2>/dev/null) || { echo "vm-win: refusing $vmx: it does not resolve; this tool $want" >&2; exit 1; }
    case "$realvmx" in "$real"/*) ;; *) echo "vm-win: refusing $vmx: it links to $realvmx; this tool $want" >&2; exit 1 ;; esac
    # A hard link has no path to resolve: a second name for another file (the user's VM) shows only as a link count above 1.
    links=$(stat -f %l "$realvmx" 2>/dev/null) || { echo "vm-win: refusing $vmx: its link count cannot be read; this tool $want" >&2; exit 1; }
    [ "$links" = 1 ] || { echo "vm-win: refusing $vmx: it is a hard link (link count $links); this tool $want" >&2; exit 1; }
  fi
  FAKE_VM=1
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Runs cargo (or any command) for an app inside a native Linux container (OrbStack/Docker), so the Linux adapters build and
# test against a real /proc and /sys (plan X47; Dyno's linux-container.sh and Pitwall's linux-container-verify.sh as one).
# The repository is mounted read-only; the cargo registry and the build output live in named volumes, never in the
# repository. Every container is created with --rm and the label paddock.tools=<id>; only containers and volumes this script
# created (that label, those names) are ever removed (rule 7).
#
#   bash paddock/tools/linux-container.sh --id dyno [--root <repo>] [--packages dyno-platform] -- [command...]
#   bash paddock/tools/linux-container.sh --id paddock --image <ref> [--platform linux/amd64] -- command...   # a ready image, run as it is
#   bash paddock/tools/linux-container.sh --id paddock --ci-image [--platform linux/amd64] -- command...   # the CI image, native by default
#   bash paddock/tools/linux-container.sh --id paddock --ci-image --image-ready   # probe only: exit 0 the image is built, 3 it is not (never builds)
#   bash paddock/tools/linux-container.sh --id dyno --clean              # stop labelled containers, delete its volumes and local CI images
#
# With no command: `cargo test -p <packages> && cargo clippy -p <packages> --all-targets -- -D warnings`.
#
# --ci-image runs the repository's CI image (ci-image/VERSION) on the host's own architecture unless --platform says otherwise:
# linux/amd64 is the registry's paddock-ci:v<VERSION>; linux/arm64 (the default on an Apple Silicon Mac) is built here from
# ci-image/Dockerfile on ci-image/garage-arm64.Dockerfile, tagged by a hash of those files, labelled, and never pushed. amd64 on an
# arm64 host runs under emulation, where a failed exec is not reported to the parent; the script then prints a warning.
# The arm64 image has no Chrome for Testing and no draw.io (neither is published for Linux arm64): it runs the Rust gates and
# Node scripts, not the e2e suites against Chrome for Testing or the SVG drift check, which stay CI's (amd64). A new arm64 build
# removes this id's older local images (paddock-ci-local, paddock-garage-local; about 11 GB a pair); --clean removes them all.
# A linked worktree's git folders (its own and the common one) are mounted read-only at their own paths, so git works inside; the
# pre-push state folder (<common git dir>/paddock-pre-push) is a tmpfs there, so `dev check --pre-push` can write its logs without
# touching the host's. CARGO_TARGET_DIR (/target, a volume) and /tmp are the other writable places. git accepts the host user's
# repository through the image's /etc/gitconfig (`[safe] directory = *`): the CI image has it, as in CI, and the image this script
# builds from PADDOCK_LINUX_BASE_IMAGE gets it in its build; an --image of another kind needs its own. The script sets no GIT_*
# variable, so a command's own HOME and its .gitconfig work as they do in CI.
# Environment inside: CARGO_BUILD_JOBS (CI sets it too) and CARGO_TERM_COLOR=never (CI: always, for its log viewer; local output
# goes to files and greps, where colour codes would split the words), and CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/target (CI points cargo at its build
# folder through .cargo/ci.toml instead, which a read-only /work cannot take).
# Environment: DOCKER (default docker), PADDOCK_LINUX_BASE_IMAGE (rust:1-bookworm), PADDOCK_LINUX_CPUS (4), PADDOCK_LINUX_JOBS (2),
# PADDOCK_LINUX_HOST_ARCH (default `uname -m`; tests pretend with it), PADDOCK_LINUX_CI_REGISTRY (dev.decryptology.net/decryp7/paddock-ci),
# PADDOCK_LINUX_RUN_LABEL (an extra label, `key=value`, on the container: `dev check --pre-push` finds and stops its own container by it), PADDOCK_LINUX_MEMORY (12g; ER-14 wants every test container capped), PADDOCK_LINUX_USER (e.g. 1000:1000 to exercise the "other users' processes" paths; builds into the container's /tmp).
set -euo pipefail

id=""; root="$PWD"; packages=""; clean=0; ready_image=""; platform=""; ci_image=0; image_ready=0
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --id) id="${2:?--id needs a value}"; shift ;;
    --root) root="${2:?--root needs a value}"; shift ;;
    --packages) packages="${2:?--packages needs a value}"; shift ;;
    --image) ready_image="${2:?--image needs a value}"; shift ;;
    --platform) platform="${2:?--platform needs a value}"; shift ;;
    --ci-image) ci_image=1 ;;
    --image-ready) image_ready=1 ;;
    --clean) clean=1 ;;
    --) shift; break ;;
    *) echo "linux-container: unknown option $1 (a command goes after --)" >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
  shift
done
[ -n "$id" ] || { echo "linux-container: --id <app id> is needed" >&2; exit 2; }
[[ "$id" =~ ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$ ]] || { echo "linux-container: --id must be lower-case letters, digits and dashes" >&2; exit 2; }
docker="${DOCKER:-docker}"
command -v "$docker" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "linux-container: $docker (OrbStack or Docker) is needed" >&2; exit 1; }

label="paddock.tools=$id"

# Removes this id's local CI images (the arm64 builds of --ci-image) except the ones named; only images with this id's label.
remove_local_images() {
  local ref keep
  while IFS= read -r ref; do
    case "$ref" in paddock-ci-local:* | paddock-garage-local:*) ;; *) continue ;; esac
    for keep in "$@"; do [ "$ref" != "$keep" ] || continue 2; done
    "$docker" image rm "$ref" >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo "linux-container: removed the old local image $ref" >&2
  done < <("$docker" image ls --filter "label=$label" --format '{{.Repository}}:{{.Tag}}')
  return 0
}
base_image="${PADDOCK_LINUX_BASE_IMAGE:-rust:1-bookworm}"
image="$id-linux-dev:2"
cpus="${PADDOCK_LINUX_CPUS:-4}"
jobs="${PADDOCK_LINUX_JOBS:-2}"
memory="${PADDOCK_LINUX_MEMORY:-12g}"
registry_volume="$id-cargo-registry"
target_volume="$id-linux-target"

if [ "$clean" = 1 ]; then
  leftovers=$("$docker" ps -aq --filter "label=$label")
  # shellcheck disable=SC2086
  [ -z "$leftovers" ] || "$docker" rm -f $leftovers >/dev/null
  "$docker" volume rm -f "$registry_volume" "$target_volume" "$target_volume-arm64" >/dev/null
  remove_local_images
  echo "removed the volumes $registry_volume, $target_volume and $target_volume-arm64"
  exit 0
fi

if [ $# -eq 0 ] && [ -z "$packages" ] && [ "$image_ready" = 0 ]; then
  echo "linux-container: no command and no --packages: nothing to run" >&2
  exit 2
fi

[ "$image_ready" = 0 ] || [ "$ci_image" = 1 ] || { echo "linux-container: --image-ready needs --ci-image" >&2; exit 2; }
[ "$ci_image" = 0 ] || [ -z "$ready_image" ] || { echo "linux-container: --ci-image and --image exclude each other" >&2; exit 2; }

case "${PADDOCK_LINUX_HOST_ARCH:-$(uname -m)}" in
  arm64 | aarch64) host_platform=linux/arm64 ;;
  *) host_platform=linux/amd64 ;;
esac
if [ "$ci_image" = 1 ] && [ -z "$platform" ]; then
  platform=$host_platform
fi
if [ "$host_platform" = linux/arm64 ] && [ "$platform" = linux/amd64 ]; then
  echo "linux-container: warning: linux/amd64 runs under emulation on this arm64 host (Rosetta or qemu-user). A failed exec is not reported" >&2
  echo "  to the parent there, so missing-program tests fail (paddock-proc's, heavy's exit-127 test, paddock-dev's slots, input_hash and" >&2
  echo "  slotflow), and timing-bound tests run slow. Those results are not findings; CI's amd64 runners are native. Leave --platform out" >&2
  echo "  (with --ci-image) for the native linux/arm64 image." >&2
fi

if [ "$ci_image" = 1 ]; then
  version=$(tr -d '[:space:]' < "$root/ci-image/VERSION" 2>/dev/null) || version=""
  [ -n "$version" ] || { echo "::error::linux-container: cannot read $root/ci-image/VERSION. Next step: pass --root <a full checkout>" >&2; exit 1; }
  if [ "$platform" = linux/arm64 ]; then
    # Tagged by the content of every file the two builds read, so a change to any of them builds a new image.
    if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then hash=(sha256sum); else hash=(shasum -a 256); fi
    sum=$(cat "$root/ci-image/Dockerfile" "$root/ci-image/garage-arm64.Dockerfile" "$root/ci-image/fetch-verified.sh" "$root/ci-image/verify.sh" | "${hash[@]}" | cut -c1-12)
    image="paddock-ci-local:v$version-arm64-$sum"
    if [ "$image_ready" = 1 ]; then
      # A probe, never a build: the arm64 image is minutes and gigabytes, so `dev check --pre-push` asks first and leaves the build
      # to `dev check --warm-linux` (exit 3: not built).
      "$docker" image inspect "$image" >/dev/null 2>&1 && { echo "linux-container: $image is built" >&2; exit 0; }
      echo "linux-container: $image is not built (it is built by a --ci-image run, or by ./dev check --warm-linux)" >&2
      exit 3
    fi
    if ! "$docker" image inspect "$image" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      garage="paddock-garage-local:arm64-$sum"
      started=$SECONDS
      echo "linux-container: building $garage (ci-image/garage-arm64.Dockerfile; once per change to ci-image/) ..." >&2
      "$docker" build --platform linux/arm64 --label "$label" -f "$root/ci-image/garage-arm64.Dockerfile" -t "$garage" "$root/ci-image" >&2 \
        || { echo "::error::linux-container: building $garage failed (exit $?). Next step: read the build output above; the image is local only" >&2; exit 1; }
      echo "linux-container: built $garage in $((SECONDS - started)) s; building $image (ci-image/Dockerfile) ..." >&2
      "$docker" build --platform linux/arm64 --label "$label" --build-arg "GARAGE_IMAGE=$garage" -f "$root/ci-image/Dockerfile" -t "$image" "$root/ci-image" >&2 \
        || { echo "::error::linux-container: building $image failed (exit $?). Next step: read the build output above; verify.sh names what is missing" >&2; exit 1; }
      echo "linux-container: built $image in $((SECONDS - started)) s in all" >&2
      remove_local_images "$image" "$garage"
    fi
  else
    image="${PADDOCK_LINUX_CI_REGISTRY:-dev.decryptology.net/decryp7/paddock-ci}:v$version"
    [ "$image_ready" = 0 ] || { echo "linux-container: $image is pulled when it runs" >&2; exit 0; } # nothing is built for it
  fi
elif [ -n "$ready_image" ]; then
  image="$ready_image" # a ready image (for example the CI image) is run as it is: no layer of ours, no rustup
elif ! "$docker" image inspect "$image" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  printf 'FROM %s\nRUN rustup component add clippy rustfmt && git config --system --add safe.directory "*"\n' "$base_image" \
    | "$docker" build --label "$label" -t "$image" -
fi
"$docker" volume create --label "$label" "$registry_volume" >/dev/null
# arm64 builds keep their own target volume: one shared with amd64 runs would rebuild everything at every switch.
[ "$platform" != linux/arm64 ] || target_volume="$target_volume-arm64"
"$docker" volume create --label "$label" "$target_volume" >/dev/null

if [ $# -eq 0 ]; then
  set -- sh -c "cargo test -p $packages && cargo clippy -p $packages --all-targets -- -D warnings"
fi

# Not --privileged: the tests must pass as an ordinary user would run them.
user_args=()
if [ -n "${PADDOCK_LINUX_USER:-}" ]; then
  user_args=(--user "$PADDOCK_LINUX_USER" -e HOME=/tmp/home -e CARGO_HOME=/tmp/cargo-home -e CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/target)
fi

# A linked worktree's `.git` is a file naming its git folder outside the root: mount that folder and the common one read-only at
# their own paths (the file names them absolutely), or every git command inside fails with "not a git repository".
git_args=(); state=""
if [ -f "$root/.git" ]; then
  gitdir=$(sed -n 's/^gitdir: //p' "$root/.git" | head -1)
  case "$gitdir" in /*) ;; "") ;; *) gitdir="$root/$gitdir" ;; esac
  if [ -n "$gitdir" ] && [ -d "$gitdir" ]; then
    common=$gitdir
    if [ -f "$gitdir/commondir" ]; then
      common=$(head -1 "$gitdir/commondir")
      case "$common" in /*) ;; *) common="$gitdir/$common" ;; esac
    fi
    common=$(cd "$common" && pwd -P)
    gitdir=$(cd "$gitdir" && pwd -P)
    git_args+=(--mount "type=bind,source=$common,target=$common,readonly")
    case "$gitdir/" in "$common"/*) ;; *) git_args+=(--mount "type=bind,source=$gitdir,target=$gitdir,readonly") ;; esac
    state="$common/paddock-pre-push"
    state_in="$state"
  fi
elif [ -d "$root/.git" ]; then
  state="$root/.git/paddock-pre-push"
  state_in="/work/.git/paddock-pre-push"
fi
if [ -n "$state" ]; then
  # The mount point must exist in the read-only folder; it is the pre-push tool's own state folder, made empty if missing.
  mkdir -p "$state" 2>/dev/null && git_args+=(--mount "type=tmpfs,target=$state_in")
fi

exec "$docker" run --rm --label "$label" ${PADDOCK_LINUX_RUN_LABEL:+--label "$PADDOCK_LINUX_RUN_LABEL"} --cpus "$cpus" --memory "$memory" \
  ${platform:+--platform "$platform"} \
  --mount "type=bind,source=$root,target=/work,readonly" ${git_args[@]+"${git_args[@]}"} \
  --mount "type=volume,source=$registry_volume,target=/usr/local/cargo/registry" \
  --mount "type=volume,source=$target_volume,target=/target" \
  -e CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/target -e CARGO_BUILD_JOBS="$jobs" -e CARGO_TERM_COLOR=never \
  ${user_args[@]+"${user_args[@]}"} -w /work "$image" "$@"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Keeps a persistent CI build folder (host runners) within a size cap, so nothing piles up on the owner's machines
# (plan X47; Dyno's ci-prune.sh).
#
#   bash paddock/tools/prune-build-folders.sh <folder> <max-gigabytes>
#
# Over the cap the incremental-compilation caches go first (the bulk, and cheap to rebuild); still over, the folder is deleted.
# A missing folder is fine. Only <folder> is touched; symlinks are never followed. PADDOCK_PRUNE_UNIT=kb makes the cap
# kilobytes instead of gigabytes (tests).
set -euo pipefail
[ $# -eq 2 ] || { echo "usage: prune-build-folders.sh <folder> <max-gigabytes>" >&2; exit 2; }
dir="$1"
max="$2"
[[ "$max" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || { echo "prune: the cap must be a whole number, got '$max'" >&2; exit 2; }
[ -d "$dir" ] && [ ! -L "$dir" ] || exit 0

unit=1048576
[ "${PADDOCK_PRUNE_UNIT:-gb}" = kb ] && unit=1
# The larger of the allocated size and the length of the regular files (hard links once, the total rounded up to a kilobyte), both
# from one pass of the kit's GNU/BSD helper (`kit.sh portable file-sizes`), never from `du`. A file system that allocates late (ZFS,
# btrfs, a compressed volume) reports next to nothing allocated for data written a moment ago, which kept a full folder under the cap
# on a runner. Folders are not content: GNU `du --apparent-size` counts them as 0, BSD `du -A` rounds each one up, and `du -sk` counts
# ext4's 4 KiB per folder (a folder of empty folders was 20 KiB, CI run 8138). What cannot be read counts 0. `ci prune-folder`
# (tools/paddock-dev/src/ci_host/prune.rs, `sizes`) counts the same way on Unix; on Windows it counts each file's length as its
# allocated size and does not find hard links, so the two agree on Unix only.
# A pass stats every file (about 7 s for 15,306 files on a Mac, where `du -sk` took 0.1 s): the size is measured once, and again
# only after the incremental caches went (docs/benchmarks.md, "Prune size, one pass").
kit="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)/conformance/ci/kit.sh"
# The one guarded delete (conformance/ci/safe-rm.sh): the folder goes only strictly under its parent, as `ci prune-folder` does.
. "$(dirname "$kit")/safe-rm.sh"
size() {
  local sizes apparent used
  sizes=$(sh "$kit" portable file-sizes "$dir")
  apparent=${sizes% *}
  used=${sizes#* }
  [[ "$apparent" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || apparent=0
  [[ "$used" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || used=0
  apparent=$(( (apparent + 1023) / 1024 ))
  used=$(( (used + 1023) / 1024 ))
  echo $(( (apparent > used ? apparent : used) / unit ))
}

now=$(size)
if [ "$now" -ge "$max" ]; then
  echo "prune: $dir is $now (cap $max); removing incremental caches"
  # Each cache strictly under the folder, a refusal a warning, as `ci prune-folder` does (find -prune never enters a link).
  find "$dir" -type d -name incremental -prune 2>/dev/null | while IFS= read -r f; do
    SAFE_RM_ANNOTATION=warning safe_rm "$dir" "$f" || true
  done
  now=$(size)
  if [ "$now" -ge "$max" ]; then
    echo "prune: still $now; removing $dir"
    safe_rm "$(dirname "$dir")" "$dir"
  fi
fi
